title: Bills/Browns Week 2 Preseason Takeaways! | Always Gameday in Buffalo
text: Hey Bills Mafia, we know there's one thing on your mind every day, your team, the Buffalo Bills. So, Matt Bove and Sal Capaccio are here to bring you the latest news, notes, and opinions straight from the source, right here, right now, because it's always game day in Buffalo. >> [music] >> Welcome everyone to another episode of It's Always Game Day in Buffalo. Matt Bove here. I'll be joined by Sal Capaccio momentarily from somewhere on the 90 as he drives back from Cleveland. I am in my basement. I just got back from dinner actually at Mulberry in Lackawanna. We were celebrating my aunt and uncle's 50th wedding anniversary. So, happy anniversary to my Aunt Becky and Uncle Ed. Watched the game from the stations today. I was watching on TV. I know Sal was up in the press box, so we'll get his perspective when he joins us. This was just an absolutely dominant win for the Bills on both sides of the ball, a convincing win, and another day where they looked really, really good. Now, there are a lot of layers to talk about and a lot of things that happened in this game. We'll start with to me what I thought was the biggest takeaway was that Kyle Allen looked very competent and very trustworthy today. And that's a really good sign. Now, he was against backups. We knew it was going to be a lot of backups in this game after the joint practice, but Kyle Allen finished the day 10 of 12 for 128 yards and a touchdown. The touchdown came on a screen pass to Mecole Hardman, but there were some nice throws in there, a couple nice throws to Trent Sherfield, and then there was a beautiful throw in the final minute of the first half to Macklin, and we'll talk more about him, too, because that's definitely a story. But Kyle Allen looked good. Kyle Allen looked like the best quarterback that played in this game. The problem for the Browns is that the two guys competing for their starting quarterback job also played in this game. So, I thought Kyle Allen looked good. I thought Trent Sherfield looked good. I thought Macklin looked good. I think there's a lot of different ways we can go with this, but it was just a solid day for the Bills. And defensively, you know, they gave up a touchdown on the first Browns offensive possession of the day. The pass rush was not clicking probably as much as you would like it to, but there were still a lot of nice things on that side of the ball. I'm going right now to my observations from the game available at wkbw.com. Not a shameless plug, but also a shameless plug. I just want to go over some of the things that I wrote down because I do think that these are good ways to start. I think if you start with Kyle Allen, we talk about Kyle Allen, I think it's pretty clear at this point that he is going to be the backup quarterback. And after that, it's going to be Shane Buechele. Almost so much so that I could see a world where they don't play Kyle Allen in the preseason finale. That might be a getting ahead of ourselves a bit, but in two preseason games, he has four incomplete passes. That's in two games total. That's really, really effective. This is the same Kyle Allen who really struggled at Bills training camp. You know, I was talking about, "Hey, maybe they'll go out and they'll add a backup quarterback somewhere." I don't think we're at that point. I think it's pretty clearly that it's Josh Allen and Kyle Allen, and then Shane Buechele, who also, by the way, like looked fine, is going to be the practice squad guy. And I think they'll do the same thing they've done these last couple years, but instead of Mitch Trubisky, it's Kyle Allen, and you put Shane Buechele on the practice squad. So, that's kind of where I think things stand from a quarterback standpoint. All right, the next observation I had was the wide receiver battle intensifies. If you would have asked me at 12:55 p.m. today, right before kickoff, who I thought was going to make the team, I would have told you I think there's six guys. And I think there's five very obvious ones. That's DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, Keelan Colemna, Josh Palmer, and Skylar Bell. And the sixth guy I would have said would have been Mecole Hardman. I even said this during the rain delay, the lightning delay. There was a Q&A that I did on social media and somebody asked me about the wide receiver position and I was making the case for Hardman because one, he can be your punt returner and two, I thought that he had looked pretty good in the summer up to this point as just strictly a wide receiver. title: Browns vs. Bills Postgame Recap | Cleveland Browns
text: Nathan's Gear here at Huntington Bank Field where the Browns dropped preseason game number two 31 to 7 to the Buffalo Bills. But in the preseason, the score is not the story. The story here the quarterback Shador Sanders he started today played the first half and looked very good in the pocket for the Browns. He went nine of 11 for 74 yards and a touchdown. That touchdown being the Browns lone points where he found Luke Floria in the back of the end zone on a third down play. Beautiful ball from Sanders. Now, he did also throw an interception down near the red zone. That was a ball that was a little little behind the tight end, but off of his hands up into the air and was picked off by Damar Hamlin. Now, Deshaun Watson did play in the second half with the second stringers. Certainly not his best outing. A couple three and outs. Also threw an interception there. We'll find out that soon and we'll have coverage for you on clevelandbrowns.com and the Browns mobile app. But Shador Sanders certainly made the most of his opportunity I thought today here as the starter in the first half with the Cleveland Browns. JT had was out there, so we didn't want to get Blake hurt. and he's only been with us a week and we had a number of things where Browns hurt Browns and which to the naked eye you won't see but we had a number of things that way when you're putting in guys that haven't really been there and some of that's true and some of it you know isn't good enough from us as coaches once they go out there but I mean I don't know what to say I mean you know I wondered why Lane Kippen reached out a week ago now I know I mean I didn't know now I Oh, I didn't call him back now. I guess I should have. Appreciate you. Thank you. >> Shit's crazy, isn't it? way. Um, didn't get completions and execute. I think that's the biggest thing. >> What did you see on the uh the interception? >> I don't know. I I got hit so they I was asking guys on the sideline what happened. So, I I haven't even seen the play actually. So, I'm not even sure. >> And then that that last fourth down, did it get tipped? >> Yeah, it got tipped. >> Obviously, we had, you know, talked to you about before before the game like how you might have respond to whatever the crowd reaction was. Obviously, there were some booze out there. Just what was your kind of reaction in in the moment? >> Man, I didn't have no reaction. I think the biggest thing is um I don't I think you guys know too and I think the whole world know it's it has nothing to do about the performance. It's uh it's a little bit personal than that. So I think that's uh it's a disrespectful thing. Um so yeah, I mean I'm going to keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally on how I feel about that. Um and yeah, just move on. But don't you think, Deshawn that that winning and and playing better would eliminate some of that booing? >> Um, last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles and that same fan base, they cheered when I got hurt. So, is that is that have to do with what does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person get hurt, especially for your own city, and they cheer, >> does any of that make you regret coming here? >> No, I don't regret anything in my life. You know, I think the Lord put me through situations for a reason. So, I don't I don't regret anything at all. But, you know, I had uh different thoughts on how it was going to be, but you know, it is what it is. Um, you know, sometimes, you know, the tables turn and, uh, I'm patient enough because I'm a child of of God to, you know, wait for that that time to change. So, I'm not tripping on it. I'm not tripping on it. >> How about the the quarterback competition? Uh, do you feel like just your whole body of work, how how do you feel like you have presented yourself in terms of trying to win this thing? >> Uh, I don't know. I mean, I think that's just going to, you know, that's going to be Coach Mon's decision. So, you know, I just continue to just try to win a day each and every day. And, uh, like I mentioned before, the the organization, Jimmy D, uh, AB and and and Monk, Coach Monkin, is going to make that decision for for the organization. >> Do you feel like you said, do you feel like you've won the job? >> Uh, I don't I don't know. I don't even put myself I don't even get my hopes up, honestly. >> I mean, yeah. I think I've done a good job to be able to lead this team and and be a a starter in this league. But again, you know, uh I can't I I don't know how other people's feelings internally, you know, I haven't talked to coach Monk about that or anybody else. So again, you know, I'm just kind of open with you guys on how this thing going to play out. You know, I just take it one day at a time and you know, whenever that time comes, it it comes. Todd said he doesn't know when he's going to make it, but he wants to get somebody in place so they can start getting all the reps with the ones. And I know we talked about it before, but how valuable would that be to be the guy and then moving forward getting all those time? >> Yeah, I think it's very valuable for whoever that the the position goes to. I mean, you got to you got to build that trust. You got to build that rhythm. You got to got to know how you know guys operate. And not just for the quarterback, but I think for the whole team, for the whole offense, for the offensive line, being able to hear one cadence, one voice walking in a huddle, being able to know like how this person operate, how this person, you know, when things break down, you know, how how this quarterback is going to operate. So, um, yeah, I think it's going to be helpful for not just the quarterbacks, but I think just for the whole offense and the whole team. >> Good. I was going to ask real quick, Deshan, do you feel like um you know, if you are named the starter, do you do you feel like some of those feelings that you talked about before, you know, will dissipate and that you can develop a a really nice relationship with Bronze fans and that you can put that stuff in the rearview mirror or will you always carry some of that with you? What's your feeling on that? I don't know. I mean, only time I feel that energy is when I'm in the stadium or it's on social media. Like I mentioned before, when I'm in public, no one has mentioned anything. So, I think that's the only time those those people that's holding it in is is trying to, you know, disrupt the energy. You know what I'm saying? Because this is a social media players can't respond back. And in the stadium, you know, players can't respond back. So, I get it. I understand it, you know? So, it is what it is. >> Say two more. >> Quarterback job is tough enough. Can you defeat that negativity? >> I don't know. I don't know. You know, it's a mental battle every day. You know, I feel like I feel like I get more love on road games than I do home games. So, if it is my my spot and he does make me the name, maybe it's 17 away games and I don't know. I don't know. What about the fact that you guys do have your first two are on the road, your first six of nine are on the road. If you win the job, might that work in your favor? >> Again, I'm not sure. I don't know. You know, I thought being away for two years and working myself back from two Achilles injuries and putting the time in and, you know, being around the facility, being around the city, doing charity work in the city, you know, supporting the Cleveland Browns, you know, hanging out with fans whenever I do see them, you know, being honest, being, you know, the type of person I know I am and the character would would help. And I guess it it haven't. So that's why I say it's more it's it's personal. So, you know, it is what it is. People have their own opinions. I can to, you know, there's only so much you can do to change that. So, at the end of the day, you know, I just have to uh continue to just work on it and strive to be better mentally moving forward. >> Um, you talked a lot about >> the last one. >> You talked a lot about your uh mental health is something that you're really proud of despite all the backlash. What in dark moments like maybe today or in the past, what have you kind of leaned on to help you not fall into like a dark hole or something? >> Yeah. I mean, it's not so much of um like today wasn't really a dark hole. It was just kind of it wasn't something that I didn't expect. Um you know, I was just kind of neutral with it, but you know, I just lean on my mom uh my mom and ultimately I lean on my wife. That's my that's my biggest that's my biggest uh person of peace that I have. So, you know, you might catch me during the games, during certain situations, looking up to her in the suite and just making sure like as long as she there, I'll be good. I'm going to get through it. So, you know, she she's been there the whole time, you know, through my situations, um, the last five years. So, um, she's the best person in the world that I can, you know, lean on and, you know, that have that support. But, uh, yeah, I say my wife and my mom for sure. >> Appreciate it. Thank you. How comfortable did you feel out there today, especially on those couple of really early drives? >> Um, I would say I feel the same out every day. >> I mean, to start eight for eight and get that touchdown to Luke. Um, did you feel like you're able to find a rhythm pretty quickly? >> No, like I feel like that every day. I'm being honest. Like just because I went eight for eight, like I don't really keep track of that, you know, in my mind. It's just like I get to that place every day, you know, in practice. So, it just like translates. >> What were you most proud of being able to build on from the first preseason game into your performance in this first half? >> Um, I would say to get the first completion, I would say that was the biggest difference. Um and then it was just rolling. That's it. And then uh operating within the huddle and um play clock and everything. Just being on time. Um not letting the play clock get too too too low um to where it could be, you know, a little hazard. But I was uh just operating, just being in control. That's it. >> Uh Todd said how impressed he was by you, not just today, but you know, since the start of the offseason program. So can you look back on how you improved from this from then until now? >> How I improved? I improved every aspect of my life. I'll say I improve, you know, my at least my relationship with God, you know, to be able to come up here every day and uh talk to everybody regardless of opinions, you know, of how people what they say online and all this different type of stuff. Even those that sitting in front of me today, I still approach y'all and greet y'all with kindness because God gave me that. God gave me the the the wisdom to be able to to to not be emotionally phased by individuals and people because I'm here for a bigger purpose. >> I'm sorry, but I appreciate that. But but as a football player, how you improved? >> I mean, I say football is an aspect of my life, but you know, I'm godsent honestly. Um and and and that's me being a football player. >> Sure. On that um I think it was a fourth down play to Blake where you stood in the pocket. Um you know Todd mentioned you've been comfortable waiting for him to come open. What did you see on that play and then also the touchdown to Luke in the back of the end zone? I would say we had a um we had a play that um we could have gotten to another play and I like the look because it was two different front side it was zone backside it was man um and we talk about decisions and talk about okay if if you may not get in the perfect place so don't try to get too perfect but just go with your gut and go with how you feel and Um, I stuck with the play and I and I went through the progressions and I kind of like know how things are going to play out sometimes. So, I was able to to to find comfort in that because I know where my guys are going to be on the field and um yeah, like I like pressure situations. I like two-minute drill. I like I like all these different aspects that you would love your quarterback to be in. Like those are the that's what makes me as a person, you know? I grew up with pressure, you know? So, like I like those moments. That's when that's when I feel the best. Even even think about the two-minute drill even in practice. Like I remember we had the same two-minute last time we played the Bills, you know, and we wasn't really successful, but you know, they got me once then. I couldn't I couldn't let I couldn't let that same thing happen for the second time. So, it's like um they did great in their scheme and everything whenever we played them the first time last year and everything they did, but I I just feel like when it come to being able to move the ball and everything, like I'm the guy that likes to move the ball and like to put the ball in the air. >> Have you ever dealt with a a lightning delay like we had today? What did you do like while you were just kind of waiting to get back out there? >> I was just talking to God. I was just just talking to God, honestly. That's all I was doing, you know? because it could get frustrating um sometimes when you're ready and it's just not time yet, you know, but like God gave me the wisdom to be able to just like regardless whenever it's time to go out there and just be you. So I I I think about that in every aspect of life like if it's something that you want and you know it's not on your time and when you want things to happen, it's on on God's time when it's supposed to happen, you know. So that's what I live by and that's what I think of. So, I'm patient with everything in life because nothing's really on my time. >> Shador, you just talked to Deshawn and you know, he's upset about the fans and the booing >> and you just talked about being mentally tough >> in that situation when you're going against a guy that you're competing against was also your teammate. >> You know, knowing that you have that mental stability like to come alongside of him, how is that, you know, how did you do that with Deshawn today or did you do that? Yeah. I mean, well, in general, I don't appreciate that at all. Just regardless competition, we all human beings, and I think we all need to understand that, you know, in this room, too. We all humans. So, it's like um I don't really do things to humans I wouldn't really want done to me, you know, and I don't really like making people feel uncomfortable and in in different spaces. And that's why even sometime like daily things I do like I try to make sure everybody comfortable you know cuz a lot of things just even I am as a person sometimes can make people uncomfortable you know so I mean I'm obviously aware of that and just for all the fans and everything like we appreciate y'all and showing up and everything and however y'all feel about the situation about with the Sean about everything like still you know I think it's I think it's more about a bigger purpose of just respect you know, it's just a respect thing that I feel like um should be there because we all out there trying to do our best and trying to uh serve the the franchise the best way possible. We going out there to win games. We doing everything we can do. So, you know, I don't really appreciate that. I guess off off of that, how has your relationship with Deshawn kind of evolved from last year to this year and through this this you know the competition you guys have kind of been through camp? >> Uh I would say I would say over time is definitely like everybody's more comfortable. I would say I would say last year I was more trying to like figure out what I have to do and each and every day you know just to just to continue uh everything to be in the right mental space overall. I would say that's where I was at last year but this year I've been able to get comfortable be uh able to talk to all my teammates like a lot more and be able to be myself. So that's why when you say it's fourth and short and and and I feel comfortable out there, that's because I'm myself again. So, um, being able being able to have those relationships with everybody in the quarter quarterback room is extremely important. And that's even what the coaches said whenever they first got there, like this quarterback room and everybody got to be a unit, got to be a team regardless of who's going out there. Um, because you would want the same type of respect, you know, if you was going out there. So, you know, our motto is really treat everyone how you want to be treated honestly and um you know, not really playing to the games, the online games and all the different type of stuff. >> I know you've talked about like in throughout this training camp just controlling what you can control while you guys wait on a quarterback decision. So, I guess after starting today, if a decision comes in the next couple of days or whenever it comes, how how do you feel about the job you've done in in doing that? Um, I think I wake up and feel the same. Honestly, I don't think I think if you do things based off the situation you in, then it's like you're not really doing everything to your max. You're not giving your all. Like, I don't just want to be the starter now. I got to lock in a little more. Like, that's what I told everybody in pregame. And I don't know if they'll put the pregame, but I said to him because it had a little language in there. It had a little bit in there. So, I don't know. But I told him like, you know, we did everything, you know, so it's it's it's it's no point of being nervous. There's no point of feeling any different type of way. We put in the work. We do everything that we could do. And I I don't live with regrets. So anything that I've done, like that's just who I am. Like I don't really live with regrets or anything. So I don't know. I sleep better at night knowing I do everything I can. And however things falls. That makes sense. >> Thanks.

title: Cam Achord: 'We have a lot of guys that like to compete and push each other'
text: Are you a guy who thinks running backs make good kickoff returners because of the similarities in in you know following blockers and holes and things like that? >> Yes. Um I think it also has changed though with the new rules compared um to the old rules. I think in the old rules you definitely wanted a thicker guy to run through arm tackles um when you run your tracks and everything. I think now with the new rules you want more of a potential shifty guy a little bit. Um, but in general, I think running backs because they naturally run and press holes, and so they're able to press the blocks, stick their foot in the ground, um, make the right cuts and reads, and they're doing that, you know, every play on offense, so to speak. So, I think, you know, anybody that's got the ball in their hands a lot, you know, can translate to a good guy back there for sure. >> Can you have a rule of thumb as a coach for when guys are looking to field punts inside the five? Like, are there times when you say it's okay, times when it's not? because obviously Sky had that one last night, but returned it 16 yards. What's kind of your rule on that? >> Uh, changes week to week. Um, but you know, base rule would be like probably anything inside the seven yardd line, you're looking to let it go. Um, but you look at the opponent also like how good's the punter? If the punter is consistently like putting the ball at the eight yard line, not hitting touchbacks, then you may be a little bit more aggressive that week. Um, but like if you're just talking generically base week, we're probably at the seven, six yard line somewhere in there. like, hey, don't really return him. Um, unless we have a return call. Like, if we're being aggressive and dropping a guy out to get the gunner down the field, then we'll communicate to the guy like, hey, be more aggressive here, but smart at the same time. So, it's a I guess a very good balance and you have to really trust the guys that are back there to make the right decisions. Um, so we try to do that as much as we can and then everything at practice you implement it like a game and so like it's like play it like a game. So when we're at practice, we try to see what the decisions are making in the game. So when they go out on the field, they're making the same decisions. >> Cam, you didn't overreact when Trey was maybe not making as many as you'd like in practice. Do you have to make sure that you don't go the other way too and get a little too excited? And how do you explain what he's done these two games? >> Uh he's had two good games, but they're only two games. Um I I'm probably more in the kind of, you know, when you're doing good, try to find something, you know, than the other way. Um so, you know, he's had two good games, which is a credit to [snorts] him, but it's still a long way to go. Um obviously, we're going to get a chance this week to actually kick um in the stadium we play in. So, that's going to be really good, too. Um, but I think anytime you're looking at any whether it's positive or negative, you got to be even kill with it and take the good with the good and for what it's worth, but also the bad with the bad and know what you're working for. So, I don't try to get too high. Um, when it comes to that, especially when reflection in the moment, you're excited, all that type of stuff. Um, but when you're looking back on it, you're just trying to stay even, kill, and making making progress with it. >> With Trey, obviously, everyone's watching. Is it going through the uprights? But what have you seen from him with the kickoff rule at the NFL and the landing spot, different types of kicks, all that? >> Yeah. Um, obviously when he's at Florida, it was a lot of hit the ball as far as you can. Um, which obviously he did one of those last night as well. So, um, he has the ability to do that if we need it. Um, but he's trying to adjust and he's he's improving obviously with the placement, you know, we want to get the ball as close to the goal line as we can, you know, but also not at the 8 yardd line, 10 yardd line. So, just being able to adjust and go right, left, middle, wherever we're trying to place the ball based off our coverages cuz we'll kick it all over. Um, try not to just kick it one place. He's done a really good job with it so far. Um, gotten better from the spring and as he continues to work it, he's able to place the ball and then move it more outside the numbers, more in the alley because we'll do different things, you know, with our coverage that he's going to have to move the ball around. Um, so we don't have to just put it in one spot. But he's he's adjusting well because it's not just swing away anymore. You know, we got to try to cover and the closer you can put to the goal line, the better it's going to be. >> What worked on the 68 yard return of Pier Strong. How important was his timing and decision making on that play? >> Um it really is. We want our returners to catch catch the ball going forward. You know, Jeff K works with our returners. He does a really good job with those guys. You see him back there all the time just emphasizing catch mechanics. it starts there like actually catching the ball coming forward because just it just makes it that much difference for the blockers. Um and that's what it is on a kickoff return the fraction the run alley is very small and it's going to close real quick. Um and then just pressing the blocks you know the guys did a really good job blocking if you really look at it on the film like there's a lot of guys that are latched on to defenders. Um the one guy we didn't block was obviously free is the guy that makes the tackle. So you know those are going to happen. Uh but they do a really good job. you know, Jeff Cory that that work with me. I'm blessed to have two guys that are really good and they're they do a really good job for us out there focusing on that and communicating. But Pier did a really good job catching it going forward, pressing the blocks, and then getting vertical. >> Cam, a lot has been made about whether, [cough and clears throat] you know, run up and down the sideline or tackling pads in practice. You know, have you seen the guys, I guess, match that energy that you bring and do you see it kind of rub off on? >> Um, I I try to be the same person every day. um you know whether that's you know tackling a pad, headbutting a guy, whatever it may be, you know. Um and I and I think it's contagious a little bit. I really do. But I think the most important thing is to be yourself and be genuine like um I think guys and people see through that when you're not yourself or you try to put on, you know, a mirage and like, hey, you know, that's just not me. Um and I think the guys know that, you know, they they see the excitement. They also can see the other side at times, too. Um but it's a healthy balance. you know, I make sure the guys know when they do a good job. I also want to make sure they know, hey, we got to get this fixed at the same time. But, um, you know, I tell the guys to be themselves. So, but I'm a naturally high energy person, so I want them to go out there and cut it loose and have fun. And, you know, it's obviously you can have a little bit more fun when you're playing well. Um, it's not going to be as fun if you're not playing well. So, um, I think some guys, you know, like that type of stuff, and other guys are who they are, which is fine. Um, but I'm always going to be myself for sure. There was that one return Bo had in practice where you pretty much ran stride for stride with him. He's like the fastest guy on the team. What was your fastest 40 in your prime? >> Uh my prime it was four I think I think it was 451 to be honest with you. 452 um in college when I came out when I was there going in my senior year. Um I told Bo I was going to run about 22 on that one. You know obviously I didn't get 22 but um but it's good. You know, I I think for those guys, you know, they like to compete regardless it's me, another player. That that's the thing you love about the guys we have. We have a lot of guys that like to compete and push one another. Um it's a really good group of guys. So, and it's exciting to coach them. >> The challenge for you over this next week where you've had a core group on kickoff and kickoff return and so on and by the end of the roster cut, you're going to you might lose some guys and you kind of have to rebuild things. >> That's coaching. You know, I think best coaches are best teachers. Um, and we got to just continue to, and that's part of our job as coaches is I wish I could keep them all. You know, I'm sure Goody and Matt wish we could keep them all. We can't. Um, but when that happens and whoever it may be or may not be. Um, you've got to figure out and put the pieces together. You know, you're putting that puzzle together because kicking game, you may have a guy, no different than on game day, he plays four phases and he goes down. Well, it's not like, hey, this guy's four different guys that may have to go into the game and you may have to take another guy off a phase because he's starting on offense and defense to play because he may be the best next guy on punt, but he was starting on kickoff. Well, now I got to put a different guy on kickoff. So, for a special teams guy, it's the roster manipulation and just trying to find to be able to get the best 11 out there. Also understanding their offensive and defensive load. So, you know, I don't really try to look into who's going to make it or not make it till it's done. Um, like I try to rep everybody at practice, give everybody the opportunities and then when it's said and done and you know we make those decision then you figure out and try to put the place pieces of the puzzle together. >> Who are some guys that have impressed you through the spring and through camp at the gunner position as >> I think we're working 18 guys out there right now and I and I'm [clears throat] not I'm not lying. Um, obviously [snorts] Bo's been been good for us out there, but there's been multiple guys and um, and I think that's the biggest thing. You see a lot of guys rolling out there in the games. Um, you see him at practice. It's, you know, it's not been one guy. You have a guy has a good day, bad day. I think it's just the amount of guys and that's what the competition is so good, right? You got 18 guys out there working and it's like, which guy's gonna get the job. So, um, I really think this week's going to be a battle, too. You know, it'd be good to go against Arizona in the game, practice, you know, and practice ourselves. So, um I I can't just point out one guy to be honest with you. I think all those guys like really flashed, which is really good cuz now it makes people makes good decisions hard, you know? I just say who do we got? So, stay there. >> Do you call them gunners by the way? >> I do. I do. I think the biggest terminology is probably I think some people call them flyers. Uh I call them gunners. Um the guys on the punt team I call slots, not wings on the interior where you see kind of like Chris Brooks and that. Um, but once you start talking terminology, I mean, you can call it peanut butter and jelly and whatever. It doesn't matter. The player's going to call it whatever they they know. So, it doesn't matter to me. >> You say jammers on the other side. >> Vice. I just call them vice. >> Vice corners and safeties. Um, and that kind of just goes with our terminology of how we put guys in spots and for the calls, you know, rather rather than just call it jammers. >> What have you thought I should say I mentioned with Adamitis? What have you thought of the job? has kind of come in and done here, you know, kind of getting familiar with that field goal operation unit, but then also kind of what he's been able to settle. >> Yeah, he's done a good job. Um, you know, I think Kyle's done a really good job coming in, you know, um, filling in. Um, he's done a really good job obviously, you know, the snapping, the protecting, stuff like that. So, I think he's done everything we've asked for him, you know, and we'll see how it kind of goes and all that kind of stuff. Um, but, you know, obviously he's done really a good job for us, you know, and he's he's, you know, not only for us, everybody else, he's put his best foot forward for sure. Going back to the Oh, go ahead, Jason. Sorry, Bill. Um, going back to the 18 gunners, like, you know, between your time as a coordinator and as assistant, you've been you've had a lot of special teams units. Do you feel like you have more options than you have maybe had there's some years where maybe you're you got guys that are going out there, but they might not know what, you know, do you feel better about what your options are no matter what goody decides? >> I think so. Yes. Because you're rep working so many guys. Um, and I think sometimes when you come to a new place, one thing for myself, whether it was, you know, New England, New York, or college, wherever it may be, is like understanding you, you're in a new place, so everyone's even like no one to me when I walked in was like, "Hey, this guy's a starter." Um, it's like I want to see all every single guy and evaluate every guy for what they've doing now, not for what they've done. Um, so working all those guys is really helping me to say, "Hey, this guy's really showed up here lately." um you know and I think that's the biggest thing is you're working so many guys but it's giving you a good view of all those guys and you know you're also putting them on the other side so you're working against each other um but I think it's a good group overall for sure >> and you can also see like Neman's done it forever uh you know you've got a bunch of Bo etc like uh Christian's done it forever does does that experience come through too though when you're watching them you've you know the guys that have done it for a long Yeah, I mean, I think anytime you got a veteran, um, he's going to know how to certain situations and how to attack a guy. Um, again, veterans are always a comfort factor for coaches, too, because they've been out there, they've been in the heat of battle. Um, but I also think you got to get young guys ready to play, and you got to teach them, and there may be some growing pains with younger guys that in the eventually, you know, hey, this guy may make it or that type of thing. Um, but [snorts] I I think overall the veterans, you're like, oh, he's done it. he naturally does it and feels it, but then that's great teaching stuff and and our vets do a great job of coaching the younger guys. We don't have any selfish players or anything. So, that's really unique um in that aspect, too. >> When it comes to roster cut downs, I don't know if tough is the right word to use here, but are they tough conversations with like Goody, Matt, and Jonathan as you guys try to figure out how each of your >> I wouldn't say they're tough. I at all. Um to me, everyone wants to win. That's that's what's great about this thing is we all want to win. We always want the best players and I think you give your input and then they make the decision what they think is best for the team. Um I mean that's what Bill taught me that all the time. title: Coordinator Press Conferences
text: Hey, hey, hey. Hey, hey, hey. Hey. hey, hey. Whatever. Heat. Hey, Heat. Hey hey Um but no, Um if anybody's got any questions, we can open it up or anything like that. Obviously, um two games in and then moving on to this next one here against Arizona. So, >> are you a guy who thinks running backs make good kickoff returners because of the similarities in in you know following blockers and holes and things like that? >> Yes. Um I think it also has changed though with the new rules compared to um to the old rules. I think in the old rules, you definitely wanted a thicker guy to run through arm tackles um when you run your tracks and everything. I think now with the new rules, you want more of a potential shifty guy a little bit. Um but in general, I think running backs because they naturally run and press holes and so they're able to press their blocks, stick their foot in the ground, um make the right cuts and reads, and they're doing that, you know, every play on offense, so to speak. So, I think, you know, anybody that's got the ball in their hands a lot, you know, can translate to a good guy back there for sure. >> Can you have a rule of thumb as a coach for when guys are looking to field punts inside the five? Like, are there times when you say it's okay, times when it's not? Cuz obviously Sky had that one last night, but returned it 16 yards. What's kind of your rule on that? >> Uh, changes week to week. Um, but you know, base rule would be like probably anything inside the seven yardd line, you're looking to let it go. Um, but you look at the opponent also, like how good's the punter? If the punter is consistently like putting the ball at the eight yard line, not hitting touchbacks, then you may be a little bit more aggressive that week. Um, but like if you're just talking generically base week, we're probably at the seven, six yard line somewhere in there, like, hey, don't really return them. Um, unless we have a return call, like if we're being aggressive and dropping a guy out to get the gunner down the field, then we'll communicate to the guy like, "Hey, be more aggressive here, but smart at the same time." So, it's a I guess a very good balance and you have to really trust the guys that are back there to make the right decisions. Um, so we try to do that as much as we can and then everything at practice you implement it like a game and so like it's like play it like a game. So when we're at practice we try to see what the decisions are making in the game so when they go out on the field they're making the same decisions. >> Cam, you didn't overreact when Trey was maybe not making as many as you'd like in practice. Do you have to make sure that you don't go the other way too and get a little too excited? And how do you explain what he's done these two games? >> Uh he's had two good games, but they're only two games. Um I I'm probably more in the kind of, you know, when you're doing good, try to find something, you know, than the other way. Um so, you know, he's had two good games, which is a credit to him, but it's still a long way to go. Um obviously, we're going to get a chance this week to actually kick um in the stadium we play in, so that's going to be really good, too. Um, but I think anytime you're looking at any whether it's positive or negative, you got to be even kill with it and take the good with the good and for what it's worth, but also the bad with the bad and know what you're working for. So, I don't try to get too high. Um, when it comes to that, especially when reflection in the moment, you're excited, all that type of stuff. Um, but when you're looking back on it, you're just trying to stay even, kill, and making making progress with it. with Trey. Obviously, everyone's watching. Is it going through the uprights, but what have you seen from him with the kickoff rule at the NFL and the landing spot, different types of kicks, all that? >> Yeah. Um, obviously when he's at Florida, it was a lot of hit the ball as far as you can. Um, which obviously he did one of those last night as well. So, um, he has the ability to do that if we need it. Um, but he's trying to adjust and he's he's improving obviously with the placement, you know, we want to get the ball as close to the goal line as we can, you know, but also not at the 8 yardd line, 10 yardd line. So, just being able to adjust and go right, left, middle, wherever we're trying to place the ball based off our coverages because we'll kick it all over. Um, try not to just kick it one place. He's done a really good job with it so far. um gotten better from in the spring and as he continues to work it, he's able to place the ball and then move it more outside the numbers, more in the alley cuz we'll do different things, you know, with our coverage that he's going to have to move the ball around. Um so we don't have to just put it in one spot. But he's he's adjusting well because it's not just swing away anymore, you know, we got to try to cover and the closer you can put the goal line, the better it's going to be. >> What worked on the 68 yard return of Pier Strong? How important was his like timing and decision making on that play? >> Um, it really is. We want our returners to catch catch the ball going forward. You know, Jeff Coons works with our returners. He does a really good job with those guys. You see him back there all the time just emphasizing catch mechanics. It starts there like actually catching the ball coming forward because just it just makes it that much difference for the blockers. Um, and that's what it is on a kickoff return. The fraction the run alley is very small and it's going to close real quick. Um, and then just pressing the blocks. you know, the guys did a really good job blocking. If you really look at it on the film, like there's a a lot of guys that are latched on to defenders. Um, the one guy we didn't block was obviously free is the guy that makes the tackle. So, you know, those are going to happen. Uh, but they do a really good job. You know, Jeff Cory that that work with me. I'm blessed to have two guys that are really good and they're they do a really good job for us out there focusing on that and communicating. But Pier did a really good job catching it going forward, pressing the blocks and then getting vertical. Cam, a lot has been made about energy, [cough and clears throat] whether, you know, run up and down the sideline or tackling pads in practice. You know, have you seen the guys, I guess, match that energy that you bring, and do you see it kind of rub off on? >> Um, I I try to be the same person every day. Um, you know, whether that's, you know, tackling a pad, headbutting a guy, whatever it may be, you know. Um, and I and I think it's contagious a little bit. I really do. But I think the most important thing is to be yourself and be genuine. like um I think guys and people see through that when you're not yourself or you try to put on, you know, a mirage and like, hey, you know, that's just not me. Um and I think the guys know that, you know, they they see the excitement. They also can see the other side at times, too. Um but it's a healthy balance. You know, I make sure the guys know when they do a good job. Also want to make sure they know, hey, we got to get this fixed at the same time. But, um you know, I tell the guys to be themselves. So, but I'm a naturally high energy person, so I want them to go out there and cut it loose and have fun and, you know, obviously you could have a little bit more fun when you're playing well. Um, it's not going to be as fun if you're not playing well. So, um, I think some guys, you know, like that type of stuff and other guys are who they are, which is fine. Um, but I'm always going to be myself >> There was that one return Bo had in practice where you pretty much ran stride for stride with them. >> He's like the fastest guy on the team. What was your fastest 40 in your prime? Uh my prime it was uh four I think I think it was 451 to be honest with you. 452 um in college when I came out when I was there going in my senior year. Um I told Bo I was going to run about 22 on that one. You know obviously I didn't get 22 but um but it's good. You know I I think for those guys you know they like to compete regardless it's me another player. That that's the thing you love about the guys we have. We have a lot of guys that like to compete and push one another. Um it's a really good group of guys. though and it's exciting to coach him. >> What's the challenge for you over this next week where you've had a core group on kickoff and kickoff return and so on and by the end of the roster cut you're going to you might lose some guys and you kind of have to rebuild things. >> That's coaching. You know, I think best coaches are best teachers. Um and we got to just continue to and that's part of our job as coaches is I wish I could keep them all. You know, I'm sure Goody and Matt wish we could keep them all. We can't. Um, but when that happens and whoever it may be or may not be, um, you've got to figure out and put the pieces together. You know, you're putting that puzzle together cuz kicking game, you may have a guy, no different than on game day, he plays four phases and he goes down. Well, it's not like, hey, this guy, it's four different guys that may have to go into the game and you may have to take another guy off a phase because he's starting on offense and defense to play because he may be the best next guy on punt, but he was starting on kickoff. Well, now I got to put a different guy on kickoff. So for a special teams guy, it's the roster manipulation and just trying to find to be able to get the best 11 out there. Also understanding their offensive and defensive load. So you know, I don't really try to look into who's going to make it or not make it till it's done. Um like I try to rep everybody at practice, give everybody the opportunities and then when it's said and done and you know we make those decision then you figure out and try to put the p pieces of the puzzle together. Who are some guys that have impressed you through the spring and through camp at the gunner position? >> I think we're working 18 guys out there right now and I and I'm not I'm not lying. Um obviously Bo's been been good for us out there, but there's been multiple guys and um and I think that's the biggest thing. You see a lot of guys rolling out there in the games. Um you see him at practice. It's you know it's not been one guy. You have a guy has a good day, a bad day. I think it's just the amount of guys and that's why the competition is so good, right? You got 18 guys out there working and it's like which guy's going to get the job. So, um I really think this week's going to be a battle too. You know, it'd be good to go against Arizona in the game practice, you know, and practice ourselves. So, I I can't just point out one guy to be honest with you. I think all those guys like really flashed, which is really good because now it makes people makes good decisions hard, you know? I just say who do we got? So, stay there. Do do you call them gunners, by the way? >> I do. I do. I think the biggest terminology is probably I think some people call them flyers. I call them gunners. Um the guys on the punt team I call slots, not wings on the interior where you see kind of like Chris Brooks and that. Um but vice I just call them vice >> vice corners and safeties. Um and that kind of just goes with our terminology of how we put guys in spots and for the calls, you know, rather than just call it jammers. >> What do you thought I should say? I mentioned count with Adamitis. What have you thought of the job? He's kind of come in and done here, you know, kind of getting familiar with that field goal operation unit, but then also kind of what he's been able to settle on. >> Yeah, he's done a good job. Um, you know, I think Kyle's done a really good job coming in, you know, um, filling in. Um, he's done a really good job obviously, you know, the snapping, the protecting, stuff like that. So, I think he's done everything we've asked for him, you know, and we'll see how it kind of goes and all that kind of stuff. Um, but you know, obviously he's done really a good job for us, you know, and he's he's, you know, not only for us, everybody else, he's put his best foot forward for sure. >> Going back to that >> Oh, go ahead, Jason. >> Sorry, Bill. Um, going back to the 18 gunners, like, you know, between your time as a coordinator and as assistant, you've been you've had a lot of special teams units. Do you feel like you have more options than you have maybe had there's some years where maybe you're you got guys that are going out there but they might not know what the you know do you feel better about what your options are no matter what goody decides? >> I think so. Yes. Because you're rep working so many guys. Um, and I think sometimes when you come to a new place, one thing for myself, whether it was, you know, New England, New York, or college, where it may be, is like understanding you, you're in a new place, so everyone's even. Like no one to me when I walked in was like, "Hey, this guy's a starter." Um, it's like I want to see all every single guy and evaluate every guy for what they've doing now, not for what they've done. Um, but [snorts] I I think overall the veterans, you're like, oh, he's done it. he naturally does it and feels it, but then that's great teaching stuff and and our vets do a great job of coaching the younger guys. We don't have any selfish players or anything. So, that's really unique um in that aspect too. >> When it comes to roster cut downs, I don't know if tough is the right word to use here, but are they tough conversations with like Goody, Matt, and Jonathan as you guys try to figure out how each of your units? >> I wouldn't say they're tough I at all. We always want the best players and I think you give your input and then they make the decision what they think is best for the team. Um I mean that's what Bill taught me that all the time. Hey Cam, going back to Trey real quick. Have you have you had kickers that maybe are better in game situations than they are in practice? And um just watching him score that touchdown was awesome. Uh and that was one thing I'll never forget about that game. It was great. >> I know there's still a week left, but throughout this year to where we are now, how have you seen Jordan Morgan uh just progress back? >> Yeah, he's done a nice job. uh he's kind of just quietly gone in there and and anchored down the left side. Um so he's been good. Um yeah, there there's not a whole lot to talk about because he's just gone in there and done his job and and stepped up. So I'm I'm very happy with him right now for sure. >> When guys like John Williams were done and Jennings got in last night, were they going against Denver's ones or twos? >> Yeah. >> So I was thinking that's a great tape you've got to watch for those guys, right? Yeah, that was a big deal to get those guys in. Um, and just see them play against Nick Bonito and Zack Allen and all those really good players that they have. So, um, yeah, it was it was a really good evaluation. I thought those guys did a nice job. >> So, you know, where is John Williams at after, you know, didn't play last year or saw a lot of rust and stuff kick off. Is he did he disaster struck? Could he could he help you out or is he still >> No. Yeah, I think so. That's that was our big question kind of going into the preseason is where's this guy at? what do we think he can be? Um, and he's been a big surprise this preseason um of just how he's been able to step up, especially uh at the tackle position. I think he's done a really nice job. Still got a lot of lot to work on, but um he's he's done a good job. >> You know, Zack Allen obviously beats Jacob on the touchdown pass. >> Um he's beaten a lot of really good guards. He's not the first one, but where do you think, you know, you like his play style, but where do you think he and some of these other guys that we don't know how it's going to play out between now and Minnesota, they may have to play on the opener. Where do you think those guys are in their being ready for that kind of football? >> I think those guys, you know, again, we still have some time, but I think the more we just get them out there, the more they can learn. Like, uh, for example, on that one play, Monk just had bad fundamentals. he got his weight overextended on the outside and Zach obviously jumped inside and beat them. So that's a huge learning thing for him as at guard. Like you go against really good players, you have to play with great fundamentals. Uh otherwise you'll get exposed. So uh that's just a learning thing that you got to go through sometimes. >> But no, like with those guys, I love how their their play style, they're all young players. Uh they're going to make some mistakes, but they all play the right way. I don't know what your expectations were from Accord coming in, you know, to this offseason. What have you thought just how he's kind of handled that spot also being able to have the series that he's had? >> Yeah. Like talking kind of in the same vein as John Williams, like I really had no expectations and it was like, all right, let's see what this guy can do. And uh it's a testament to him and how he's worked and how coach Getsy and how coach McCartney have gotten him ready uh for every game cuz he goes out there and just manages the game and does a really nice job and it's been really impressive uh to watch him go out there and operate. >> That play style element that you brought up, is that something that's like harped on throughout the training camp or is that who those guys are? >> Yeah. No, I mean that's something we talk about a lot uh for sure as who we want to be as an offense and as a team. >> Steno, did that did that play that Golden made against Certan I mean you've been talking about how different he is and but like does that kind of solidify hey this is the kind of thing I'm talking about? >> Yeah. No, and MG's been he's been on fire the last few weeks as far as just like how he's burning routes with the violence he's had. um great hands, all that stuff. So, it's been cool to watch him again go out there against probably the best corner in the NFL um and and do what he did. Yeah, it's very encouraging. Sento, whether the the number is 9, 10, 11 offensive linemen, however you guys evaluate and decide that, what do you look for over this next week ahead of cut week or the cut date to say, "Okay, this guy's solidified his spot or this guy's played into or out of his spot." >> I think the biggest thing, obviously, we have to evaluate where um, you know, Zack and Aaron Banks are at. Um, that's going to probably play into it a little bit as far as how many we keep. Um, but then again, how do they handle themselves in this joint practice against the starters of the Cardinals, you know, and and what they show us there? I think that's going to be the biggest thing. And then obviously go out whatever guys get out there in the games, they got to go out there and compete and play well. So, all of it's just a big evaluation of the just kind of the the total parts of everything that we do for the preseason. So, um, I can't really name one specific thing that I'm looking for other than just making sure they're improving. >> You mentioned Zach and Aaron. Is there a any realistic possibility they're not ready for week one? >> I mean, yeah, probably, but I I don't anticipate that happening. Um, they're all trending forward to being ready to go. Banks did get, you know, the teamwork last. I think, you know, you might have been here before the Chad Clifton big Lamborghini uh program for him not practicing, but how do how do you go about if that's what Banks needs to be ready for game day? How do you guys go about making sure that he gets the work he needs without creating more issues? >> Yeah, I mean, at some point, we're going to need him to go out there and and put it all together for a string of time. Otherwise, you won't know if you can rely them as the season goes. So, I think that's going to be a big thing for him over these next two weeks is just getting out there on a regular basis, getting through practices, um, and, you know, performing at a high level. >> You guys, >> good. All right. Thanks, guys. See you.

title: Wesley Bailey, Alex Cook, CJ Daniels & Ty Simpson Recap Saturday's Preseason Win Over The Saints
text: No, definitely is a blessing. You know, I've been doing this since uh 2021. That's when I got my first sack, so to be able to do it on the next stage is definitely a blessing. So, I think they just allow me to play free and just keep balling and having great teammates to be there as well. It's a blessing, for sure. >> What makes it a blessing? >> Same thing we just talked about, you know? Just having great people in that building, man. You're you're showcasing that you have a nose for it. Can you just talk to me about just the speed of the game and are things starting to slow down for you? >> I guess. I'm not sure what to say. I'm not sure how to answer that. Uh It's football, you know? We've been doing it for since we've been six or seven, eight years old, so just continue to play the game I love. >> All right. Thanks, Ashton. >> Thanks, appreciate it. Appreciate it. Appreciate y'all. Have a blessed day. >> Thank you. >> What did it mean not just to get a an interception in a key situation, but then you got 100 yards in front of you? >> Oh, yeah. It's definitely a blessing. I mean, you know, I coming from the UFL, I I mean, I dreamed of being back in this back in the NFL and you know, I my last game in the UFL, I I I was grateful to get a pick-six and I just I was dreaming like, "Man, if I could just get one more pick-six back in the NFL, that would make my whole my whole life." Were you at all thinking that coming in and or afterwards? How do How do you process that? Coming from the UFL, it doesn't matter. You got to just take it just day by day and every day you're just fighting for a spot and you know, you just pray that you that you make plays like this to help, you know, help your chances in the end and yeah, you just got to keep on stacking those days. >> Did you What did you see on the play and and did you expect to have as much space in front of you as you did when you took off? >> so we're in a you know, typical cover four. Um I was just I was feeling the I felt the back go out, felt the seven route by the tight end. I knew that spot route was going to come sit right at the end zone and I was just waiting for the QB to throw and I kind of held my inside levers and once I see his eyes progress to the spot route, I just went ahead and jumped it you know, thankfully I was able to catch it and stride and take it to the take it to the house. >> Speak to the necess- the mental fortitude mental fortitude necessary to make it back to the NFL. >> Yeah, I mean that that's a good question cuz when I was when I was in the UFL, I I tried to be as present as I as I was as I as I could be and you know, you always want to go back to the NFL. I appreciate you. I appreciate you. >> So uh CJ what's your thoughts on your performance tonight 66 yards? >> Uh I had a pretty decent game for the most part. He's been pretty confident. >> Um you know he's a guy that's been in the system. Um he's a guy that you know knows what's going on. He's a guy that can alert to other people just to get them in places where they need to be. Um he's a great leader. He's a guy that's very mobile as you've seen today. You know being with that second group and being the quarterback of that group and you know him just trusting me to make those plays so >> What are some things that you can come and learn from Puka and Davante that you can take out there to make you be successful on the field? >> Um everything. I'm a listener and you know they've been doing it at a high clip for you know a while now so you know, just being at practice and you know, just watching them the way they move and just trying to mimic everything they do. And just asking questions each and every day, so um really just any type of detail situation, you know, I'm trying to get any type of knowledge I can gain from them for sure. >> What do you think the strongest part of your game was today? >> Uh just making plays on the ball came to me. Um I think that's the main part. Just earning the trust from, you know, the quarterback. >> You've been here with Ty since the draft. Where do you feel like he's uh maybe grown or or got more comfortable since you guys first got here? >> Yeah, definitely. Like I said, each and every day. Um you know, just coming in ready to work, being open-minded. Um you know, he's gotten better and as you've seen from last game and this game, just just him taking strides each and every day. Just being behind uh you know, Matthew, um having having a great room and you know, being a learner as well. So, he he's definitely taking strides. >> What do you think you learned from the first game that you were able to apply in this one? just being patient and let the game come to me, you know what I'm saying? You know, not being in a rush. Just just just being in the flow of the game. >> Mhm. What do you think was uh like what went so well in the operation of the two-minute drill at the end of that second half, both whether it be with you and then Stetson as well? just being ready for it, you know what I'm saying? text: And for mistakes and things obviously inevitably are going to go wrong even in the regular season. For it to feel like a game but when you step in the stadium and be in in you're in that environment, you know, it's first and 10 and then you get a chance to see the success of a play and then it's second and three and react to the situation. So um yeah, I think um obviously getting here and getting the offense under starting to understand the offense as much as I've had it will continue to grow with the reps and getting out there but to be able to go out score points, execute, um and improve I thought was really good today. >> Can you you might have talked about it before I walked up. Just walk us through that that long run. >> Yeah, oh. Yeah, so I was as I told them we're reading the nickel if he blitzes we're going to throw it. He stayed so then my read's just on the end and he gave me a pull key I was able to get in the space. I thought the entire offense did a great job of like executing the play really to um keep the defense on one side of the field and then I was able to score and get some momentum on our side and from there we're able to take that and run with it. Yeah. Oh, yeah, for sure. For sure. I think just because like obviously you're reading it and you know, like sometimes like you're on the back they can be on the backside of the play, right? They're thinking the ball's going to the running back. So it can be per se a play off with those guys. I think it's it's it's a testament to them and how locked in they are to the playbook to go out and still be blocking on the backside to allow me to be able to get in the space and make a play. So it's a team game and like all the big plays they revolve around all 11 of us on offense and we got to be on the same page and that's a perfect example of it right there. >> Did when you come to the sidelines after you know, sack fumble and then the interception, does Drew have to talk to you? Do you talk about that or do you just go over it with uh >> I go over with Brew. Like my personality, like I'm pretty even killed and so no matter what happens like could be a great play like the run or the second play of the game where is you know, a fumble turnover. My my mentality, my personality is to be the same no matter what. You know, we're the quarterback and I think like a lot of guys look to us in our position, right? Because the ball runs through us on offense and so when you make a play, you know, there's still another play to be made, right? You throw one touchdown in a game, you still got to come back and make plays to compete and of course the other team's good too. So if they make a play on you, right? Like everyone's looking to you to see how you respond. So I always want to be even killed and so yeah, like coaches will come up to you, they'll talk to you and everything, but my mindset is already on to the next play. How can I improve? What do I need to do to execute moving forward no matter if it was a success successful play or negative play that just happened. >> Even if the fumble's not on you, there's no like damn it's my second play and that >> No, I mean it's football, right? Like it's football, you know, we all want to make plays and like the guys up front they want to protect me, right? They're not trying to get me hit and so no, I think yeah, like I've looked over there and I was like wow, the flat's wide open. Where's the corner and you know, he's in my chest. So um like it part of football and I think that's how you respond. So, as I said, like to be able to for us to go out, but when we get the ball on the 10-yard line, we go 90 yards for a touchdown. Um then we come out third quarter, put together some really good drives, score, uh make some plays on special teams, get a big fumble, finish out the game well. Defense had our back all day, no matter who was out there. I think um that's a testament to playing good football, complimentary football, and um really going out there and laying it on the line each play. >> Obviously, no Ben Niemann, and you guys still working on some positions at offensive line, but just what's your early impressions of the unit as a whole as y'all come together? >> Yeah, I think they're they're becoming a cohesive unit. Like, we had a lot of guys getting in there, and I thought the communication was really well. Like, um in the third quarter, we had a center go down, Niese, um on the screen, and Seth came in there, picked up right where he left off, and was able to finish out the drive. So, those guys, you know, they have to be ready, and you know, I obviously we talked about the quarterback position, but I think like the O-line's also the other hardest position to always be ready, right? Cuz it's the five guys out there, but on any any given day, anyone could be up and have to get get thrust out there, and you're So, they're they're playing against the best athletes in the world, and they're going backwards, right? So, um I thought they did a really good job today communicating, stepping in there, making plays. I know they'll say we have things to clean up, and you know, it's preseason week two, so we got time to to get it under wraps, but I really enjoyed being able to be behind that unit today. >> Ashford, >> Last one, Dave. >> Just uh thoughts on him out there today and Thayer and kind of his ability to process pretty quick, it seems. >> Yeah, yeah, I thought he operated well. I know um he definitely probably wanted to get in the end zone, um but the operation was smooth, especially like the second quarter. Sometimes you stand there, you know, you get the uh rush of the game beginning, and then you got to wait a quarter to get out there. It can be hard, so he stepped in there, went right down the field, um was moving the ball, and I thought again, he he does a good job showing a lot of poise, getting an understanding of the offense, and as any quarterback will say, if you're not the guy getting all the reps right now, now it's just get more reps under your belt, get more comfortable, so that you're ready to evolve to any situation you're put in. >> One thing Dan Campbell always says is just a totally different deal actually learning all this stuff in the game. What do you feel like you learned from last week to this week? >> Yeah, a lot. I mean, you know, you're playing football again. And I feel like it's an amazing team, and there's a lot of guys here that do their job at a very high level. And uh it's it's a testament to those guys, and I'm excited to be able to have their respect in that regard. But um it's it's a good feeling to look over and see them see them lit, so it's good, man. I love it here. >> It seems like you got the quarterbacks' respect. Both of those guys had good things to say about you, and you've been on the field with them. What do you think about the way they command the offense and just command the huddle? >> Absolutely, man. Those guys do their job at a high level. And uh as a running back, it's my job to protect them, and it's their job to get us in the right play, get us in the right thing. And I have some history with Dobbs. Um you know, when I was in New England, he was in New England as well, so I know know we know we go back. But those guys do a great job, and they both played great today um at a very high level. And um so it's great to be able to be back there with them, cuz um you know, if there's anything that I need, I might be able to ask them in the moment, and um they did that. So I'm thankful to be able to be back there protecting them. I'm thankful for them to be able to go out there and play at a high level like they did. >> I know you said you're a veteran, so you're used to this a little bit, but what is the process of getting ready for a game in 72 hours? >> Oh man. Um man, it's no straightforward process. I mean, football is football. And people fail to realize like in in football you have to be pretty intelligent because you have to be able to know things at a very high level and be able to react when they're called. So, it was about a lot of learning, a lot of late nights sitting up and um and learning. So, I feel like I had to I teach myself pretty fast, get caught up to speed, but I feel like as a pro that's your job. And uh coming into year eight, you know, it's you have no excuse. No matter no matter what the opportunity is, you got to be able to be prepared for and then it came and I feel like great things happened from that.
