title: Is Aidan Hutchinson About to Reach Another Level?
text: One number? >> Yeah. >> [laughter] >> But um let's talk about Aidan Hutchinson. I think that's the exciting part because uh we we talked about Hall of Famers earlier and I think with Hutch you just kind of assume he's Hutch. He's great. But is [clears throat] there another level Hutch can get to, you know, Defensive Player of the Year winner? He was fourth in the league in sacks last year coming off a broken leg. People need to understand that as well. But um I'll ask the question to you guys. Dan was talking high about him. He's been really good lately, obviously. We know what he is. But is there another level for Aidan Hutch to >> Who wants to lead? >> Go ahead, Jay Rog. >> Yeah, I mean, there's there's always an opportunity to get better. But I think we need to start off with this. Top five in sacks, first in pressure, top three in win rate, close to the top of the league in in uh time to pressure and time to sack and his his get-off for his size is is really good. So, like Aidan Hutchinson's already I don't want to say budding up against his ceiling, but he's he's really really really good. And so, what is the next tier? Well, it's Myles Garrett, right? Like Myles Garrett is from another planet. Uh how do you how do you tap into to that level of talent and you know, it's it's just continuing to to tweak and fine-tune and get a little bit better in in all the things that you already do really well. But I will say being able to practice daily against Penei Sewell to refine those techniques against your equal in the world on the blocking side is is the best thing that Hutchinson can possibly ask for. You know, all these other great edge rushers don't have or very few of them have that that great counterpart in practice to to push them in that iron sharpens iron way. And so, you know, I think Sewell is such a key to where Hutchinson's already reached because he's grown so much since what I thought was a pedestrian rookie year despite the sack numbers to where he is now and and you know, creating that ceiling for him to get even a little bit better. >> Yeah, I think the area where Hutch stands to improve the most this year and this might sound counterintuitive is by playing a little bit less each game and the Lions it appears on paper finally have a defensive line that will allow him to do that. He was the only defensive end in the NFL last year in the regular season who played over a thousand snaps. He just and he he plays a huge load and over the course of a year, you know, that has to wear on you and even over the course of a game and now that's something that Aiden has even acknowledged and I think he talked about it in the spring. I asked him again when we had him on our Fox 2 training camp special, hey with with these fresh legs on the edge now in DJ Wonnum and Derek Moore, while of course you want to be out there for every single play, could you stand to benefit do you think from a few more breathers per game? And he said, yeah, I I think so and he actually said that we you know, we began to do that by the end of last season and I felt it later in games where I had like a little extra pop that I might not have had before and sure enough if you go back and look at his deployment and his production at the end of last season, he was playing over the first 13 games 93% of the Lions defensive snaps and over the last four, that fell to 83% which feels a little bit more realistic. And over those four games, six sacks. Now, it doesn't mean that there's a direct correlation between those two things, but when he acknowledges it himself that he felt like he had a little extra pop, it's worth exploring and I asked Shep that same question maybe two weeks ago that you know, with Wonnum and Moore, do you guys consider giving Hutch a few extra blows per game? And you know, he hits you with the with the first retort, which is always, "Yeah, you come down and tell Hutch you're not playing 90, you know, 95% of the snaps in this game." But, he went on to to sort of concede, "Yes." He said, "Seriously, absolutely. That is something that they're thinking about." Because he acknowledges the wear and tear over 21, 22 weeks just takes its toll on the body when you're asking a guy to play 90%, 95% of snaps every single week, especially when he is playing a highly physical position where it's like shock and shed, as Shep said, every play. And so, you know, he said, "You want to get to a point where Hutch doesn't feel like, I got to carry this load. I got to do this by myself. You want to get to a point where he can think to himself, 'All right, I'm tired. Let me tap my head and let my brother come get some.'" So, I I I do think that they're equipped for the first time to scale back just a little bit on Hutch's use, and they should feel, and he should feel, the benefit of that late in games and late in the season. >> I do think that can go a long way, Birch. I think that's a good point to bring up. Something I'll talk about, like I remember Hutch's 2023 season, his second year in the league. Like, I want to say the majority of that season people were kind of disappointed in his production. Um he finished that year with 11 and 1/2 sacks and 100 pressures. I think the pressures were second or first in the in the league among edge rushers. Um now, the final two games of the year, um game number 16 and 17, he had three sacks against the Cowboys, and he finished with two sacks in week 18 against the Vikings. Before that, he only had six and 1/2 sacks through the first, you know, 15 games of the season. And I was trying to tell everyone, like this guy's productive, he's just not finishing correctly. And like he doesn't have a ton of help on the edge, um but he's having a really good season. He just needs to learn how to finish some of these more some of these sacks a little bit more. And then he goes off and he has five sacks in the last two games, everyone's like, "Oh, that was a pretty good year." I'm like, "Okay, like I'm glad I'm glad we're on the same page." You look at what he did last year and obviously he was on such a tour pace in 2024. I would have loved to see what he did with a full game a full season of of games that year. I think he probably would have had like 17-18 sacks at his pace, but even last year another 100 pressures. This time he gets up to 14 and a half sacks. And now everyone's like, oh this guy's elite. Like this is the Hutch that we're we're talking about. I'm like he was basically doing this. He just didn't have the help on the other end, you know, funneling things back his way after he's creating pressure. That's what can limit you from 11 and a half sacks to 14 and a half sacks when you do have a little bit of help on the edge. And Alim McNeill Muhammad what he did last year helped Aiden. This year you're talking about the rotation of guys that are going to be opposite of him. Derrick Moore we saw what he did in practice today. He was tearing stuff up. I'm sure we'll talk about him later this episode, but he had a great day. DJ Wonnum we see what he can do and we know what he can be in this league. Tyler Lacy playing that big end. They're going to have a rotation of guys that I'm really comfortable with doing their job. I think that Hutch is going to appreciate this year having that consistent help across of him. And then you think about some of those games last year where Hutch would have a sack and then it would get called back because of a penalty by someone else. Like Jerry Jacobs or Brian Branch something like that. Like probably three sacks that were taken away off his off his total last year. He probably could have had like 17, 17 and a half last year if we're being honest. So I absolutely think, you know, we're talking about the question is Hutch poised for even more? Based on what we're seeing in practice right now, I would say yes. And I think the question is can he get the help opposite of him to create that environment to where he can take his game to another level because he's been consistent really for three years now at this level. And he's finishing more. He's got a better pass rush repertoire. Going against Sewell every day like you said Justin is continuing to make this guy better. And now he's at a point where he is making young guys better going against him. We see what he's doing for Blake Miller. Blake Miller's getting a first hand education in defending Aidan Hutchinson. >> Yeah. He's probably getting a D in that right now, but it's [laughter] okay. >> It's Aidan Hutchinson, man. He's going [clears throat] to give a lot of people that. >> So, um I I I look at his development over the last, you know, two, three seasons and this guy's at another level. Is he quite the Myles Garrett conversation? No. That doesn't mean he's not an all pro talent and he really is and we're seeing that uh in practice. We've seen that last year. I do think he's going to continue adding to his game and taking his game to another level. I just think I look at what's around him in training camp and I really like the setup they have for him between Derrick Moore, DJ Wonnum, Tyler Lacy. I think these guys are going to play within the structure of the defense, funnel things back his way and he just has to take care of business, which I think he will do. >> I just want to statistically hammer home Colton's point here on the the '23 season. Hutchinson in the middle of that year and even kind of bleeding into the second half had a seven game stretch where he had one game with one sack. He had two sacks over the course of 10 games and like you just that's that's not acceptable for great players. You know, you can say he's pressuring and having an impact, but if you're not finishing and getting those sacks, like great players don't have those kind of lulls. He goes into that '23 season before he breaks his leg and sacks in four out of five games. Last year he had sacks in 12 out of 17 and I don't think had more than a back-to-back stretch uh without a sack and, you know, if you want to compare it to Myles Garrett, Myles Garrett had sacks in 13 out of 17. So, the consistency and the sack production consistency for Hutchinson's really what has taken off here in the last two seasons. >> Yeah, and if we're going to start comparing every defensive end to Myles Garrett, >> The greatest defensive player of all time. >> Sweet. No one's as good as Myles Garrett. Exactly. I was going to say, he's in the conversation for greatest defensive player ever. So, if you want him to be Myles Garrett, you're going to be forever disappointed. It doesn't mean he's not one of the 25 best players in the NFL.

title: Insiders preview Indianapolis Colts vs. Atlanta Falcons
text: We're here at Lucas Oil Stadium for the Colts' second of three preseason games and the first action here since January at Lucas Oil Stadium for the Colts. It is 2026. The NFL season is nearing. I'm Nathan Brown, your Colts insider for the Indianapolis Star. He's Joel A. Erickson. We are here to break down what we're looking for in this game against the Falcons. We saw these two teams face off in a pair of joint practices earlier this week at Grand Park. More starters that we were watching there. Some A lot A lot more for the Colts. Virtually all of their backups going to be playing today and not a whole lot of starter action. What are you going to be most looking at here today on the field, Joel? >> The backup quarterbacks. Same story. The kickers a little bit, too. Spencer Shrader, I think the Colts like him. I would think they want to see if he can get back in this race. But really, it's the backup quarterbacks. Riley Leonard is supposed to start and play the first half today. Anthony Richardson will play the second half. There There was some talk after the way Richardson played and Leonard played in the first preseason game that it had to do with who they were playing with. Now that gets even up. This Falcon secondary really struggled in the practices. So I'm curious to see if Riley Leonard [music] can take advantage of that today. Other than that, I think for the most part it's it's it's those spots and it's really If I'm looking for a sleeper spot, it's the backup [music] offensive line. I think when you start going through that, it gets pretty thin once you get past Jaylon Farmer. >> And we've got a couple guys that are injured there, too. Nolan Rucci, Luke Tenuta, who have both been hurt. So the Colts have brought in a new name there. So we'll see how that battle plays out. I wanted to ask you, too, that backup quarterback battle. I know there's been a lot of chatter. The Colts have said they want to keep all three of these guys. Shane Steichen told us on Thursday that they're still undecided and are going to let this play out for the next couple weeks. For someone who's watched every single snap of these guys in camp, where do you feel like this battle is right now? If If the Colts went out today, and I'm not I know some folks ask us who we think should be. I don't think that's the question to ask. Knowing Shane Steichen, who do you feel like, from what you've seen, would be his backup quarterback if today was week one in the NFL season? >> So, the the hard part here is that a lot of what I think matters most to Shane Steichen is stuff that's very difficult for us to see, because it's are you going the right place with the ball? And it might seem like oh, you just throw to the open guy. It's harder within the offense. I'm just telling you right now, from our perspective, to know where to go with the ball versus what Steichen would think. I think Leonard has been more accurate and more consistent from an accuracy standpoint. Anthony Richardson gives you a much higher ceiling, and there's a different kind of offense they can run with him that could be a curveball, I think, for teams. So, I actually do think it's a very difficult decision based on where we are. But, again, last year we thought it was a lot closer than it was with Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson. It was Daniel Jones the whole time. So, that's kind of running through my head as we go into these last two preseason games. >> I'd also keep an eye on the Colts secondary today. Makai Blackman and Jaylon Johnson Edwards did not have great showings in the preseason game in New England last week. They're going to have to potentially use some of those rotational guys at corner as we get closer to week one, knowing that Cam Taylor Britt will be out with a one-game suspension. [music] We haven't seen Mooney Ward out on the field for the last couple weeks or so. We don't know where he is as he works through a back injury. I'd also keep a an eye on the linebackers. We've seen a lot of guys rotate through. I don't know who would play or wouldn't play from a starter standpoint. I don't know if they even have starters decided yet. So, that's where else I would keep an eye. If you are [music] here at Lucas Oil Stadium or watching from home, we hope you guys will tune in. Catch us after the game. We'll have a breakdown of everything that happens out here on the field. Several stories on indystar.com. Keep an eye there. Thanks for supporting and subscribing and we'll be back to you after today's action.

title: Ka'imi Fairbairn training camp presser | Full Q&A
text: Yeah. >> I know you've kicked here before quite a bit. We'll talk to you about just the fine points of kicking. What do you feel like this year was the biggest for you? What did you work on and got better at? >> Yeah, the technical stuff of kicking is always going to be there. Trying to sharpen my sharpen my craft as much as I can. I I did some things with my kicking coach just to sharpen up and get ready get better for the few misses that I had last year. I'm trying to get better on kickoffs. More piercing ball flight. And yeah, just the the regular steps you take every off season to get better. >> How much of a role do you have in getting Kai up to speed on exactly what you guys need in the operation? Is it just feedback? Is it fine-tuning? What exactly do you do with him to kind of get it to where exactly you guys need it? >> Yeah, it's just uh him getting familiar with our operation and our culture. And Frank's done a great job of that. And he's been real um uh you know, listening to what we have to say and and getting up to speed really quickly. Um the main thing for him is just knowing our operation and our cadence and our rhythm. And he's got really quick hands. We we play ping pong every day. So, that hand-eye coordination I like to say we work on that in our time off. But yeah, I've enjoyed working with Kai a lot. >> You guys have changed a lot since you guys have been together. >> Yeah. >> Has anything you have over the years you felt like we've become better at trying to get the new guy up to speed? >> Yeah, you kind of know the the things that you got to highlight or emphasize on whatever it is on game day especially. The communication system like the less I have to think about his job or the snapper's job, the better I am. Um so, just communicating all those little details at the beginning. >> Is there any difference in that he's so young than the other punters? Um no, I wouldn't say. He's held in college, so he's familiar with with the job and he got good work last year, so No, it's I wouldn't say there's any problem. Yeah, he I don't tap him on the shoulder, but he knows whatever whatever he needs me to kick, I'll give her rip. Yeah, definitely you see the range extending for kickers every year. So, you know, getting stronger and not having to change my technique once you get to that farther distances has been my goal. Yeah, we made a few couple weeks past 63, 66. I'd say to begin with it's just fun. Like I I enjoy it. That was a sport I played growing up, so it's fun to get moving and my mind working in different way. And then just warming my hips up now than having to kick, you know, a 50 yd ball, a 30 yd ball. I can start with short passes. That's really my purpose for it. Um Frank's great for me because he challenges me and he puts me in uncomfortable situations to try and get me ready for game. So, when game comes along, I'm ready. He's not not scared to communicate the hard way, which I appreciate. He coaches me hard and that's all I can ask for. >> Several players this off season got contract extension. For you, what did it mean to have an organization believe so much that they want to give you a brand new deal and keep you around for the long term because of they see you as the kicker of this franchise? >> Um it's everything. This is home, you know, I've been here 10 years now and uh what you know, the McNairs, what Nick has done, what DeMeco's done has been incredible. So, you know, going through the the stages of, you know, the Texans where we were good and then we were bad and now we're you know, fighting for a Super Bowl. So, um all I want to do is win here. So, you know, I'm I'm happy to to be here for extended amount of time and um I'm I'm just going to put my head down and go to work. Yeah, we have a open dialogue about those kind of things. He presented it to me and I said it it would be uh an advantage for me to just take that game off. I I was worn for the first half and then uh kind of build that um that volume of kicks and um I appreciate it. It was a huge bonus for me. So, yeah. Props Props to him. Thank you. Thanks, guys.

title: DeMeco Ryans training camp presser | Full Q&A
text: What's up, coach? What's up, guys? Ready to roll? We signed two veteran guys. We'll see what they can provide when it comes to adding depth to our receiver room. We know everybody knows, no secret that we're we lost a very significant piece of our receiver room and and Jayden Higgins. So, still trying to find a way to, you know, help out in the receiver room and that's what those two guys provide. Veteran experience, guys done it before, done it at a high level, played a lot of different systems. We'll see what they can bring to us. The competitive nature of our offensive line definitely picked up from where it has been. I really love with our first group, the way they played in the game, you know, Thursday, just the way we had clean pockets to throw the football, the way we cleaned up the pocket when we were free. So, there was a lot of really good things, good positive things to build on from the offensive line. Waynes dealing with a broken thumb. We'll see, you know, how he progresses and when he'll be when he'll be able to get back. From the second half is just being disciplined. We have a lot of young guys in there. Some guys only been here for a few days. So, it's really just being disciplined, being where you're supposed to be, being able to make a play. So, uh when I look at the game, really watching that first half and what I saw our guys do, I saw our guys take a step in what I asked them to do and that's rep our style of play. And our guys did that. They repped our style really well and I thought we had a really great first half. And the other guys were getting those opportunities in the second half. You just have to find a way to be where you're supposed to be and make a play when it's your time to make a play. Jaylen Smith is continuing to improve. Uh he made a few plays in the game. Uh what I love about Jaylen Smith in the is the the play of the game to me is you know, a run breaks out on us on the left side there, and Jaylen is the right corner stuck at the line of scrimmage, but he plays with elite effort. Runs the guy down, gets him down, and the next next play that's when Wade picks it off and takes it to the house. So, it just really, you know, reinforces what I teach, and that's playing with elite effort. No matter how play breaks down, you play with great effort, you can make plays. This is what Jaylen has done, and he continues to progress. He's done a really good job on special teams as our gunner. So, he's, you know, second year, lost a lot of time his first year with injury, but he's stepping back in in a really good way, positive way, showing up for us. It's been valuable for to us to have Trent at this time. You know, we didn't have Trent, he didn't he wasn't able to go through training camp. So, I know for anybody who's able to go through camp and get those reps, it's only going to be beneficial for you to come to season, and Trent's has done a good job. We see if you look at the runs and when we're out there, you run it behind Trent, there's going to be a lane, and that's what he does. He moves people with ease. It's hard to get around him. In pass rush, it's hard to go through him. So, he's a he's one of the the better guys, you know, with his size and his his ability. Like, I think the quarterback likes him, and also the running backs like running behind him because he provides that kind of lane for us. >> It's not impossible for undrafted guys to make the team, but it's a little bit difficult just with the talent that you all have. What do you think about uh the undrafted players you know have to go through and and all they put themselves through to try to make the team? >> I have a special place in my heart for the undrafted players because a lot of people would say just based on where you are you shouldn't make it. But, you know, if guys come here and they just put their head down, they work the right way, do what we're asking them to do, if you're one of the top 53 guys on our team, we're not turning away great players who can help us go win football games. So, it never matters to me, you know, when we signed a guy, where we signed him, how much a guy getting paid, it doesn't matter. Once we got 90 guys on our team, it's our job to decipher who are the best 53 for us and we're going to go with the best 53 in our opinion that allows us to go win football games. So, undrafted guys have made a Aziz was an undrafted free agent in 2019 and look at the career that he's had. He's done an outstanding job just working the right way, being accountable, being a great teammate, a great leader, and he's had himself a tremendous career thus far. So, our undrafted guys can look to Aziz and and you want to see what it takes to become a pro and this what take what it takes to stick around. It's about that consistency, being a professional. That's what Aziz represents and that's what those guys can look to to see what it takes to make it. Go ahead, John. I thank you for the question, John. Bourne is he's done a fantastic job, you know, all camp. And we look at that touchdown that Woody ran. I'm talking about Trent and how he blocked, but as I told our guys like the touchdown saving the block was Bond. And the effort at which he stayed with his man, he finished it. That's great for any receiver. And when you can block the way Bond blocked on that play, it was outstanding for us. It broke the play home. Bond has done a great job. The scouting report with him was smart, tough, dependable guy. And ever since he stepped foot here in Houston, that's what he's been. He's been smart, he's been tough, he's been dependable, a guy we can trust, and he's made a ton of plays for us. >> To take the little Brian's words, smart, tough, dependable. >> I don't know Bill O'Brien's words. I didn't talk to him. >> Going going into the Carolina game, you know what your priority for all of this is going to be for this this being the last of the season game. What are the top priorities leading to this game and then looking forward to the first game of the season? >> The top priorities for us this week, first and foremost, we'll get an opportunity to go and joint practice versus the Panthers, so we're excited about. And our our starters going out and competing in that joint practice versus those guys, and then we'll see, you know, how the game shapes up and who will be out there for the game. But the the main priority for this week is getting our guys good valuable reps versus a really good Carolina team. >> Okay, just a couple more. >> Jake Homos is new for you guys from free agency this year. How has he kind of adapted and picked up the defense? And correct me if I'm wrong, it seemed like he was maybe making some of the calls for you guys when he was out there. >> Yeah, Jake Jake Homos picked up the defense really well. He is our been a signal caller for us, the Mike backer. He's wearing the green dot when he's on the field. He's done a great job of communicating, uh showing up, making a few plays, uh made a nice play in special teams there on the kickoff in the game on this past Thursday, just beating this guy, playing with speed, playing physical, making a nice tackle there. So, he's a guy who's showing that he can add some value when it comes to position flex, special teams, you know, four core player, he can do that for us, and he can go play on defense as well. So, I'm pleased with his camp, pleased with what he's done uh since he's been here. >> How do you feel about how he played, especially late in the game, big third down stops for you guys? What do you make of his play? >> Yeah, Calvin he he tackled well. Uh he he flies around. He plays with that swarm mindset. I love that about him. He's a smart player, uh small undersized player, but he's going to bring everything he has, and that's what I love about him. And he brings it every single day, whether he's covering, uh he's tackling, he's going to bring it. And that's all you can ask, and he's done that. He's done a really good job as well all camp. >> Brandon. >> Obviously, you got another glimpse of what Woody can bring to this offense with the touch down run. What what have you seen in his growth from last year throughout the offseason and now in camp a year later? And what big strides would you need to go back there? >> Yeah. Woody's done an outstanding job from I I see the growth from starting with me is the uh pass protection. I thought he's the he had a really great rep uh in the game. They sent the corner pressure from a double A gap look. Woody did an outstanding job of picking up the corner blitz. He's just being stout in his protection. And then, when he's touching the football, I'm seeing a more dynamic, faster, more physical runner. He's running behind his pass. He broke a few tackles on his touchdown run. He just looks faster, looks more decisive. He I mean, he's looking really special. Looking like he's going to have a special year. We'll also see what he can do from the kick returner spot as well. So, he's added value to our team. He's grown a ton, uh much more feel like relaxed and confident in his style of play and what he can bring for us. So, I'm I'm excited about Woody this year. All right. Thank you, guys. >> Enjoy the weekend, fellas.

title: Marlin Klein training camp presser | Full Q&A

I think that's why I chose Michigan, to be honest with you. >> When you look at offensive coordinator Nick Caley, he is one of the former tight ends to coach. >> Yep. >> How much has he been able to help you get yourself acquainted to this offense? >> I mean, so much. I think that's somebody, you know, he's kind of biased. He always says he's not, but he is. And that's a good thing for us. Uh I think, you know, the the coach he is, how much You can just tell how much it means to him every single day, every single meeting. Uh every time you talk to him, it's it's all about ball. Barner, a veteran tight end there. So, you got to kind of learn the ins and outs. Has it been an easy transition to do that with guys like Foster and and Dalton, who have been in multiple offenses before? >> Yeah, I think I think, to be honest with you, I think it's been such a blessing. Barner, like all those guys, to now being here with Kate Stoever, Foster, Dalton, Brevin. Like, I mean, I've I've kind of been around the best of the best, so so people always ask me, like, "Who do you like to watch?" I I like to watch the guys that I'm with. Uh cuz I think I truly believe that they're the best of the best. Uh and and I can learn from them, you know, so much stuff every single day uh with them even talking. Just just being able to watch them do what they do on and off the field. It's It's It's been a blessing. Uh I think I want to do whatever it takes to win. So, I don't like losing. I hate losing. I did that enough in my my last year at Michigan. Um but I think in my career I've won a lot of games and it always started with running the ball, being a physical football team. All the good teams that I've been on we all were able to run the ball on whoever was in front of us. I think that's kind of what this offense shows what what coach what coach DeMeco is, you know, trying to establish and what the front office has done a great job with bringing guys in that are able to do that stuff. Um so, I think it's just been it's been a blessing being here, being coached by those guys and I truly believe that whatever they, you know, whatever play they call, whatever they teach us is going to be the right thing at the end of the day. Yeah, I mean obviously I can't speak for both sides, but I mean CJ was over there too. Nico was on my side. So, to be honest with you, I love those guys. I don't know how they feel about me. You got to ask them, but >> [laughter] >> now where they played, I still hate that team down there, but I love those guys. They're they're leader of men, great players, great teammates and being being able to to be around those guys every single day in the locker room, on the field. I've learned so much from both of them. Look, I'm always going to root for the For For For you know, I'm never going to say anything good about the team down south. They might be able to do that, but uh I don't play there anymore. I do have a winning record on them, and I'm proud of that cuz you know, Michigan means everything to me. Uh it's done so much for me, so I truly take pride in that, but I know they do, too. So, uh you know, late November, that last week in November is going to be, you know, some talks. Uh maybe we'll watch a game together. Who Who knows, but um yeah, I'm I'm looking forward to it. >> Can you talk about your relationship with CJ and just how much you've grown with him as quarterback and what you've seen from his development throughout fall camp? >> Yeah, I think he's gotten better every single day. Uh obviously, I wasn't here the the last couple of years, and he played at a different school than me, so I don't know how much his progression has been over these last couple of years, but uh being able to be here uh coming from a freshman QB last year, my my last year in college, to to now being with a guy like CJ, uh the leadership that he has uh stood out to me day one. I think he's a leader of men. Uh you know, he he just He shows He shows up every single day with the same energy. Uh he's ready to work every single day, and he's going to push you to be better uh cuz he wants this team to win, and and he's going to make sure that we do. >> I'm sorry. Earlier, you talked about the fact that you're in a position um How have you all bonded, and what is the competition like? Cuz there's only so many, you know, there's only so many snaps going to be given out. So, how is the competition going >> I think all of us just continue to come in, uh work work our tails off, and and obviously, everybody's going to try to get the most catches, most touchdowns, and whatever, but I think what stood out to me is everybody pushes each other. I think, you know, the the more we push each other, the more we're going to the the more we're going to get out of each other. Uh you There's no complacency in that room. Uh Coach Ferentz, tight ends coach, Coach Kiley, they would never allow that stuff, so uh I think that the more we push each other, um you're going to get the best out of each other. So, uh whoever they're going to put out there on Sundays, that that's the coaching staff's uh decision. Uh all I know is we're going to work our tails off and and put that in their corner. Foster. >> Sorry guys. Thanks. Thank you.

A smaller classic undersized receiver with good hands and good route running ability. Zay Jones former second round draft pick from my alma mater East Carolina and the son of former Dallas Cowboys first round draft pick Robert Jones, my former college teammate. Zay is a long receiver at 6'2 200 lbs. Watching him run you see the long stride, you can see some speed and he is still getting back into a football mode after tearing his Achilles last year for the Arizona Cardinals. title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Any word on Trey Moore if it looks like a long-term injury? >> Uh yeah, just I'll give you the getting back to you from last night. I just want to make sure I you asked me last night about three guys. Um Trey will miss some time. You know, I don't see him back being soon. I'm not sure how long it will be. I think we'll determine that later when all the testing is done. Um but Trey will definitely miss some time with an ankle. Ali got hit in the ribs. He was cleared to go back into the game. We just decided not to put him back in the game. Um but he was cleared to go back in. And then the other one you asked me about was Ronnie. Um it was Ronnie's hamstring on that one. He actually made a really nice play. He cut across. We got off the field on the third down. Um but he felt his hamstring. So, I would say Ronnie will probably be unlikely this week. >> Thanks. >> Yeah, no problem. >> Omar? >> Uh Jeff, obviously you went into the second game trying uh wanting to take a look at some of the um deeper deeper players on your bench. What did you learn about that unit and those players and and also the rookies? >> Uh I mean, that's a you talk about that, you're talking about every single player. Some I was really pleased with. I mean, I thought some guys stood out and um helped their cases and and you know, made some plays. I thought the rookies who we asked to play, I thought a lot of those were in and out quickly. Um >> [clears throat] >> you know, and then clearly we have some work to do, Omar. There's um you know, there was there was some mental mistakes. There was some physical mistakes. A lot of those guys got a lot of time for the first time together and um you know, certainly the outcome wasn't what we wanted. I just I think that's coaching. I think that's playing and it it needs to be better and in a lot of those cases. But But what it really does help though is when you sit down today and you you know, you take a deep breath and you get away from it's a preseason game, and the score was the score, and now you have this chance to really evaluate these players. It is such a good evaluation tool for Solly and I to sit down and talk um to where [clears throat] this roster is at, where it needs to go, what needs to get better, who we feel like moved up and down, and it's why preseason games to play all these guys is really really important. Thank you. >> Chris? >> Hey Half, uh wanted to ask you about what this week means to you and to some of these players. Obviously, roster cuts are coming up. Um some players will have dreams ended. Some players will have dreams realized. And tell me from the standpoint of, you know, Stephen Dix or from veterans who have been in the league for a few years, what do you want to see? What does this week mean to you? What does this week mean to them? >> Gosh, I mean, you're talking about Stephen Dix who just got here yesterday. I mean, >> [sighs] >> it means a lot for him, right? I mean, I'd like to actually sit down with him today and have a conversation with him. I think I've said two words to him other than talking to him about the calls on defense. So, get to know a guy like that, but you know, this last week's going to be different for a lot of guys, you know? Our starters didn't really play. None of them. They They They barely played on Friday. Some of the guys who will start got a handful of snaps. So, for those guys, we got to get back to work. Um we got to continue to build off of our scheme and what we want to do going into the actual season. So, the practices are going to be a little bit different now, right? The The guys who haven't played football, we need to ramp up their reps tomorrow in practice. But then you get a lot of guys who just played. We have to be really careful there because they're just coming off a game, and they're not going to be ready to practice. So, their practice will be more like a jog through. So, tomorrow when you guys are out there, you're going to see full speed with some guys, jog through for some others to get their bodies back because a lot of those guys are going to play more on Friday night. And then the ones now, it's the starters, it's we got to ramp this up and and really get ready for the season. Uh some more situational football, uh some more move the ball and just play ball uh where there's less scripting and and and more thinking from the players. And then like you're saying, there's some guys who are on the bubble that, you know, they're fighting [clears throat] for their jobs and we need to do everything we can as coaches to help them. and then they need to put in the work so we can kind of, you know, let Solly and I sit down and evaluate where we're at with the roster, but certainly probably a stressful time for some players and you got to respect all of them and what they're trying to do. >> All right. Thanks, coach. >> Isaiah? >> Morning, coach. >> What's up, Isaiah? >> Two questions for you. The first, I know you said you wanted to review the film um on the quarterbacks. So, what did you see from them after you reviewed the film? >> Well, there's 37 offensive snaps, which is probably the lowest that I've ever seen in my whole entire life as a coach on offense. So, you're talking about minimal snaps for both of them. Um and some really hard situations that we put them in. You know, being backed up, playing from the minus five-yard line multiple times, trying to throw the ball. You know, backed up in there, it was hard. Um so, there's things where you know, I think they were put in some some tough situations, but then truthfully, there was times where just it wasn't good enough and it needs to be played better and it needs to be coached better and you don't always want to put it all on the quarterback. It's did the wideout run the right route? Did he drop the ball? Was the protection okay? but just [clears throat] really a tough night to get a really clear eval. you know, but certainly it needs to improve. >> Cool. And then I wanted to ask about the trio rookie receivers. You know, Kevin Coleman was obviously fed the ball a lot last night. You know, Caleb Brothers had the highlight play on the first preseason game. And obviously Chris Bell still working back from injury, but there's some promise there. Like, what do you want to see ideally like in a perfect scenario? What would you like to see from your trio rookie receivers this year? >> From the whole year? Um, improvement. You know, I'd like to see them, you know, push one another and I'd like to see them develop good chemistry with with Malik and um, you know, and and really kind of find out what their roles going to be and who they are. You know, what type of receiver they are in the NFL and who they're going to become. And I'd like to see them, you know, develop a level of consistency where we can trust them. You know, playing as a rookie is not the easiest thing in the world. Um, I'm sure there'll be some highlight moments like you talked about last week with Caleb. And then there's going to be some moments where we're going to have to grow and learn from. And then there's going to be a lot of our rookies this year. I mean, if you look, you know, at guys who are going to be playing, there's probably going to be quite a few of them on the field. So, that's what I'm looking for. I'm excited for them, though. >> Cool. Thank you. >> Yeah. >> David. >> Hey Haf, a couple questions from me. First, to follow up on Perk's question. This is a roster that seems to be ever changing. Like you talked about Stephen Dix coming in and making calls defensively. Jayon McMillan just claimed. How realistic is it as we're in this last week before cuts to for guys to make the necessary jump in a week as opposed to the ones who have been through it for all of camp and and going back to OTAs. >> Say that again. >> Uh, guys that have just joined this team and and are going to be fighting for a roster spot this last week. How realistic is it for those Uh, as opposed to players who have been uh in your system since OTAs and the start of camp. >> I got you. Yeah, I mean certainly it's it's going to be just by the nature of it, it's going to be a little bit harder because they're going to have limited reps, right? In in practice this week, but then they're going to get another shot Friday night to play a lot. So, we'll give them a fair chance, you know, watch the tape, see if we see in the talent individual the makeup of the player. Um, so we're going to have to dig in as coaches and they're going to have to give us everything they have. It's just going to be a a much smaller sample size, but at the end of the day if if we feel those players can make us better, and then [clears throat] then we got to really think hard about that. I mean, harder, but they'll have a chance. >> The other question I had for you on an unrelated note is Quinn Ewers, is there any chance he can practice this week? >> Yeah, no, I'm I'm hopeful that we'll get to see him at practice this week. >> Well, >> Hi Jeff, I wanted to follow up a little bit on what you were just talking about with Isaiah regarding the offense. Um, obviously we've only seen them really the starters for like 14 players at 14 players in a game situation. Uh, do you have you learned as much as you would have liked at this point in the preseason about your offense and what stands out most either on the positive side or negative side regarding your ideal offense? >> Well, I'd always like to learn more and know more, but there's a fine line as we deal with some injuries, right? And decide how much we're going to play these guys in the preseason games. I think you learn a lot in practice. I think you learn a lot in joint practices. I think it's still a work in progress and it's going to be, um, but you find out a lot about your guys. Um, and we'll continue to do that this week and we'll continue to do that, you know, even we have a week after to get ready for that first game. >> So, just continue to build on it. What was the second part of your question? >> What what stands out in terms of what you've liked and maybe what you've been concerned about offensively? >> Yeah, I mean the things that I like I think, you know, you look at the quarterback and I think there's been constant improvement in confidence. There's been times when we've run the ball really well. I mean, if you look back at the Washington game with the ones and then you even look back closely, there were some good runs against the Giants and there's been some good runs against us each week as we practice against each other. Um, I think the overall consistency. I mean, it has to get better. And you know, I think that has a lot to do with finding out the depth of the team. And then getting these guys to play together more and more. And that's why it has to be this year. It has to be constant improvement as as we gel together and find out who the guys are and get them playing together. >> One more? >> Uh, wanted to ask you about traded uh, Dante Trader. He got some run last night uh, primarily with the second or third or I don't know how we figure out what unit that was. That'll do it for us tonight. Have a great night. Thank you for tuning in. >> Good night. >> Hey, this is Deuce. Thanks for tuning in to the show. If you really want to help us, [music] make sure you like us wherever you get your podcasts like Apple Podcast or Spotify. Also, make sure you follow us on the New England Patriots YouTube channel to see this show and everything else that we do here at the Patriots. Thanks a lot. [music]

title: Tommy DeVito, Kyle Williams, Behren Morton & More Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: Tom, >> one second if I cut you off. >> Go. >> Want to say thoughts and prayers are what you Quinnon and his family. Obviously not something that you like to see on the field. Obviously, it's a physical game, so definitely not the way you want the game to start out. So, I hear he's doing better though. So, thoughts and prayers with him and his family. So, >> yeah. >> Just you said that you would like to start a little quicker, cut the penalty, whatever. What did you think of that first half and what did you think of your your game tonight with the offense? H definitely some of the same stuff again, you know, just uh being ourselves, putting ourselves in tough situations. Um second and 10, it's not ideal. So still just trying to nip those little things in the butt and get better. But you can see the times where we're clicking, we're rolling. So just got to eliminate those those negatives to get us rolling faster. >> Tommy, the touchdown pass, can you take us through it and what you saw from Kyle? >> Yeah, it was great. I mean, basically two goes or three goes, one down the seam, two on the outside. The coverage they played put an isolation on Kyle. So, hold the safety, let him roll, had great protection, shoot, throw it out there, hit him, let him do the rest. >> You uh kind of describe Kyle and what you've seen of him uh since you joined the team, and as he grows, seems like he's getting better uh running routes and what have you. What do you like about him as a player? >> Twitchy. super twitchy. I mean, you can see that anytime anybody wants to come down and press him, it's like good luck. You see that last week when the dude pressed him through the fade ball, he's just his release package off the line is second to none. It's special. And I know he's still growing as a player with everything else. But it's awesome to see that and able to play fast and use his speed and play big and do all the great things he's been doing. >> And and how about watching Baron at the end of the game? Um, I know you have the blender in the quarterback room, but I does that like get put away this week after what you saw? >> Oh, he certainly was not in the blender. You know, that was that was awesome to see. I was so happy for him. Uh, first NFL touchdown. I know it's preseason, but first passing touchdown is big. Something he'll remember forever. Um, so that was special. But the way he just operated drives, I think he had two 12play drives that ended up in touchdowns. 12 play drives are not not something easy to overcome and to accomplish and just sustain throughout the field and score, let alone once but twice. So, testament to him and pushing the guys up front and the group around them and finding a way to score. >> Uh Tommy, we saw you moving around in the pocket a lot tonight, whether it was to run or just kind of resetting the throw in these practices where you can't get hit. How do you work on that or is this kind of the setting where that's something that you're really focused on? >> This is the setting to focus on them because like you said in practice, dudes will just run by you. you always get into the argument with the defense. Was it a sack? Was it not a sack? You really don't know until comes up in game situations. So, this is the perfect time for that. >> It felt like, you know, this week was kind of a step forward for you from from last week. Did you feel that as well just in terms of the totality of of your game tonight? And how comfortable do you feel in your role with this team right now? >> For sure. Yeah, I feel comfortable definitely. You know, like I've always said, the more reps, the better. And obviously game reps are even better because like you just said, that's the time where you can get hit. And you know, you like to say that everybody plays the same as they do in practice, but when when those live bullets are flying, things change a little bit. So just being able to get comfortable with the guys and everybody around me and just keeping to put our best foot forward. So I think that like I said, the two joint practices definitely helped coming into this and just the more competitive periods that we have for myself, the better. >> Tommy, uh, from your point of view, how difficult would you say the wide receivers are making the upcoming roster decision, you know, for the coaching staff in terms of of who makes the 53? >> Yeah, I mean that's the best possible situation you can ask for an organization, right? To have so many options where you have to make hard decisions like that. But again, that's just testament to the coaching and to the guys are just coming in every day putting their hard hats on and working and not worrying too much about what that day is like because I've been on the other end of that day multiple times. been cut twice, you know, stayed down once. So, I've been there, but you know, the same thing I tell them, just keep your head down and work. Everything will handle itself. Um, but just enjoy the process, enjoy here. So, those guys have been doing it to the fullest. They've been staying late, especially the rookies been staying late, getting in early, making sure they're on top for all their stuff and show tonight. >> Good. Thank you guys. >> I guess Kyle, we'll start with uh your uh touchdown reception. take us through the play and and what what you did and kind of that feeling going into the end zone. >> Uh I mean, yeah, we got the look that we wanted. Uh press coverage. Uh something that I really enjoy to see and you know, just Tommy, you know, took a chance on me. You know, what a great throw. Honestly, I mean, we've been on point this whole camp. So, it was good just to see it uh connect and just strike the band. >> Kyle, your second year here now. what what are some of the things you've been focusing on to take the next step in your development? >> Um being physical for sure and just the comfortability into the system, you know, being comfortable in different places in my role and being able to just take that um with a whole lot of I would say I guess have a lot of accountability towards that. Just being comfortable and just making good decisions for real. Um, Kyle, we know it's a crowded wide receiver room right now. How would you say you have made strides specifically this week and even tonight in terms of just showing more of what you can do for this team? >> Uh, I mean, I've always been confident in my game for real. Uh, just just being consistent, honestly. That's all it is is being consistent. You know, just, you know, we have a great group of guys. You know, it's always competition. It's competitive, but it's friendly competition. You know, nobody gets mad at anybody. And it's just it's iron sharp and iron at the end of the day. So I'm really glad glad to have these great group of guys, great vets from top down. So it's just a fun room to be in. >> Kyle, on on that play, um the the 69 yard touchdown, what has to go right in order for that to to come to fruition? And do you view that as being one of the bigger strengths that you can offer a team in getting behind the defense and making those types of plays? Like is that your your biggest asset in your view? Um, I mean it's something that I'm good at, I would say. I wouldn't say it's my biggest asset, but it's something I'm good at. And honestly, you know, all 11 players got to be on the same page. You know, from QB making the right uh mic point to the line being able to hold up their blocks. Without them, you know, that play wouldn't be made. I just did my 11th and, you know, everybody else did theirs and that's how those big plays come to fruition. Hi Kyle, just going back to that that competition question, how much, you know, moving forward and and w knowing the competition, does that notion of just being ready when your number is called, how much is that going through your head? >> Um, not too much, honestly. I feel like just going through our practice and competing with these guys and just at the talks that we have is I feel like we're all prepared and I know I'm really prepared, especially what I have to do. And when that moment comes, I know I'm going to be ready cuz it's just all my prep leading up to it. >> Kyle, just watching from afar, it looks like you you've improved even in camp. Do you feel like you're getting better on a daily basis, route running and things that you you've been able to pick up with this offense? >> Oh, yeah, for sure. Day by day, brick by brick. I mean, if I feel like I wasn't getting better, that would be a shooting. I'd be shooting myself in the foot. So, I mean, I got to give it to the coaches, the players, obviously the vets, they push me, even Drake, Tommy, I mean, everybody around me pushes me, and it's the same thing vice versa. So, when you have a great group of guys that worry and care about your growth as a player, I mean, it's just like the sky's is the limit. So, for me, it's just approaching every day, you know, like it's my last and just trying to get better, take it stride by stride. >> Thank you. Appreciate you guys. How tough is it to see how a lineman go down today? And where's the depth of this group right now? Last week, too. >> Yeah, it just sucks seeing, you know, any player go down, especially an offensive lineman. Prayers are to that Eagles player, too. You know, hopefully he's all right in the beginning of the game. Um, but any player that goes down in this game, you know, it's it's scary when they go down, especially one being offensive lineman. You know, Mike Group, it sucks to see. You know, it's awesome to have everyone nice and healthy, but you know, it's football. Injuries are going to come and so, you know, it's just sucks. you know, hoping for quick recovery and just keep going forward. >> From your perspective, what happened on that sack >> uh that that came around your edge? >> Yeah, just mistakes. I just need to be able to see the twist going better and be able to pass it off with my guard and just work better together >> with Marcus going down. Were you expecting to play all the way into the fourth quarter tonight or is it kind of just all hands on deck? >> I came tonight to play, you know, however long they needed me. So whether he went down or nine, I was always just ready to play whatever they needed from me, what I was going to go out and give to them. Is there anything specific you're working on before the season starts? >> Yeah, I mean they're not going to go on and name a whole bunch, but really just physicality is the biggest thing going out there and be able to compete with, you know, the guys on the field and, you know, amazing guys we're going against right now, but once the real season comes, you know, it's going to be another level of playing and so always bringing that physicality on every play that I do is the biggest thing. >> Baron, would you describe yourself tonight as a better quarterback or punter? Uh well, first off, I want to say um you know, my thoughts and prayers just go out to the Eagles. Um you know, that guy went down. Um I wish him a speedy recovery. Um and wish nothing but the best for him. Um yeah, no, tonight was fun. Um I wasn't expecting to punt. Um it's been since high school since I punted, so um you know, just got to make the most of your opportunity when it comes. Um and so, you know, try to do that tonight. Baron, can you um just take us to the moment on the sideline when you realized that was actually going to happen that you were going to punt and what was just your reaction to it and how you responded to it? >> Yeah, coach came up to me and just said that um you know if we we if we got a punt on this drive, you're going out there. Um and so I was pretty cold at the time, so I went over to the net, hit hit a few balls. Um I asked Andy or uh Ash how how far do I need to stand back? Um he told me 15 yards and catch the ball and just put it down there. And so uh Coach Springer did a good job of lining me up. Um he said just hit it middle. Um and then we'll we'll we'll make corrections as we go. >> Can you just take us through the uh the play to to Nick at the end there? >> Yeah. Um you know it was it was a long drive. It was um you know hats off to the offensive line and keeping me safe, keeping me upright. Um Nick had a great release. Kind of you know avoided the corner. Looked like cover two. So, kind of put on the line um where it was him or nobody, you know, didn't want to put it in dangerous way, but um Nick made a great play. Um and you know, hats off to the O line for for keeping me safe. >> So, Baron, two two weeks of games for you in the NFL, your first two, and you're put in two similar situations at the end of a game. Uh what is it about those situations at your position um that I guess you love that challenges you um in those situ? Yeah, I mean I think playing quarterback, you know, especially playing in the NFL. Um, you know, you dream of this moment of leading your team down to have a game-winning drive and, um, you know, it goes back to all the hard work that we've put in through the spring when we got here and summer. Um, and then obviously training camp and, you know, to go out there and do it. Um, you know, being well prepared from coach McDaniels. Um, you know, for the offense, you know, that was big for us tonight. Um, but, you know, there's a lot to correct from today, um, that we can get a lot better from. And so maybe we don't put our situation um where we need a game-winning drive and we don't have to be in that position. >> Baron, how would you describe the relationship that you have with the rest of the rookie class? Do you find that you guys are pushing and motivating each other, especially when you're getting so many opportunities in these preseason games? >> Yeah, for sure. Um you know, it's a it's a really cool group. Um you know, we we've had a lot of fun um you know, just hanging out at the hotel. Um understanding the playbook together. Um, so, you know, it's been a lot of fun. I've made a lot of really, really good friends that, you know, I'll have lifetime relationships with. Um, but, you know, really special class. Um, you know, I'm really proud of the way that, you know, the guys, you know, we don't get a lot of reps during practice. Um, and so when we come out here, you know, you're getting 30, 40, 50 reps a game. And so, um, you know, paying attention, um, you know, and being prepared when your moment comes. Baron, I'm wondering, did you have any conversations with Bryce uh during the game as you were punting? And then also, what kind of feedback did you get from Jeremy? >> Yeah. No, I did. Um because in high school they didn't rush that fast. Um and so the first rush kind of threw me by surprise and so I was like, well, I need to have steps. So I asked Bryce at halftime. I hit a few punts at halftime. Um he was great, tremendous guy. Um helped me out when I needed it. Um, Coach Springer was, you know, singing the praises of doing a good job. Um, but, you know, when, you know, the opportunity comes, you know, just trying to make the most of it. >> You you said earlier you hadn't punted since high school. Is that in a game or at all? Like, is this something you've worked on at any point in the last few years? >> No, it's it really isn't. Um, I I I did in high school and I loved it. Loved to punt and kick. Um, went to college, uh, was always the backup in case anything ever happened. uh but never hit any in practice um for my five years at tech. Um and then I for my pro day I actually punted and kicked in my proday just to showcase that I could do that and so that's obviously why they had an idea that I could do it and then um tonight um you know the opportunity came and you know try to make the most of it. >> How did you feel like you went punting at your proday? >> Um punting at the proday was pretty good. Um tonight I didn't hit some good punts. Um so I got to be better. >> Thanks guys. How's everybody doing? >> Good. How are you? >> Good. >> Nick, uh just kind of take us through that play, the the touchdown. What What did it mean to you and how cool a moment was that? >> Yeah, it was awesome. But first of all, for uh just praying for Jaquindon, um the player who got hurt that first kickoff return. You know, we all praying for him on the sideline, thoughts and prayers. I hear he's okay, which is great. That's not how you want to start a game nor happen in a game at all. So, I'm really glad he's okay. Glory to God for that. But as far as that moment, um, I thank Baron for slinging the rock that well. So, he commanded the huddle in that two-minute. We had some adversity and he did a great job and I was just a guy on the receiving end. It was it was an awesome experience. >> Nick, um, how would you describe your experience just from being here with the Patriots signing undrafted and standing up here at the podium after a preseason game scoring a a game, you know, game-winning touchdown? >> It's pretty cool. I mean, being up here in New England is it's it's kind of funny that, you know, we you know, ever since I was a kid, they were like, you know, at the very least, he's going to get a shot with the Patriots for obvious reasons. But, uh, but it's been really cool. The culture here is is just unbelievable. As somebody who doesn't know any other organization, coming from college, it's something that's totally different and it makes you want to work hard and makes you want to be better every day in the little things. And I'm not just saying that to, you know, as a PR answer. I really mean it with Coach Braves Elliott all the way from the top down. It's it's a it's a really good culture and it's something that's super challenging and it's super deep but you know it's something that has made me better as you know a player and a man and you know it's been great. Nick, is it a strange situation for for you when you're obviously you want to win the game and so you're you're ahead and then they they score, which is in theory something would be disappointing, but for you a guy who's looking for every opportunity to prove yourself and and prove what you can do and and expand your opportunities to be in the league. Is that opp when they score, do you think, all right, well maybe I've got another opportunity to catch a ball, catch or do something and improve your chances and show what you can do. Well, I guess you Yeah, I guess you could say that, but also just, you know, with the flow of the game, if they score, that's another opportunity for us to go respond. So, I know it's a preseason game and people, you know, it's perceived to be nothing that really matters, but it matters to coach Bradel at halftime. It matters to him. It matters that, you know, we come out and we respond and we make plays. And as far as individually, if I'm a part of that and if they trust me to be on the field, that's a great thing, you know, and you know, I I'd love to get another opportunity to go get blown up on another kick return if that means I'm going to be out there for another drive and help win the game. So, you know, yeah, I mean, it we take it serious and every other opport every every opportunity is a good opportunity. >> Nick, I'm curious. You mentioned, you know, growing up New England and just the memories as a young football fan of of the Patriots and what stood out for you. >> I don't know if we misinterpreted that. I grew up in Jersey, >> right? Okay. >> But everybody would say that at least I'm going to get opportunity with the Patriots when I was a young kid with that dynasty growing up. But, you know, it's similar. I mean, even to your point, I mean, the Northeast, it's just, you know, it's like the same corporation, different division. Just I'm four hours down the road. The people are very similar. So, to be able to come up here, you know, the the the type of person is that I, you know, run into up here is very similar to where I'm from. And so, you know, the grit, you know, the old school kind of immigrant mentality, much like my family, you know, it's really cool to be up in a culture like this and to be up in New England with a dynasty like this with guys who are pretty blue collars. It's been great. It's been awesome. >> And I'm curious too about the reps you get in practice because Baron touched on this. You guys don't get a lot of reps >> in practice often. It's a very deep room. >> Uh, how have you felt in terms of like making the most of those opportunities and then carrying them over >> to the game? What's what's the mindset of of a player in that situation when you know like every rep is magnified because they're fewer and far between for you? >> You know, it feels really good when you have a good rep and it feels really bad when you don't have a good rep. And that's kind of what it is as a competitor, as somebody in a room like this as a rookie who, you know, I'm an undrafted guy. Doesn't really mean I don't really mean anything to the room yet. So, like I said, you know, with limited opportunities, when it's good, it's good. And when it's bad, you know, you lose sleep at night sometimes. And so, but that's everybody. I would say even if you had 100 reps, the nature of a competitor is that that one rep you don't have, you want back and you overlook all the good ones. And so for me as somebody who's just trying to maximize my opportunities, I think I've done a decent job, but also there's there's plenty to correct and there's, you know, an amazing support system with these coaches that are real. They're open and vulnerable and they tell you the truth and that helps you get better. So just trying to maximize what I can as long as I'm here. >> Last question, Dan Roach. Nick, along those lines, how much uh having been around this the Patriots and Mike Vreyel, the coaches and the wide receivers, how much is your thirst for that NFL dream even more now? So, after getting a taste of what you've gotten, >> it's just a I mean, overall as far as that NFL dream and you know, everybody's got to do a job and work hard at it. And this is just the job I want to do and work hard at as long as I can. And I know it's a really tough thing to do. And you know, it's not my will, it's the Lord's will, of course. I can't control so many things, let alone control what I can control as a wide receiver, whether it's getting the ball or certain routes he runs. So everything, a lot of this is up to, you know, powers that aren't myself. And so for me, all I can do is keep a level head and stay humble and just work hard and whatever whatever opportunity I have, try to maximize and let the chips fall where they may. >> Thank you so much, guys. >> Dan Ro from the back. >> Real real quick, uh, just want to give my thoughts and prayers out to uh, Mr. Jackson and his family and everything they're going through. Um, you know, it's very tough situation. You know, I hope uh I hope everything is going good for them and you know they're in good spirits and they know that the Lord's looking over them. >> You talk you just heard Nick talking about what he went through and his experience and everything else. How much has this been, I guess, fun for you, but also just you keep grinding and keep trying to get better and better. What's the competition been like and how has it made you better as a player and a person? >> Yeah, it's been awesome. I think anytime there's competition, you know, uh as a competitor, you you you rise up and you uh you take that challenge on. You just go out there and compete every day. And you know, the room we have, it's so special. It's so awesome to be a part of. Um walking into the building every day, having, you know, the group we have and being able to lean on each other and competing against each other and call each other out and always just like looking to try to get 1% better as a room. It's been it's been awesome. Been so very thankful and blessed for all those guys, you know, to to continue to help me. And you know, now I feel like I get the opportunity to kind of help those guys where I was less than a year ago, you know, in the in the in in the same spot. So, [cough] >> Mike Reese in the back. >> Eft your second year, you know, with the team. C. Can you share what areas you feel like you've been able to to build off of and maybe grow as a player? Yeah, I think uh I I mentioned this uh probably a couple days ago, like I'm out there just playing football now instead of uh running lines on pages and, you know, trying to make sure everything's perfect. you know, obviously still focusing on those details and uh and technique and fundamentals, but going out there and just playing ball and having fun and just, you know, adding my own flavor and spice to it as, uh, you know, as I get so much more comfortable with the with the playbook and, you know, the NFL and just being able to go throughout the weeks and know what's going to happen instead of like kind of asking the older guys and trying to figure out what's the best routine. You know, now I I feel like I I have a good routine. I have good role models and, you know, just kind of building off of that. on your far right >> what's most valuable for you uh these taking these preseason reps >> shoot the reps I think you know um you don't get any you know I try not to take any rep for granted um you only get so many you don't know how many you're going to get um even if it's in practice or or in a game just trying to go out there and leave everything out there I have every play you know no matter what if I'm dog tired 16 play drive it doesn't matter I'm going to try to go 100% no matter what and you know just leave it all out there Eftton, building off that, what emphasis or importance do you put on this coming week just given how crowded the wide receiver room is and the roster cut deadline coming up? >> Yeah, I mean, I think just because it's the last week, it it shouldn't change your mindset and the way you work. So, I'm just going to continue to attack it and continue to give everything I have no matter what uh what the circumstances are. If it's uh since it's last week, everyone knows it's going to be a big week, but shoot like like I said, it shouldn't change your mindset in the way you attack your work. Eftton Kyle with another touchdown. Just how have you seen him been been able to just sort of attack these these games the last two weeks? >> Yeah, you know, he's a baller. Um he's got a everyone knows that he's got a great release package and he's going to take the top off and go score, but he's been doing just great things throughout the week working on uh not just the go balls and, you know, getting better as a player. So, it's been awesome to kind of grow with him and lean on each other, you know, coming in the same year and kind of being familiar with the same spots with with Washington and Washington State. And um I it's been cool to see him grow as a player for sure. >> Last question. >> Have you been able to take anything from those release packages that he has? >> Yeah, I mean definitely I'm trying to trying to add it in there. He's got uh a cool you little unique flavor he has to his own. So trying to you know anytime you get to see someone um elevate and make plays I think as a you know as a player you're always trying to add some some new stuff to your bag as well. >> Thank you very much. >> Thank you. Appreciate you guys. Um, I would say it's just a higher level of football and I just am still adapting to it. So, um, it's it's just super fun. I'm just trying to take it day by day. >> We talked to Tony Du about you and he reminded us on several occasions. It's like Lane's kind of a rookie right now because he hasn't gone through the the whole season because of what happened last year. Do you feel like a rookie? >> Uh, yes and no. Um, in terms of experience, definitely not. I mean, I'm still learning and seeing new things every single day. So, um, again, just taking it day by day. >> How does it feel when you I don't know, maybe you'll hear it a little bit later, but when you hear that your coach is talking about you as this gritty player that he singled out when we asked about the depth in the running back room. >> Um, just got to keep going, you know. Uh, not it wasn't all just me, it was the line as well. And, uh, it seemed like we competed really well tonight. And, uh, it was fun. It was a good time. >> A couple more. What did you think about Baron? He's punting. He gets sad. He's still on the field. He has to punt. He's throwing. >> Yeah. I didn't even know he was back there, but they were like, uh, I turned around and, uh, Julian was like, Baron just kicked it through the end zone. I think I thought that was pretty cool. And I was like, have you punted before? He's like, not since high school. So, it's pretty cool. >> Thank you. >> Thanks, man. Thank you, guys. What were you doing before you? >> Man, I was working out with my trainer in uh in Nashville and uh we pretty much going every day and I was just waiting on the call, you know, and uh thank God, you know, they called me up and uh now I'm here. >> How do you feel like you can, you know, contribute to this team this season if given opportunity? >> Uh like I said, whatever the coaches need me to do, I'm going to do it. Special team, win the ball, block, whatever. Uh I'm going to give it my all. and uh you know just do whatever it takes to win. >> Awesome. Thanks. >> Thanks. >> Hey Gabe, how how would you describe some of the things that you're working on um in these games um to help take your game to another level? >> Yeah, just the little things. Um first of all, just alignment first off. um hand placement um you know looking at backfield sets you know all the little things that you know not only my coach um but also raves that he also talks about. So, um, those things like that I can work on and, um, I continue to work on. >> Gabe, what was was anything said to you after the roughing the passer? >> Like >> coaching staff, anybody saying anything? >> No. Well, they're just saying like that's just how the league is like, you know, um, any second that he throws the ball, you get him. You know, they're most likely to call that. So, a learning lesson for me, but um, you know, then again, just got to be careful, you know, after he throws the ball. So, >> you were on block two plays later and you went right after him. Is that sort of just like the learning process? Like were you trying to be a little careful there? >> Yeah, just being a little careful when you come on block, you know, um the free runner, you just got to be precautious when he throws the ball and um you know, just got to capitalize. >> Gabe, I know it's um other side of the ball, but Baron Morton, what was it like kind of seeing him come out for the punts? What was the team's reaction in that moment of just, you know, not seeing Bryce and seeing your quarterback go out instead? >> Yeah, I was crazy. I mean, when I heard our punters, you know, went down and Bryce um I mean, Baron went out there. I was like, quarterback. I was like, well, I mean, let's see how well this kid does. But I didn't even see his punt, but I mean, I'm sure he punted it pretty good. Um, but, you know, Baron's a good guy and someone that, you know, is a good teammate. Um, you know, it's just, you know, just a reliable guy. Just someone that go out there and punt the ball. So, you know, he can count on him just to, you know, do do whatever it takes for the team.
