And uh it seems like we're doing that at this time. >> Got it. Thank you. Art Stapleton. >> Hey, John. How are you? >> Hey, Art. Uh, wanted to ask you the one one guy that stood out for me yesterday and then you look at the stat book and you see he played every snap was JC Davis. And I'm curious from your perspective, from my perspective and my my [clears throat] career, it's not often that you see a sixth round rookie offensive lineman take to a game and then also play the entire game in that heat and humidity down there. Uh, and really nothing that jumped off from what I saw that said he didn't do a good job. Your thoughts on JC and what he's been able to do and how difficult that is for maybe a young lineman to to take that kind of assignment yesterday. >> Right. I agree with what you said. You know, it's it's a challenging thing. It doesn't happen too often. Guys aren't asked to do that very often. And he did it and it was it was a goal we got, you know, going into the week. We decided to see if, you know, to put him in that situation to see how he handled it and also, you know, to help him again grow into the ability to do it, you know, can can you play a whole game at left tackle in the National Football League preseason game, albeit, but still a game. And uh he did it. He did it well. He he had a lot of plus plays. He graded out very well, you know, and uh that's a big step in his development for sure. I mean, also in us gaining confidence in his ability to go in there and do good things in a game. how when you're talking young offensive linemen in general, I mean, we've seen it. You know, Andrew Thomas took his lumps as as a rookie and, you know, it took him a while to kind of get going and regain that momentum. How hard is it to maintain patience and how easy is it for young linemen to kind of when once they go one way and the pendulum swings to kind of get it back technique-wise playing in that situation? And it just seems like that's certainly a position that that really brings a lot of different challenges uh to to young players especially. >> No, I think you're right, Art. I mean, it's it's a tough position to play and you know, a guy like at would have had first round expectations and all that and and that's that's that's another layer to that whole thing you're talking about, right? And JC doesn't have that. he doesn't have that layer to it that that AT had, but um he's going to be expected to play a role on the team and uh it's going to be a very important role, you know, so and he could be in there, you know, so uh at any time really. So, he's got to be ready for that. And uh hopefully, you know, you're right, you like to get off to a good start, but man, the bullets start flying in in in an NFL game with the type of players you're playing against, the speed that that he thinks hit you with, and they certainly test you as a rookie. they they find out how fast you can think and adjust and and uh you know make changes on the move and uh so that's the things that I think you have to deal with. Obviously once you've seen those things you're better at it. So and things happen so fast for the offensive line probably more so than any other position. So probably all those things go into exactly what you're you're saying and what you're observing. >> Thanks John. Appreciate it. >> We'll take four more. Ryan Dunlevy. >> Hey John, how are you? >> Hey, I'm good. How you doing? >> Good. Uh, I don't think you've been asked what went into moving Audu from tackle to guard because that's something that's been obviously you weren't here, but that's something that's been a longstanding debate on what his best position is. Uh, what went into moving him back to guard, >> right? Uh well, he's uh he's the position flex is the move is the idea. So, and you may have noticed he went back out to tackle in the fourth quarter, you know, so uh the ability for him to play uh both guard and tackle particularly on the right side would be helpful for us. And that's our thought, you know, he's kind of getting to the point now where we feel like he could he could swing right tackle, right guard. Right now, we're kind of keeping him off the left side and just keep it to the right side. And that helps a little bit with some of the techniques. you know, it's like a hitter, you know, he's not a switch hitter right now on both sides, but he is playing both the inside position and the outside position. So, we think he's ready for it that he can handle it, you know, and that gives us some position flexibility as a backup >> and then flipping sides of the ball. What are you seeing right now from your put Hood aside from your top three outside corners? Because there's position battles where no one steps up and there's position battles where it seems like multiple guys have stepped up and I don't want to put the cart before the horse, but if you look at Banks's play, Adbo's play maybe the last week after a slow start and Newsome steadiness, it almost seems like they've all stepped up. >> Yeah, Ryan, I agree with that. You know, I think they're all making it a really good problem for the Giants. And uh and I would put I would put Colton in the same category. He'll be back this week practicing. So, that's uh that's a that's a good situation to have. And, you know, even we got Cory Black back there. Our Green has played well. Those guys have done a good job. Our Nicholls have played really well. Drew, you know, he he had the they gave up the one uh wheel route there. Uh tight coverage, but but the guy, they made a nice play and and and uh came back and caused turnover, knocked two balls out during the game, and then Nick continues to play well when he goes in. So, I just feel like all those guys are doing a good job. It seems like we're deep at corner, you know, certainly, you know, plan on that panning out throughout the course of the season. And I'm sure all those guys are going to play a lot of football for us, you know, and play very well. >> Thank you. >> Howdy, Trina. >> Hi, John. How are you? >> I'm good, thanks. >> Big picture question if I could. For a lot of these guys, this is going to be your last week with them, and I'm just wondering what's your message to them as they get ready for this final uh preseason week of preseason before roster cut down dates and especially those guys who maybe are borderline bubble guys, >> right? Well, one thing that's a great great question and such a such a human aspect of this whole thing and the relationships and and uh you know we we tell them you know you your your best dream is not too big. Matter of fact, it might not even be big enough, you know, and and and you have the right to to go ahead and and feel free to to hope for all the things that that inside that you might not even want to tell anybody because because for fear that someone might but if they're not laughing at your dream, then it's not big enough either, you know. So, say it, speak it, and go for it, you know. And and these guys have really done that. I feel like they've really put that out there and they they've talked to each other. They've they've uh committed to helping one another achieve each other's dreams. Those kind of things we talk about, you know, in our meetings and I know they they talk about amongst themselves as a group of guys and uh so, you know, you're pulling for everybody and everybody's pulling for everybody. Everybody wants you see it on the sideline. You see it between guys who are competing for the same position. They're rooting for each other and helping each other along. I mean, you see so many of the best things about human nature come out on a football team, you know, believe it or not. And maybe people that aren't a part of the sport would would have a tough time believing that, but I think those of us who've been around the sport understand that that is how it works, you know, and it's a cool thing. So this week, to your point, is a very challenging week because there will be guys that won't be here after this week. You know, maybe they'll come back, you know, we, you know, we brought Ben back, you know, the defensive lineman from who just got released by the Jets and came back to us again here this week. And and so, you know, I I told him, I said, "Hey, we had this conversation, man." And I I I I told you he'd be back here. Uh and I don't know why I thought he would, but but he is, you know, so maybe maybe you go back to what Wellington Mar famously said, you know, once a giant, always a giant. And I think that that holds true as well. So you become part of the part of the part of the team, part of the organization, part of the the fabric of what it means to be a Giant. And uh and I do think that those guys, you know, they treasure it. I know I'm getting a little long-winded, but how many of us, you know, that played football wouldn't wouldn't have loved to have had an opportunity to be in a football camp in the national football like to be invited to get a try out even, you know, all the all all the not so good players like me, you know, would have would have loved that. And I tell these guys, you are you are the very best. Every single player here in this room is a great football player. There is not one football player in an NFL camp who's not a great football player. You talk about the one the top 0.00001% of of of football players, even athletes in the world that that are going to be in a football camp. So, but then there's levels to that too, just like there's levels to anything else. So, within that, striving to be the best you can be. But I would say everybody, every one of our guys, uh, whether they, you know, they're here the next week or they're not, will look back and say they did their very best. They put their best foot forward, and it's something that they can look back on really for the rest of their life, uh, proudly. >> Thank you so much, Ed Valentine. >> Hey, coach. Um, >> hey, Ed. as you look forward, you know, to the uh to the beginning of the season, you know, you're kind of turning your attention to to that at this point. Um, but, you know, you have a lot of guys, a lot of veteran guys who didn't play Saturday. Um, that's a long time from like week one to the beginning of the season, you know, for guys to go without competition. Do you factor that into into how you approach, you know, this week and and the rest of uh the rest of your preparation, you know, for the season opener? >> Uh most definitely, you know, most definitely. You have to you have to factor that in and consider that, you know, uh playing together in a game, communicating together in a game, those things are valuable things that it's better to have some experience with before you get into the, you know, the game that counts. So, so to speak. So yeah, that's part of it. Even the way we practice, you know, what we work on, how we set up our practices. We set up our practices for the week this afternoon, uh, and what we needed to work on. Uh, that's definitely a a big part of that that mindset in terms of, you know, how we how we organize the plays and what we work on. So big big yes big yes to what you asked. So, the only other thing I had for you is just some thoughts on where Darius Alexander is at this point in terms of, you know, his readiness. >> Uh, well, yeah. I mean, he's mentally prepared and ready to go. Uh, he's working very hard and he's working on his game just like all the guys are. You know, there's things he does exceptionally well and there's things that, you know, aren't his strengths, so to speak, but, you know, he's still one of the still, you know, very highly talented guy, high draft pick guy. and we'll see where uh you know how much progress he continues to make, but I think he's come a long way in training camp. Uh he knows what he's you know what he's working on across the board. He knows where he wants to make the most improvement. Uh I I see improvement and I see a lot of really good things that he's already good at, too. >> Last one. Jordan Renan. >> Hey, John. Real quick, I assume you go back to the alternating days of pads this week. And does Malik shed the red jersey? Possibly. We'll have to see. That's that's a possibility. Um yes, we'll just have to see where that's at. I don't think it's a necessity this week. We're still three weeks out from the game, the first game and then after that. But um we'll see where he's at this week. We're uh we uh see how he feels tomorrow. >> And you are doing alternating days with the with pads this week. Is that the plan again? Something like that. >> Something like that. Yeah. You you have a you have an obsession with like alternating days with pads and and the pads plan, don't you? >> Well, I mean, we're just uh trying to figure out like for coverage purposes like where we stand on like what we should expect from the practices. >> Oh, okay. Yeah. >> If you're running like a walkthrough practice, it kind of, >> you know, maybe changes the way we approach that that day. >> Well, we won't I'll tell you this. We'll have a walk more of a walkthrough practice on Saturday on a Thursday. I mean, on Thursday be more of a walkthrough practice. The other practices will be, you know, good tempo, but uh they won't all be padded at [music]

title: Postgame Interviews: John Harbaugh, Jameis Winston, Odell Beckham Jr. | New York Giants
text: You look at this almost like a two-parter, Thursday and then Saturday and then you wanted to get something out of the both things together. >> We did. We did. It was just an opportunity to get two really You know, I tell coach Halfley does a great job. And I I love what they're building. I respect what they're building. We played against him in Green Bay numerous times, two or three times when he was a defensive coordinator. Their defense is is playing really hard and tough and they didn't play their starters or anything like that. They're a young team. They're going to be playing, I think, 11 or 12 rookies are going to be starting for them, you know. So, what he's building here is is is the right right the right right way. So, to come down here and the way they competed and everything was really good for us. So, we wanted to you know, after we thought we did well in the practice, we wanted to make sure we followed up by doing well in the game. That was That was the goal and our guys did a good job of that. >> What do you think of your offense in the game? >> I thought they did well. You know, the protection was good. We ran the ball well. All that was good. >> The physicality in this game was evident that you were out physically that football team. That was one of your goals. >> Well, I mean, we just we our guys our guys our younger guys are we played our backups, you know. Uh so to speak. But, there's a lot of guys fighting for jobs on this team and I thought they came out and they they they made a point to try to make their case and they did a good job of it. >> Go ahead. You know, some teams don't have a backup like Jameis, you know, and you know what he is really and he's kind of sort of a backup. He's a veteran. But, so do you expect him to play well in this situation like that? >> Absolutely. Jameis, you expect Jameis to play just like that. You know, Jameis was in control. He He ran the show. He He made you know, he's poised in the pocket. He was very accurate with his passing. He just you know, he played at a high level just like you'd expect him to. I mean, that's the great That's a great a great thing to have a have a quarterback like that as your number two. I mean, Jameis has been a starting quarterback in this league for a long time. He's started a lot of games, so it's big big uh I thought he'd play exactly the way you expect him to to your point, Paul. Yeah. >> Dennis' contributions tonight, what do you say? >> Oh, yeah, he did great. I mean, he's he played like he always plays, you know. One of the most consistent players you're you're ever going to see. >> Coach, what can you tell to those fans who are waiting for week one? >> What's that? >> What can you tell to those fans who are waiting for week one of this new NFL season? >> What I'm waiting for week one? >> Yes, they might win the Super Bowl this year. >> Oh, yeah, well, you know, we we kind of look at it like we have a lot of work to do between now and then, you know, so uh that's that's 3 weeks away. And um we will probably start looking at our first few games in terms of our preparation because those are the games that count, but we still have uh there's still roster battles, you know, and all that, so we're going to try to take it one day at a time, try to be a better team. We'll be up back Monday, try to be a better team, you know, after practice Monday than we were when we started. I just try to keep it simple like that and see if we can get to that first week of the season as good as we can as a football team. >> So, James had an 11-yard touchdown run to really set the tone of this game. Shows those wheels still work, huh? >> Yeah. Uh I think um our offensive line just did a good job of setting a tone by establishing the run game. Uh and I sometimes get to show the the young school cats that I still can, you know, be an athlete and get out the pocket. >> Was it fun to to really run the offense today? >> It it was. Um anytime you get to the play for that extended period of time, you get to develop a rhythm. Uh Coach Nagy uh was on a roll and like I said, when you run the football, uh it makes it very uh it caters to the entire offense. >> Uh you and Odell almost hooked up in the end zone. You said it was a great throw, he's got to go get up go get that. But like in general, how did Odell look >> He's looking good every single day. Um we we all want to make that play. Um but we we we're going to make that play. That's what he does. That's what I do. I can't wait to get back to practice and rep that and just get more reps. >> What does it say about the quality of this team, the urgency that everyone showed, even if it wasn't all the first teamers that were out there? >> Yeah, I think it's the leadership leadership around like we understand the responsibility that we have and I think that's the most beautiful thing about training camp and preseason football is everyone knows that hey, time is almost up. So, being present and being willing to do whatever is required to be your best is going to give you your best your best chance to make the team. >> Do you appreciate the coach the way that he doesn't look at incumbents? He looks at the challenges and the battles at every position and he's got even the veterans really working really hard to make a spot. >> Well, I'm I'm just grateful for Coach Harbaugh's leadership. He holds everybody to a to a standard just like he holds himself. We see him grinding and working and studying hours and hours of tape and communicating with the quarterbacks, communicating with the offensive line, communicating with the defensive line, communicating with the DBs. He has his hand in a relationship with every position group and I think that that speaks volumes because he's holding everybody to that standard, coaches coaches included. >> The word is accountable, isn't it? >> Uh well, he he I think it's intentional. He's obsessed with football. He lives, sleeps, and breathes it and he invites us to participate with being obsessed and being in love and sleeping and breathing it and you can see about the challenging training camps that we have and how close that we're coming together as a football team. >> Is this a better team than the team that came to Florida that's going home? >> Uh well, yes. Every single day we're looking to be a a better team and I would say every practice, every rep we're striving to be better. One of one of my favorite quotes is we're in a race to get better. Coach Uh, uh, Roman said that earlier season, Sean Payton said that a lot. We are in a race to get better. >> How did it feel today being out there? >> Uh, felt great. It felt like old times. It's just, um, certain play that's going to stick with me the same way it always has all my life. When you want to be great, um, and you know, opportunities come your way. You got to make the most of them. Today, I feel like I let myself down, let my team down. And, um, those are plays that I'll make. And, uh, just can't wait for the next opportunity for that. >> Yeah, the end zone you almost had it. Was there anything with the new gloves at all or >> No, no, no. Just trying to look up, make sure my feet get down. Just a play that I'll make 10 times out of 10, and today it wasn't it. um, that's what makes you great though. You you come back from that. You take it on the chin like a man. You eat it. You watch the film. And you go on. You build your confidence. I'm good, you know. >> Do you see the old Odell back on the field? You had some really good moves out there and what >> Yeah. I mean, it's never I'm never going to be 23-year-old me, but I'm very comfortable and confident in this, um, version of myself. Um, you know, just a play that I wanted to make and didn't make that I usually do. Um, and next time the opportunity's there, I'll make it. >> Were you having fun out there? >> I was having fun. >> That's the best part. >> It was fun. Um, the national anthem, she got me. Had a couple tears fall, so that's when I knew I was finally back in that moment. >> That's awesome. Thank you. >> What's up, brother? Oh. Good? >> I'll take it now. >> You want to give one real quick? Questions real quick? Okay. >> Look at it. Keep doing it. Um, coach just said that you you can look at that as a negative that you didn't make the play. >> Mhm. >> He said, "I'm going to look at it as a positive that >> you look at it and leap and, you know, leap and it was there." What do you I mean, you look very frustrated though. >> Um, I'm pissed. This is the one that keeps me up at night. It's a play that I know I can make. Um, just felt like I was hanging so long. didn't want to see you get your feet down. You take it on the chin like a man. Confidence is still there and I know that I'll make that play next time. It reminds me of the time we were playing at LSU and it was against Auburn it was in the rain ball down the right side. I said next time it's mine. I dropped it then the catch happened. You know what I mean and it's like now you go work overtime. You turn up even more. You know you you you keep going. You don't shy away from Excuse me. But like that that's what motivates me to be even better to come back to work harder to know that I need to put another step forward um and bring my best. Oh yeah. I take that I don't care if it was high or low or wherever it was at like it's on me. Like I feel like if the ball's anywhere near me if it touches my fingertips I'm supposed to catch it. So that's on nobody but me.

title: Bobby Skinner on NBC Sports Final
text: Watch out for the Giants' preseason hype train rolled into the station in Miami this week. Preseason, that's the time of year when looking good gets confused sometimes for looking great. That said, brakes appropriately pumped, cold water officially doused, I think we can all allow ourselves to get kind of excited about what the Giants are showing so far this summer. But don't take it from me. Bobby Skinner is here, back from taking the Giants Nation Show on the road down to South Florida. He's been in West Virginia. Where the Giants go, Bobby Skinner goes, and it's great to have him here at 30 Rock. Thanks for being here. >> Thanks for having me. >> Uh so, what did you see in Florida that stood out to you from what you saw in West Virginia? What do you like about the Giants? >> Well, you talked about preseason and over-hyping it, and we went in and it's like, you know what? The Miami Dolphins are a bad team, right? We were looking for matchups, and it's like, man, this is this is kind of a rough roster. So, we went in like, you know what? The Giants can't just have a decent practice. They should have a good joint practice. And instead of that, they were dominant on both sides of the football. Where the offense, that was the best day that I had seen them in all of training camp. The defense, the pass rush had been good. It was dominant, where the Dolphins couldn't operate on offense. So, the Giants have been one of the bad teams in the NFL. For them to get good, they have to show that they can be a level above those other bad teams. >> And that's what you saw. Did it surprise you to see that? >> Uh somewhat, because the Giants offense didn't look great against uh the Giants defense in West Virginia. And that's always the training camp conundrum. It's if someone's doing good, someone's doing bad. >> That is true. >> And there's not a lot of, you know, faith in the Giants secondary. So, for the offense, it's building something new with Matt Nagy, the offensive coordinator, Greg Roman following John Harbaugh. Uh and then Jackson Dart being year two in a brand new offense, where he's doing things he's never done before. So, to go out there and just look their best against another team, I thought was encouraging for them. >> So much of this Giants season and the hope that fans seem to have with this team is predicated on getting it right at quarterback. Does it feel so far like they've got it right with Jackson Dart as he enters year two, but really his first camp as the starting quarterback? >> They've at least given themselves something to buy into, right? You know, a lot of times these year two quarterbacks, teams sell themselves on hope. Well, he gave them 24 touchdowns in 12 games last year. And I think there will be some growing pains in the new offense, like I mentioned the practices. But with the offensive line being actually a strength for the Giants, and then Jackson Dart's ability to make plays when things aren't there, I think they've built themselves a floor, at least a decent offense. You even saw in that preseason game when Dart did play last week against the Vikings where the offense didn't look great, but he comes back into the game, scrambles to the left and finds Malachi Fields his new rookie weapon for a touchdown. And I think those are the things you'll see Dart do as he learns the other parts of the offense. >> depth chart is fascinating to me. Fields is one especially. I mean, when they got him in the draft, I thought, okay, maybe they've really got something here, a potential potential big-time player. Um Malik Nabers, big news today is that John Harbaugh says he could possibly shed that red jersey, that non-contact jersey, as soon as this week, which is remarkable to consider that this guy is not even a year removed from torn ACL surgery, and then a second surgery, and here we are. What do you see from Malik Nabers that maybe kind of leaves you shaking your head like, I can't believe this guy's doing this. >> He looks good. I mean, I think he's going to play week one. And And that's like the things we've talked about with the offense looking sloppy. They don't have their easy button. That is Malik Nabers being the, you know, that, "Hey, well, sometimes when it's not right, it's right when you throw the ball to Malik Nabers." So, and you're seeing the video now, like he's moving very well for, you know, being, you know, fresh off of that, you know, that second surgery. Um and you mentioned the receivers. Isaiah Likely, he has set himself up with Malik Nabers not practicing as Jackson Dart's top target. And you'd say, "Hey, they're big free agent, he should do that." That's almost been a curse for the Giants. Their biggest free agent being, you know, being one of the >> long long list of of failures. >> being an issue for them. So, Isaiah Likely making himself as the number one target when Nabers isn't there. So, now that number two target, and then that doesn't put the pressure on a guy like Malachi Fields to to a number two right away, where he can be, you know, the big contested catch guy and grow as a number three. >> Odell Beckham Jr. is one that everyone obviously looks for. Uh it it would be a great story if OBJ could make this roster and his return to the Giants. I Do you feel like he's at least on the bubble, on the fringe, or do you think this is a long shot? >> I think this is becoming a long shot because when they signed him, the Giants actually brought in wide receiver depth compared to last year where they didn't have that. And you thought I would The things things [music] played themselves out even if that was Odell playing himself out. Nobody's been injured in that wide receiver room. Malik Neighbors, we just mentioned, we expect him to be ready week one. >> [music] >> And there's clearly five guys above of him on the depth chart. And then you add Braxton Berrios with his specials. I'm not sure. And that touchdown that you saw him drop, if he catches that, I feel like that becomes a lot of fan pressure. Like you're going to cut this guy after he goes and makes a play like that. And you can see he can still do stuff, but is it going to be enough to make the roster? I think the numbers are are working against him right now. >> All right, it's a stacked backfield as well with with not a lot of room for errors I think. Tyron Tracy Jr. is is unfortunately on the cusp of finding out. Cam Cam Skylar is still the number one. I mean, he's your guy, right? But there's a lot of a power running potential with this backfield that you see with the Giants. >> Well, absolutely. And the Giants uh you know, they've shown proof that they might like this running back room. They don't love it. You know, they were willing to draft Jeremiah Love if he was available. They went after Kenneth Walker in free agency. And then they brought in Najee Harris who I don't think we're expecting the world for him to light the world on fire, but they didn't bring him in here for anything. And then Tyron Tracy, you know, getting your quarterback hit uh with a blind you know, a blind side hit essentially. Fumbling the ball untouched. Those are things where a new coach is trying to build a culture and a meritocracy. Those are things that are going to put you down the depth chart. >> And John Harbaugh even alluded to that today. He said, "Look, he also did a lot of things well on Saturday in Miami, but those two things in two preseason games are things you absolutely cannot do. So, I don't know if that's some foreshadowing here. And it's tough because everybody loves Tyrone Tracy, but you're right, it's a crowded backfield. And as you see Devin Singletary scoring a touchdown, and I'll tell you when you when you see Singletary running that in, two tight ends and a fullback, that's power running. >> Yeah, and the Giants it feels like they're trying to build a culture almost like a culture of violence. Like, "Hey, we're not just, you know, every coach comes in and to preach this culture." They are bringing in Patrick Ricard, like using not just a fullback, but the fullback in the NFL. Using the two tight ends. They want to bring that that run game. And I think part of the offensive struggles passing games in West Virginia was the fact that they were running the ball a lot. They were in fully padded practices running a lot, you know, like they had full pads I think 13 12 out of 14 practices. They had their body armor. Yeah. And I think last year it took them almost, you know, like twice the time for them to run the same amount of padded practices they have now. So, they're looking to build that, and that's where I say I think the offense does have a floor even if Jackson Dart in the passing game may take some time to gel. >> All right, on the defensive side of the ball, you mentioned the pass rush standing out in Miami. So, what to you do you think the identity of this Giants defense looks like a couple preseason games in? >> It has to be the pass rush. Those trio of edge rushers of Brian Burns coming off of a 16-sack season. Abdul Carter who is my favorite guy to watch on that defense. I think the numbers are going to come for him this year. >> Why is that? >> You know, he was I think seventh in the NFL in total sacks, hits, and pressures. title: Todd Bowles: The Defense is Setting The Tone | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Okay, first question will come from Scott Reynolds. >> Hey coach, through training camp and now these two preseason games, what have you discovered about your defense and and what do you like best about it that you've seen so far? >> I think them understanding each other, especially up front, understanding the pass rush games and playing together. It it's kind of young, but but you've you're no stranger to playing young quarterbacks. How do you feel about that position? U you know obviously last night you had uh Tristan was out and Justin and um and uh Ben, but Paul Roel played the whole game. How did he do and and what is the status of those guys this week uh for Jacksonville and can they practice or what are they going to do? >> Uh he played the whole game. I thought he fared well. you know, he had some plays he liked to have back, but at the same time, he fought his butt off and he battled in there. For him starting a full game like that, playing against their ones and twos, I thought he fared well. Uh, we're going to try to start working Tristan back to what some degree in there. The other two, I'm not sure about. >> Thanks, >> Scott Reynolds. If any media have questions, please raise your hand. We got a small sample size last night but we need more practice in certain situations to clean up things. title: Zyon McCollum, Dean Patterson IV & More on Team Chemistry | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: You forced two quick drives, and just your feelings on that. >> Yeah, Bo has talked to us beforehand and he said two three and out and that'll be it. I mean, if we can go get it done. So, we challenged ourselves to go and get those three and out and it ended up working. >> In a preseason where you know your workload isn't going to be that high and you come into this game and you get those two three and out. Just how good does that feel? >> It feels great. I mean, we put pressure on ourselves going into the game, you know. Whether it's a preseason game or a Super Bowl, we want everything to be the same. So, having that intensity, being able to go out there and execute, it's a good feeling and it makes us know that we are in the right spot going into Jacksonville. >> Is there anything that you felt like you guys could do better? I know it's just preseason, but it's the first time you guys took live bullets as a as a unit. >> Yeah, I mean, I'm happy but never satisfied. We're going to have to look at the tape to, you know, get the details down, but we're starting to learn how to win, how to finish games, and so that's a good feeling knowing that we've emphasized that throughout camp and it's coming to fruition. >> Bo's mentioned there's some wrinkles in the secondary that he added this year. How do you guys feel like that's been working so far? >> It's been working incredible. I mean, we're coming together as a group more than anything that I've seen. We're starting to talk, we're starting to communicate more, we're starting to disguise a little bit. And so, us coming together as a unit is, you know, what's going to help our front go. Our front gets to the quarterback, so that's going to help us go. And so, coming together as a team is really what we've been harping on and it's good to see it. >> You saw a couple of the young guys getting involved tonight, too. Keontae Scott's name was mentioned a couple times. Ruben Bain had that pressure. Just how they fit in, especially tonight as well. >> Yeah, they're going to be so much fun to play with. You know, Keontae, he brings so much energy. Bain, he's kind of a silent assassin. And, you know, they just bring a mindset to this team that we've been missing and it's good to have them on our side. You know, they're young guys and they're learning fast, but it's going to be a lot of fun playing with them. >> Thank you for your time. >> Zion's been a great, um, you know, model figure for me. You know, he's an excellent player and, you know, I kind of try to model my game after him. And even Jacob Parish and Ben Morrison, you know, they're all outstanding players and I'm just trying to play to their level, you know what I mean? >> Awesome. Well, thanks so much for the time. Congrats on the win. >> For sure. Thank you. >> And the ball is in your hands. Just what's going on through your mind? >> Um shoot, ball is in the air and I was thinking about getting sticky, you know what I mean? So, got the ball and then supposed to hit the near sideline, but you know, just a kind of a spur of the moment thing and then, you know, just high and tight, keep it so that get the offense in a better position to score. >> Did it feel a little bit like deja vu after getting an interception in last year's preseason? >> A little bit, you know, there was there was some correlations, you know, I hit the sideline trying to take it back, but uh you know, I can't take everyone back, so you know, I just >> What what can you say about this opportunity cuz you came in, you know, recently and you were out there and able to make a play today. >> Yeah, I mean, it was awesome. Um you know, I spent a season in the UFL, you know, learning and you know, I took that experience with me. I learned a lot. Um you know, it really brought me back to earth with the opportunity I had last year and you know, to get another opportunity this year, you know, I I knew I had to make a play and you know, make the most of it. >> Thank you. >> Thank you. Thank you, guys. >> Yeah, I feel good. Feel like Zach. Um he does a good job and uh everything compliments itself pretty well. So, yeah, feel comfortable. >> Took some hits tonight, but what was it like after? >> Uh yeah, I mean, it is what it is. Uh you can take hits and you know, sometimes the soul needs it. >> Did the Did the ref take you off? >> Yeah. Yeah, I just told him I got up looking We literally made eye contact and I was like, "Please don't do that." >> [laughter] >> And then he pulled me out and but I'm fine. Yep. >> Do you feel like this there's definitely a quarterback battle here for the backup job? >> That's not my job to to say whether there is or there isn't. Um you know, I'm I'm a UDFA going into my eighth year. Like, I've been in competition every every single year and you know, whether you think it's a competition or it's not, you're competing with a lot of quarterbacks that aren't even on this team. So, um you know, I I I think that's just kind of comes with the territory and I'm not unfamiliar with competition, but it's also not my job to worry about that stuff. It's just do your job. Um feel like I've had a really good camp. Feel like I some good plays today. Obviously, weren't able to put together a drive to put a touchdown up, but you know, I I I feel confident in the in the body of work I put out so far since getting here and um you know, see to capitalize on through the rest of camp. >> Jake, you sure you you've been in this league long enough. You've seen I mean, I know there's a lot of excitement about a young guy that comes in, but you sort of know how this thing works. You've had a lot of experience. >> Yeah. >> You got to feel comfortable with that, where you are right now. >> Yeah, I mean, I think that there's you got to feel comfortable, but also, you know, not you don't want to get too comfortable and um you know, I I think that's just kind of like how that's just kind of how these things go. It's just like uh like I said, I'm I'm a UDFA, former UDFA, practice squad guy that's going into year eight. Like, I've been in competition and I think anytime you sign up to be an NFL quarterback, like you are in competition, whether you acknowledge it or not. And so, you know, it just kind of comes with the territory. I'm pretty uh familiar with with it and it is what it is. >> Thanks, Jake. >> Yep. >> It would it would truly mean everything, man. You know, I growing up here, obviously, coming all the games, man. It It's I mean, you know, I'm I'm I'm a hometown kid, man. I A lot of people really don't get this opportunity, man. So, I'm going to be able to do everything and and apply everything that I can to be able to capitalize. >> Do you have a memory from under training camp or coming to a game as a kid? >> Oh, yeah. Actually, that was kind of my senior of high school, the Super Bowl year. You know, I was I'm here with with all the festivities in in my Chris Godwin jersey, mind you. You know, I'm I'm I'm in the indoor kicking field goals. You know, it was it was one of like the little little games they had around the city. But yeah, man. And then and then being being in the nosebleeds of that game, cheering, you know, so so happy, man. I love to see Tampa like that. And and and I and I really want to be able to get Tampa jumping and hype, you know, definitely excited for the team. So, yeah. >> Do you feel like you've become a better player since getting to the Bucks? >> Yes, sir. Yeah, B Mac B Mac does a great job developing receivers. He he pushes me every day. Truly couldn't wish for a better coach, honestly. >> Man, I I appreciate you guys. Thank you. >> It's a pleasure.

title: Todd Bowles on Jalon Daniels’ Spark | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Evening. >> Todd, I think your starting defense was out there for six plays and gave up 13 yards. What did you see about it? What you saw from your starting defense? >> Like the energy, like the way they flew around. You know, they they came out and played as one, so that was encouraging. >> Todd, that pressure off the side seemed to stand out early. What were your thoughts on Yaya's performance along with Reuben Bain in your first change to look at him? >> They were getting off the ball, you know, it was exciting to see him get off the ball and happy to see him play. >> Todd, can you talk about the spark you got from Jaylen Daniels? Obviously hadn't really done much offensively and then to score on three straight drives with him leading the way. >> He did a good job closing out the game second week in a row. He made some plays, some clutch plays. Obviously there's a lot of things he's got to learn, but at the same time he goes out there and he makes things happen and he gives us a chance to win. >> What about Cameron Johnson? What did you see from him tonight? Cuz we saw an awful lot of him. >> Made some plays in kickoff return. We wanted to see him at receiver. He made some plays. Obviously I got to look at the film to see everything else, but he definitely was noticeable. >> Could you talk about Patterson's performance as well? He He also tied for the same amount of yards that uh that number 19 did. So, could you talk about his performance? >> I thought he showed up. He did a great job with the act yards after catch. Uh turning short yards short gains short pass plays into some gains right there and he did a very good job. >> Todd, I know you planned on playing starter or backup about 8-15 plays depending on how the game went, but you were down a bunch of tackles in this game. Did it just make sense not to give them that drop back type situations like with those and >> We wanted to emphasize the running game. We we said that going in, so it was part of our plan to try and run the ball going right there, but you know, down a couple tackles, you always you never try to get them hurt that much. At the same time, we tried to have a game plan of running the ball. We started out well. We got the penalty that pushed us back late, but I was happy with the efficiency. >> Todd, you have three tackles down and Trout out as well. Those four are there of those likely to extend all the way to the opener right now? >> Uh we'll see right now. We'll see. Uh Tristen's been working his way back. We'll see about the other ones. >> Todd, was Connor basically scheduled to get any snaps today or was he >> Not today, wasn't no. >> Um speaking of injuries, with the I know a number of your wide receivers were held out. Do you know at this point if any of those receiver injuries would carry on to to possibly week one? >> Not at this time, I don't. >> Todd, going back to Jaylen, there was a sequence where he made a great escape down by the goal line and then get I got everybody lined up for the touchdown real quick. Just talk about his poise in that moment. >> No, for a rookie, he he's a very smart player. He pays attention in the meetings. I mean, he's great in the building. He wants to know everything. He processes processes everything well and you know, that that was an example of it. He he executed it well and he played good ball. >> How about your running back depth? We saw Josh Williams out there before we saw saw Shaun Tucker tonight. What has Josh shown you to to get the earlier look? >> Uh he had a good game last week, you know, he had a good game last week and we wanted to see him against better guys, so we wanted to put him out there early. Didn't mean nothing as far as them flip-flopping, but we wanted to see him earlier. >> Todd, I know you mentioned Yaya Diaby and Ruben Bain, but what can you say about David Walker consistently generating pressure up there? >> I know he had some pretty good rushes. I got to look at the overall part of the game, but I did see two good rushes. >> Could you see him from Milton Kamara who was in practice squad last year? He's shown up made some splash plays the last couple of weeks. >> No, he has a lot of energy. He's just grasping the entire system. You know, he has some very good plays where he's very tough and he plays with all the energy. He's just got to make sure he has a good command of the defense. >> You're going to have some joint practices coming up in the final preseason game. Where do you anticipate the hardest roster decisions will be? >> All of them are hard. Anytime you got to cut somebody, but obviously the receiver room, there's going to be some there's going to be some in the backer room inside and outside. The last D-lineman's going to be some and it's going to be problem in the secondary. So, you know, wideouts as well. So, we got we got a big problem as well as quarterback. >> Would you would you consider keeping three quarterbacks or would would you be more nervous about putting Daniels on on waivers or something like that? [clears throat] >> We'll consider it. We'll see. We haven't talked about it all yet, but you know, there's a lot of decisions that have to be made. >> Coach, do you do you expect Tristan Wirfs to be part of the joint practice against Jacksonville? And do you think the tackle situation could kind of mess up the joint practices at all? >> No, we'll see. We we're going to start working him and see how he feels and kind of go off how he feels. >> Anything else? >> Thanks, coach. >> Thanks. >> We're going to bring in Daniels in a few minutes, though, the locker room.

title: Jalon Daniels Talks Success vs. Kansas City | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: What's good, y'all? You >> think you're used to these victories, huh? [laughter] >> Absolutely. You got to love some wins. >> Jaylen, you seem pretty excited in the tunnel after the game. >> Yeah. Uh, definitely. I mean, uh, my family, that's what I was looking at at first. They were right above the tunnel. They flew all the way out here from Los Angeles. So, you know, I always love when my my mom and my pops are able to come out here and watch me play football. But then just being able to celebrate the win with all the Bucks fans that were at the tunnel as well was was amazing. Jaylen, second week in a row you come in, get the team on the board, get the win. Um, what is it about about you that brings life to the huddle and and got you guys going? >> Yeah, I mean, I I just come in with with confidence. I think I'm very confident with everything that I do within this game of football. I've been playing it since I was seven years old. And um, when you think of it like that, when you go out there and play football, you're kind of just like, "All right, bet." I mean, I've been dreaming to be in this position since I was that young. And every single opportunity that comes my way, whenever my number is called, I'm going to go out there and do it 100% confidently. do it out there with a smile and go out there and play 100% hard. >> Joe, what does it mean not only to get the drives to take the lead, but be able to stay in there and get the conversions to run on the clock to close out the win? >> I mean, it means everything. Um, they they say that the very the best football play that you can run as an offense is is victory for. So, [laughter] uh, to be able to have those three knees to be able to end the game, that's something that you want to be able to do every single week. And I think that being able to, uh, go out there and execute that offense within the second half with all those guys allowed us to be able to come at the end and do that. >> How do you think you've improved the most? Um, I I would say being able to to understand what Zro was saying through through the headset, being able to reiterate that to the guys and being able to make sure that I have all of the knowledge that I need to know pre- snap and being able to to go out there and be able to execute that. I mean, that was something that I didn't really do in college. I kind of just got, hey, you got wristband 91, look at the wristband, and I'm I'm reading it all. So now I'm hearing Z-Rob say it and uh having to be able to remember all of those calls, remember exactly why I'd have to switch one play to another and then being able to have to reiterate that to all those guys wasn't the easiest thing at first, but I think that I've grown to be able to become better with it. >> Jaylen, there was a sequence right before Tucker's touchdown where you ran almost scored and then you got everybody lined up right on the goal line. Take me through that whole sequence. What were you hearing? What did you execute in that? >> Yeah, I'm not going to lie. when I when I spun off it, of bro, I honestly thought I was about to try to be able to dive in there and then I [laughter] kind of kind of got stalemated there at the at the the one yard line, but um in my head I was just like, "All right, bet. I wonder what what's going to be the next call." And then I hear Zerro saying, "All right, bet. Uh we're on the ball right now. Right now, run this play right now." And I'm like, "All right, bet. Hey, I know exactly what the play was about to be." And in my head, I'm sitting like, "All right, bet. Tuck. This is you. You about to get this ball. Go ahead. Find the hole." And he was able to do that. >> Was Dro saying bet back? No, he wasn't saying I mean [laughter] he wasn't saying bet back, but I know he knows I was probably saying bet. >> Jaylen, what's going through your head when you're like creating plays out of structure, when you're throwing on the run, when you're moving out of the pocket, you're still able to find a guy. >> Um, at the end of the day, one thing that I learned from uh the University of Kansas with something called rule of zero. Rule of zero just means you want to be able to get back to the line of scrimmage no matter what. Uh, you don't want to make a bad play worse. Sometimes the defense, they they get paid to be able to go out there and play defense as well. So when they're out there doing what they can, if you're able to extend the play and try to be able to continue moving the sticks, that's something I want to be able to do. But at the end of the day, if the defense is doing their jobs, I'm going to do what I can to be able to get to the line of scrimmage. And if I can't, I'm going to throw the ball away. >> Is that where you get the I think you had two snaps that got away from you. And again, just kind of pick it up and go. Is that where that calm >> thousand%. I mean, you got to be the eraser. When there's something bad going on, you can't you can't allow it to be able to keep on continuing. So when the ball hits the ground at the end of the day, get back to the line of scrimmage and if you're able to get more yards than that, do what you can. or even like the ability to to get them to jump off sides, like just the little things like that. >> We That was one of those things where I was like I literally came into the huddle and said, "All right, guys. We got we got a third and one right here." Um we're going to try to be able to get them to jump off sides. And um obviously we had a few false starts in the first half. So when I came into the huddle, I said, "We cannot have that right now." Um and and just basically try tried to reiterate that as much as I could. And then when we got on the line of scrimmage, we were able to make them jump off sides. That's exactly why you seen all the excitement from me as soon as they jumped off sides. >> What was what was reaction to that? I didn't I didn't even see Zerub after that. I kind of just seen Bake on the side like there you go. [laughter] >> You just also like the guys like Cameron Johnson and Garrett Green. How's it been like building that chemistry and playing with them and how have they helped you at this level as you kind of get used to your NFL journey the preseason games? >> Yeah, I mean you you you mentioned a couple guys who have been in the NFL. They've seen uh a lot of quarterbacks come into the NFL. They've seen a lot of um things that you're able to they they were able to help me with a lot of things. uh especially when we're talking about being able to communicate within the huddle, being able to see things differently, being able to make sure that when we are at the line of scrimmage, how to be able to operate that and be able to make sure things continue to go smoothly. So, um hats off to those guys for being able to continue to to welcome me with Open Orange as being a rookie, being a UDFA rookie, and um I think that they definitely are guys who have continued to be able to help me continue to grow. >> All right, that's all for >> Appreciate y'all. Go Bucks.

title: Todd Bowles Reflects on W vs. KC | Press Conference Live Stream
text: Then we'll come from Scott Reynolds. >> Hey coach. >> Through training camp and now these two preseason games, what have you discovered about your defense and and what do you like best about it that you've seen so far? >> I think them understanding each other, especially up front, understanding the pass rush game and playing together. It it's kind of young, but but you've you're no stranger to playing young cornerbacks. But what what are your overall thoughts in terms of the players that comprise your depth chart right now? >> I think they're very athletic. Got to get Officers and Marson. Got to get out there at the same time, but I think they're very athletic and I think they're very good at man coverage guys. >> Thank you. >> We'll go to Logan Robinson. And so, we pretty much got a good gauge on that. >> Scott Reynolds. >> Todd, you look at your your depth at inside linebacker. How do you feel about that position? You you kept five inside linebackers last year with John Bostic making the team as a special teams contributor, but how is that shaping up now between those younger players outside of your your four veterans? I'm going to include Trotter in there cuz he's a second-round pick, but in terms of your undrafted free agents and and Jackson and Bostic from last year. >> The heck of a competition. I mean, all of them have made plays on defense, and all of them made plays on special teams last night, so that's going to be a tough one. >> We'll go to Rick Stroud. >> Hey, coach. You know, obviously last night you had you know, Tristan was out and Justin and um and uh Ben, but uh Paul Rubelt played the whole game. How did he do? And And what is the status of those guys this week uh for Jacksonville? and And And can they practice or what are they going to do? >> Uh he played the whole game. I thought he fared well. You know, he had some plays he like to have back, but at the same time he fought his butt off and he battled in there for him starting a full game like that playing against their ones and twos. I thought he fared well. We're going to try to start working Tristan back to what some degree in there. The other two I'm not sure about. >> Thanks. >> Scott Reynolds, if any media questions, please raise your hand. >> Coaches, as you head into to Jacksonville um with these joint practices with the Jaguars, what's your relationship like with Liam Cohen these days and and what are you looking to specifically accomplish in these two joint practices? >> No, my me and Liam have always been great. We've been great the whole time. Our relationship hasn't changed a bit. We talk, we text, we bounce things off each other. So, that thing that's been part of it that's been great. It'll be great for us to get practice reps against them because you know, this will be the last ones going into the season and you'll see a full gamut. We got a small sample size last night, but we need more practice in certain situations to clean up things. So, hopefully to get some good work in up there. >> And sticking with that coach, what exactly will you be looking for in joint practices this week? >> Uh just situational football. Us understanding situational football. Obviously, uh playing against somebody else is always different, but playing in different situations and putting guys in different situations and continuing that going into the season, that's going to be important for us. >> And don't know if you had a chance to watch the tape yet, but you mentioned last week David Walker and his run defense. Uh have you had a chance to look at that yet and notice any improvements there? >> Yeah, I looked at it. I saw some improvements at him. He had some good pass rushes. There was some improvement in the run game. He's got to keep getting better. I think his is more time on task. The more he plays, the more comfortable he feels. >> Awesome. Thanks. >> Rick Shroud. >> Coach, you obviously have depth at receiver. You do have a couple injuries there, but what did you see from Dean Patterson last night? And just you know, you've got some veterans as well. How how tough is that going to be to make a decision? And does does any of those guys on the lower end there have a chance still? >> Yeah, they have a chance. I mean, it's going to be tough. And we watched Dean week by week. We watched this guy get better from the spring. And every week you watch him, he's showing gradual improvement doing everything. And and that's great to see for this guy. We know he can run after catch. We know he's tough. Uh it took him a little bit to pick up the system, but every time you put him in there, he's making plays. So, we just got to see how he plays on special teams. And it's a tough room to compete against, but he has made strides and we do notice them. >> I was going to say, is there some guys on special teams uh that have that have shown you anything on at the receiver position? >> Uh other than the returners, I thought Seals had a good night at special teams last night. He played well at the gunner spot right there. Obviously, Cam does a good job returning the ball there. Yeah. Guys just have to step up and see. >> Thanks, coach. >> [clears throat] >> Just to pick up on Rick's question In expanding that, what are your thoughts on on the coverage units last night on special teams and outside of the receiver position, who are some players that are catching your eye? >> I thought there were major improvements from last week to last night. Those guys did a heck of a job on kickoff and they did a heck of a job on the punt team as well. The coverage units, it was a different guy all the time. I mean, you seen Ford to make a play. You seen Keontae make a play. You seen Seals obviously make a play. Bullock made some plays. Bowyer made some plays. I thought the young guys really showed great improvement from last week to this week and that's what you want to see. >> Thanks, Todd. >> Logan Robinson. >> Todd, you've had a little bit more time now since the game is over. What were your thoughts on Jaylen Daniels just looking back at the tape some more and evaluating there? >> He played well. Again, he played well two weeks in a row. That first throw he made off schedule when he came in and wasn't for first down or anything, but it was a heck of a throw and heck of a ball placement. He's calm out there. He's poised. He makes plays to win the game and you know, those guys believe in him and two weeks in a row he showed he played well. >> Todd, obviously Ted Hurst is still learning the mental side of things. Kind of what was the overall message behind the unnecessary roughness penalty that he took out on that first drive? >> It can't set us back, you know, that was a young mistake. It was a rookie mistake. He'll learn from it. We don't teach that. Obviously, he'll learn from that and have more poise. >> If any other media members have a question, please unmute. All right. I think that's all. Thanks, coach.
