It didn't mean nothing as far as them flip-flopping, but we wanted to see him earlier. Todd, I know you mentioned Yaya Diyabi and Ruben Bane, but what can you say about David Walker consistently generating pressure out there? >> I know he had some pretty good rushes. I got to look at the overall part of the game, but I did see two good rushes. What >> have you seen from Mo Cam? Was in the practice squad last year. He shown up made some splash plays the last couple. >> No, he has a lot of energy. It's just grasping the entire system. You know, he has some very good plays where he's very tough and he plays with all the energy. He's just got to make sure he has a good command of the defense. You're going to have some joint practices coming up and then the final preseason game. Where do you anticipate the hardest roster decisions will be? >> All of them are hard. Anytime you got to cut somebody, but obviously the receiver room, there's going to be some uh there's going to be some in the back room inside and outside. Uh the last D lineman's going to be some. It's going to be a problem in the secondary. So, you know, wide outs as well. So, we got we got a big problem as well as quarterback. >> Would you would you consider keeping three quarterbacks or would you be nervous about Daniel on on waivers or something like that. >> We'll consider it. We'll see. We haven't talked about it all yet, but you know, there's a lot of decisions that have to be made. >> Coach, do do you expect Tristan Works to be part of the joint practice against Jacksonville? And do you think the tackle situation could kind of mess up the joint practices a little bit? >> No, we'll see. We're going to start working them and see how he feels and kind of go off how he feels. >> Anything else? >> Thanks, What's good, y'all? >> You can get used to these victories, huh? >> Absolutely. You got to love some wins. >> Jaylen, you seem pretty excited in the tunnel after the game. >> Yeah, definitely. I mean, uh, my family, that's who I was looking at at first. They were right above the tunnel. They flew all the way out here from Los Angeles. So, you know, I always love when my my mom and my pops are able to come out here and watch me play football, but then just being able to celebrate the win with all the Bucks fans that were at the tunnel as well was was amazing. >> Jaylen, second week in a row, you come in, get the team on the board, get the win. Um, what is it about about you that brings life to the huddle and and got you guys going? >> Yeah, I mean, I I just come in with with confidence. I think I'm very confident with everything that I do within this game of football. I've been playing it since I was 7 years old. And, um, when you think of it like that, when you go out there and play football, you're kind of just like, "All right, bet." I mean, I've been dreaming to be in this position since I was that young. And every single opportunity that comes my way, whenever my number is called, I'm going to go out there and do it 100% confidently. Do it out there with a smile and go out there and play 100% hard. >> What does it mean not only to get the drives to take the lead, but feel to stay in there and get the conversions to run on the clock to close out the win? >> I mean, it means everything. Um, they they say that the very the best football play that you can run as a offense is is victory formation. So, uh, to be able to have those three needs to be able to end the game, that's something that you want to be able to do every single week. And I think that being able to uh go out there and execute that offense within the second half with all those guys allowed us to be able to come at the end and do that. >> What do you think you've improved the most? >> Um I I would say being able to to understand what Zro was saying through through the headset, being able to reiterate that to the guys and being able to make sure that I have all the knowledge that I need to know pre- snap and being able to to go out there and be able to execute that. I mean, that was something that I didn't really do in college. I kind of just got, hey, you got wristband 91. Look at the wristband. And I'm I'm reading it all. So now I'm hearing Z-Rob say it and uh having to be able to remember all of those calls, remember exactly why I'd have to switch one play to another and then being able to have to reiterate that to all those guys wasn't the easiest thing at first, but I think that I've grown to be able to become better with it. >> Jaylen, there was a sequence right before Tucker's touchdown where you ran almost scored and then you got everybody lined up right on the goal line. Take me through that whole sequence. What were you hearing? What did you execute in that moment? >> Yeah, I'm not going to lie. when I when I spun off it, of bro, I honestly thought I was about to try to be able to dive in there and then I kind of kind of got stalemated there at the at the the one yard line, but um in my head I was just like, "All right, bet. I wonder what what's going to be the next call." And then I hear Zro saying, "All right, bet. Uh we're on the ball right now. Right now, run this play right now." And I'm like, "All right, bet. Hey, I know exactly what the play was about to be." And in my head, I'm sitting like, "All right, bet. Tuck. This is you. You about to get this ball. Go ahead. Find the hole." And he was able to do that. >> Was he Rob saying bet back? No, he wasn't saying I mean he wasn't saying bet back, but I know he knows I was probably saying bet. >> Jaylen, what's going through your head when you're like creating plays out of structure, when you're throwing on the run, when you're moving out of the pocket and you're still able to find a guy? >> Um, at the end of the day, one thing that I learned from uh the University of Kansas with something called rule of zero. Rule of zero just means you want to be able to get back to the line of scrimmage no matter what. Uh you don't want to make a bad play worse. Sometimes the defense, they they get paid to be able to go out there and play defense as well. So when they're out there doing what they can, if you're able to extend the play and try to be able to continue moving the sticks, that's something I want to be able to do. But at the end of the day, if the defense is doing their jobs, I'm going to do what I can to be able to get to the line of scrimmage. And if I can't, I'm going to throw the ball away. >> Is that where you get the I think you had two snaps that got away from you. And again, just got to pick it up and go. Is that where that calm >> thousand%. I mean, you got to be the eraser. When there's something bad going on, you can't you can't allow it to be able to keep on continuing. So when the ball hits the ground at the end of the day, get back to the line of scrimmage. And if you're able to get more yards than that, do what you can. or even like the ability to to get them to jump off sides. Like just the little things like that. >> We That was one of those things where I was like I literally came into the huddle and said, "All right, guys. We got we got third and one right here. Um we're going to try to be able to get them to jump off sides." And um obviously we had a few false starts in the first half. So when I came into the huddle, I said, "We cannot have that right now." Um and and just basically try tried to reiterate that as much as I could. And then when we got on the line of scrimmage, we were able to make them jump off sides. That's exactly why you seen all the excitement from me as soon as they jumped off sides. >> What was what was reaction to that? I didn't I didn't even see Zerub after that. I kind of just seen Bake on the side like there you go. >> You just like the guys like Cameron Johnson and Garrett Green. How's it been like building that chemistry and playing with them and how have they helped you at this level as you kind of get used to your NFL journey the preseason games? >> Yeah, I mean you you you mentioned a couple guys who have been in the NFL. They've seen uh a lot of quarterbacks come into the NFL. They've seen a lot of um things that you're able to they they were able to help me with a lot of things. uh especially when we're talking about being able to communicate within the huddle, being able to see things differently, being able to make sure that when we are at the line of scrimmage, how to be able to operate that and be able to make sure things continue to go smoothly. So, um hats off to those guys for being able to continue to to welcome me with open horns as being a rookie, being a UDFA rookie. And um I think that they definitely are guys who have continued to be able to help me continue to grow. That's all for appreciate y'all. Go Bucks.

title: Tanner McKee & More On Preseason Game vs Patriots
text: It's not what? Um, better to today. >> Yeah. >> Uh, why? >> Why? We talked a lot about execution and not shooting ourselves in the foot with penalties. Um, felt like we did a lot better job. Um, not going backwards. It's really hard to play offense, obviously, just playing first and 20 or second and 15, whatever it is. But, you can't call the plays that you want to play that you want to call when you're in those situations. And so, just finding a rhythm, getting the drive started. Um, and I thought just was better as well. >> Did you was the playbook opened up a little bit just to give you guys a little more to play with this time? >> Uh, I would I would say so. Um, yeah. I I I would say so, which was great. Um, I I thought Sean called a great a great game. Um, just, you know, had a had a couple really really good calls, easy throws for the quarterback, easy reads. Um, and so, yeah, I I thought it was great. >> How about Carson? >> Yeah, how about Carson? Um, yeah, great, you know, awesome for him stepping up. you know, we we just got word that that JJ's doing okay, which is which is awesome. Um, uh, but, you know, Carson, you know, stepping in, taking taking those extra reps and balling, um, which was great. It was really good to see, you know, having a lot of confidence in him, um, doing the right thing, you know, eyes looking at the same at the right spot, knowing when he's the hot, knowing, um, in pass protection who he's got. Um, it was it was great to see and, uh, just the excitement that it brought on the sideline when he was hurdling guys and when things were going on, it was it was good to see. >> Did you, uh, want that last drive? >> Uh, as a competitor, you always want to go in to to win the game. you know, um, I I'm waiting for for coaches to tell me when when to go into the game, when do when do I leave the game. Um, and so, as a competitor, of course, I want I want every drive. Um, so, yeah. >> Speaking of, uh, compete being competitive and competition, where do you think things stand between you and Danny Andy at this point? Um I don't know. I I I play when the coaches put me in. Um you know, obviously put my best foot forward, try to do all the extra things. Um whether that's in the film room or on the practice field, staying late, talking with the guys, um bonding, whatever that is. Um and I let them decide all that. >> Did you Did you know the Was the process the same way in terms of like you knowing that you were not going to be the the first guy up or you know, you found out the same time. Everything was kind of just around >> Pretty Yeah, pretty much the similar to the last game. >> Yeah. How did you feel like you did in the joint practices this week? >> Um felt great. Just getting a lot of extra reps with the uh against another team, which was great. Um obviously the the Ravens game didn't go that way that we wanted to. And so being able to get another um another shot at running our plays against another team was was great. You know, obviously in joint practice you you open up the playbook a little bit more knowing that it's you know, not going to be televised and it's not every team's going to be able to watch that film. Um and so that was great doing doing all of our stuff. And yeah, it was it it it was great cuz obviously I think I think we all kind of had that itch. We want to get back on the field. We want to play against someone else after what we put on film uh last week. And so um it was nice that we got the opportunity to do that in joint practice. And then obviously, you know, great tonight that we were able to sustain some more drives, put some more points on the board. >> The um the word came pretty quick that you know, JJ had who was injured and stuff and he was out on the field. How did that help you guys settle down and feel positive and confident about the football that happened so soon after the after we left the field? >> Yeah. Um yeah, pretty I think everyone's different. Um a lot of different emotions, you know, just you know, praying hoping that he's okay. Hopefully, you know, it's the best case scenario. Um at that moment just you know, hoping that he gets the best care and everything and you know, everyone's asking about him hoping that he's getting okay. And so then, you know, word was going around that he was talking, he was responsive and he was moving, so that that kind of got everybody to settle down a little bit, and just at least, you know, we know our teammate's doing okay. >> How do you feel you are in terms of learning this offense? Would you say that like, you know, at first it was like, you know, kind of like process, maybe a struggle, and then you feel like you've kind of been on an upward trend? >> Yeah, I would say so. I mean, anytime that it's a new offense, there's going to be a learning curve, and we definitely had that. It's it's very different than what we've run in the past. And so, just with the new terminology, different, you know, techniques, fundamentals. And so, of course, there's going to be some some bumps in the road, but as long as we don't make the same mistake twice, and as long as we're trending upwards, I think those are going to be good bumps, as long as, you know, they they stay in practice, we learn in film, we learn from other people's mistakes. Especially a guy getting limited reps, I got to learn from Jaylen's mistakes, and Andy's mistakes, and Cole's mistakes, as as well as my own. And so, just being able to stay on that upward trend. Cool. Thanks, guys. You know, what do you think about tonight overall versus, I guess, the first game? Did they give you a little more in terms of what the playbook or what you could do? >> Yeah, I mean, I think there there's a little more that was going in that went into it. Obviously, when we go in and we're practicing against them, there's some more stuff that was put into the offense and everything. So, um Yeah, I mean, I think there's we're going to look back at this and say there's there's some things that we want back. For me, personally, I'm sure I'll look at a couple plays and be like, man, I wish I had a couple of these back, but um you know, I think, again, it's preseason, we're just trying to keep moving forward and keep improving. >> Um you had some productive moments, obviously, the fourth-down throw. What did you see on that one? >> Yeah, it was good, I mean, if we get through my progression on that one, that was one where, you know, kind of get all the way back to number four in the progression, and uh me, I just felt like just the timing and rhythm of it was was right there. Yeah, Coop was in the right spot and just gave me a chance and so yeah, I think that you can we can look at some plays like like that one for example and say okay, yeah, that's some things that guys are everybody's hitting on all cylinders and more guys are in the right spots and there's going to be some other ones that we're going to want back. >> Is it uh you mentioned the timing and the rhythm and stuff like that. Is that like what maybe's lacking when the when passes aren't being completed? >> Yeah, I mean I think that's a little part of it. Um so >> [snorts] >> I think for me I got to going to have to watch the film and kind of look and see every see what I can do to to help with all of that. But um I mean there's little things. I think that's part of this offense is the timing and rhythm of it all and uh when it's off just a little bit I mean it not always going to complete them. >> This isn't your first rodeo um in terms of being with a new team too. You know, how do you think this is going versus maybe some of the other places you've been? Has it been different because of I don't know whatever this point your career all the new faces and the changes that the Eagles are actually obviously going with a new scheme as well. Is that affecting you? >> Yeah, you know, I think um for me every place is a little bit different. Uh I feel really comfortable with the guys here. Uh I think that's one thing that you can see the talent that we have on this team. I think from a coaching standpoint too like an offense um you know, I feel like I've got a really good understanding of all all the stuff that we're that we're doing. So um yeah, I mean there's every place is a little bit different with the the transition and everything. But uh I'm enjoying myself here. >> Do you think this this competition's going to go down to like the wire? >> Yeah, I mean I don't know. We'll have to have to see how it how it all goes. Um you know, I think that's one thing that there's not much been said with everything where every day is a new day and so we'll we'll we'll see how it all ends up. >> Obviously when you have two quarterbacks fighting for a backup jet number two job, there's a chance that one could be expendable trades and that kind of stuff. Do you do you ever let your mind wonder okay, this could happen to me if I if I don't win this number two job. >> Yeah, I think we're focusing on the here and now. And you know, with that all that other stuff is, you know, not what we're worried about. And so, yeah, I mean, we just focus on what we can control. >> I didn't get a chance to ask you about how you thought you did in the joint practices. What What did you think of those two those two days of work? >> Yeah, obviously it's good to you get to a point in camp where it's it's kind of good to see some different faces out there to see a new scheme. And yeah, I think that's the the one benefit of the joint practices and you can go be in a controlled environment and everything. So, I thought there were some things that we did really really well. and so, yeah, I mean, I I felt really comfortable with everything that we were able to do in in the joint practices. >> Okay. Thanks. >> When's the last time you hurdled someone? >> Man, it's been a second. You know, couple of them I didn't think I was going to get up there, but I I'm going to say back in my ball state days. That's probably the last time I did it, so. >> I've heard that some coaches don't really like it when a player hurdles. Are you going to hear about that? >> Um I don't know about those ones. Hopefully I don't, so you know, any way you need to make a miss, that's kind of my go-to, so. >> Has anyone given you any advice about hurdling? >> Man, I just I I don't think I can do any backwards stuff like that just yet, but no, I was playing, but you know, being able to work with him every day has been a true blessing. >> I was listening, it sounded like Davante was telling you that you try that again next week. >> Man, yeah, dude's going to stand straight up, but you know, that's the only way I felt for it. That's why they're professional, so I'm going to have to figure something else out now. >> How much fun did you have out there tonight? >> Um you know, I had a blast. Um unfortunately, we didn't get the win, but we you know, executed a lot more things. Definitely, you know, took our game up a level from last weekend and you know, just got to keep progressing from there. >> You were able to rack up a lot of yards after the catch. What what is your mentality when you get the ball in your hand? >> Um you know, any way the team really needs me. Kind of going back earlier like I said, whether it's running the ball, pass game, stuff like that, even special teams. Um you know, just got to go out there and try to make a guy miss. That's my go-to. Um you know, cuz you know, that's how the elite guys kind of really, you know, separate their selves is making that first guy miss out in open space. >> Do you take pride in in your ability to kind of do a little bit of everything? >> I do. Um you know, that's kind of how I started my career. Special teams, trying to out full back, you know, I've done that as well. Some people say I am a full back, some people say I'm running back, you know. I'm here to do whatever. That's really what it is. Um special teams, so I do really take pride in that. >> What do you tell people your position is? >> Uh a little bit of everything. I tell them Swiss Army knife, try to do a little bit. Uh I'm, you know, running back I've done since I was a little kid. I've blocked for a full back. I haven't really done special teams, so that's definitely, you know, year three it's definitely helped me from my rookie year to now. I feel a lot better about that. >> It seems like you've been primarily used as a running back in this offense. What when you signed here, what was your understanding of what your role was going to be? >> Um you know, things kind of switched around here, and uh you know, we haven't really, you know, gotten fully into the I mean, we've gotten into the playbook, but there's always, you know, add-ons and stuff like that, especially with a new offense. So, we're all still kind of learning, you know, the you know, the technique of the runs, the passes, and stuff like that, and just building off of that. >> Thank you, Carlos. Appreciate it. >> Appreciate it, man. Thank you, guys. >> Is that the uh the quickest you've ever gotten a sack? >> Yeah, that's probably the quickest I've ever gotten a sack. I you know, uh we were in a good call this call right there. I was able to time it up well, and uh you know, jump it a little bit. >> What goes into timing it like that? >> Uh really it's just trying to I was trying to just, you know, read the QB's mannerisms, with him being under the center. Uh trying to wait for his hand to go under under the center. That lets me know that, you know, he's getting ready for the snap, but that's, you know, some of the stuff that our coaches had to teach us to pick up on when we're in our blitzes, uh and get good timing on it. >> How confident do you feel right now at this point in your career? >> Yeah, I'm I'm feeling confident, you know, I I've learned a lot, you know, have great had great veterans in front of me, uh with Nick Perry and Zach, you know, even when Nick Perry was here in my my rookie year and then uh my uh my second year, too. Uh, just learning from them and learning from the coaches. Coach Vic, you know, he's a great defensive mind. Uh, just trying to soak in all the knowledge I can from him, as well. But, uh I feel like just being able to have those 2 years under my belt and soak up as much knowledge as as I can from guys that are have a lot of experience has really helped me out. >> It seems like you're you're the caliber player that you could be starting in this league. And we know the situation with this team. How do you how do you handle that part? >> Uh, I just try to make sure I'm doing my part, you know, whatever my role is on this team. Uh, I I try to just do be the best player I can to help out my teammates and and and and put do 100% of in my in that role that I am and you know, whatever that is, you know, I just try to put my head down and grind really every single day. >> Do you feel like you're that caliber player? >> Uh, you know, I definitely, you know, very confident in my in my abilities and but uh you know, as far as right now, I'm just trying to make sure I'm grinding and doing my part to be the best player I can be and uh you know, continue to improve upon myself so I can be, you know, maximize my capabilities. >> I know you're new here, so I already asked this question, but but what do you like about getting the opportunity to blitz and getting after the quarterback? >> Uh, you know, I I love it, you know, um you know, when we blitz, we have a mindset as linebackers on, you know, with the Philadelphia Eagles that we want to get home. Uh, we want to get wins and and and and make plays, so that's really just our mindset that we preach in our in our room uh every single day. >> Where does that sack rank among like your fastest sacks of your career? >> As far as my career, that's probably the fastest. Um, I was I was surprised like how kind of split it like that, but I was able to get a good time in, you know, on that blitz, so it worked out nice. >> Okay, thanks so much. >> Appreciate it. >> Uh, it seems like you're just a confident player right now. >> Yeah, you know, just being able to, you know, rep it in practice and and feel confident. Uh, like you said, I go out there and just got to produce and perform and, you know, I'm I'm trying to trying to stay here, so just being able to to go out there and have fun with my guys. >> It seems like over the last few weeks, you've been kind of a different player. Uh, do you feel that? Like do you feel just maybe we're only seeing the results, but do you feel like it's kind of been building toward this? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, obviously it started in the off-season, and once we got to, you know, camp, just needed to, you know, just kind of taking that next step. And you know, there's definitely in the beginning just needed to kind of find myself, and then, you know, build find that confidence, and you know, uh with Q coming in, our D assistant guy, I mean, being just talking with him, you know, it's been awesome. He's been really helpful in building that confidence and just, you know, going out there and just playing playing free. And so, I owe a lot to him. >> How have you guys built that confidence? >> I mean, just, you know, after every practice we go in the D-line room, you know, we grab lunch, and then, you know, we watch film, or or, you know, talk about his playing days and like what he used to do, and you know, just what I could do better out there on the field, and you know, he's very passionate about the game of football, and you know, I I respect him, so I, you know, what he has to say, I appreciate. >> Did you hear what Vic said about you this week? >> I I did. I did. And you know what? I'll take that as a compliment. You know, he's not wrong. You know, last year just had to find myself. You know, I was on scout team, just, you know, understanding how the NFL worked, and you know, we have a pretty good offensive line, so getting to work against those guys and just get better. You know, it's obviously showing that it's helped. >> I'm sorry. I I joined in late, but what is what is just this whole training camp been like, you know, taking reps early on with the developmental guys, and then, you know, working your way up the depth chart? What's like kind of your mentality through it all? >> I mean, you know, obviously my goal is to play. You know, I want to be a contributor for this team. You know, somebody's got to take those reps, so when I get thrown in there, you know, it's just an opportunity to, you know, go out there and show them that, you know, I'm able to climb that depth chart, as you say, and and, you know, just keep performing. >> Some of your finishes at the quarterback were pretty violent. Is that part like that you want to be a part of your game? >> Yeah, I mean, that's been a part of my game since college. I mean, I loved, you know, that the that you have to have that violence to play defensive line, otherwise I wouldn't be here playing defensive line. You know, obviously the Eagles saw that in me when they drafted me. So, you know, it's only right to show them that I got it. >> Uh it seemed like everyone was It seemed like everyone was pretty excited for Josh to get his sack. What was that moment like for everyone? >> I I mean, you know, for for guys that have never really played football to come in and then, you know, perform and and you know, see that success, I mean it's awesome. You know, it's hard to play football, especially in the NFL. So, when you get that get those sacks or you get the tackle or whatever, you mean even for you are, you know, he was in on a couple tackles tonight as well and you know, I just told him, you know, be free, have fun out there and when you do like use that to juice you up for the next play to to go make another one. >> He had a second sack after the >> Jose, yeah. >> Yeah, yeah. How did that play kind of come about and like >> Yeah, that I mean that was just Coach Vic's play call. Uh you know, Jose's an awesome person to run those types of games with and he really did a great job coming in there and picking the guard for me to to wrap around and that tackle stayed on him. So, you know, I told him I owed him one especially since we ran two in a row. So, I told him, you know, I got him next time. >> Thank you, Corey. >> I'm tape. I appreciate you putting it on tape enough to make the case that you wanted. >> I mean that's not up to me, you know. I'm just going to keep doing it. You know, we got one more game. So, I'm going to go out there and and perform again and you know, you know, prove why I belong to be here. >> Yeah, it was just unreal. I mean, just thank God for kind of this whole process and getting to this point and yeah, I'm just grateful for everyone who's kind of let me get to this point. >> [laughter] >> Arrogant. >> [clears throat] >> What did that moment mean for you or like kind of signify when you brought him down? Kind of what was going through your mind, your emotions? >> I was just happy. I think No, I'm just listening. Um yeah, no, I think it was just happy. I think I tired myself out more celebrating than actually running after to get the sack, but I mean, it's just all the work that we've been putting in and all the support that I've been getting from my coaches, players. I think you saw how happy all of the people in my room were for me. So, that I mean, you can see how much it means to them, like my development. So, I was I mean, yeah. >> Can you take me through the actual play? It looked like were you trying to like show a spike inside and then >> Um to be honest, like when someone asked me what I did, I was like It's just I thought like a gap just kind of opened up. I haven't watched it back, so I think I had a chipper, so I went in and then I think the tackle maybe tried to block the D-tackle and then >> Okay. >> open lane and I just ran. It could be different. I haven't seen actually haven't seen it. >> looked like you tried to sell a stunt. >> Oh, maybe. >> To be honest, I don't know. I just ran and I saw open space. I'd be lying if I said I tried to do something special, but yeah, um it just opened up and I was happy to be able to get the QB down. >> We've talked about you and Oluwole going through this experience together. To see both of you end up on the stat sheet tonight, is that pretty substantial and significant to you? >> Yeah, it is. I think I talked to you about taking wins.
