Um and when it times when it gets time to to to game plan and get people the rock, we'll we'll get them the rock. >> How much fun is it to see maybe some of the veteran guys and guys some of the like the young guys like the pre-season games? >> It's great. You know, like I I uh you know, you're always you know, to you know, Gus has all these sayings, you know, but like the the the greatest form of of joy is when you have joy for others, you know, and it's uh uh to see our team kind of appreciate how each one is working. They've all been there. They've all had their first pre-seasons and being the fourth quarter and I thought our guys were resilient. I thought the defense was outstanding. I thought our offense ran the ball really well. Those uh young bucks, and uh but to see them all cheering and pulling for one another, I think it's pretty cool. >> Even given that >> It It was those two plays. You know, I felt like felt really good about all the different things that were happening. Um you know, we had the explo- defensive explosive play on defense uh the and on a negative play that was negated by a penalty. Um I got to get clarity on that one cuz I didn't agree with the call on Tony Adams. And then uh the interception got negated. Uh I do think the defense stood up in that uh sudden change situation when we went for it on fourth down and got stopped, but like I said, I I think this was a really really productive week. Um you know, defend- as an as a team, you know, we've Monday, Wednesday, and then the the joint practice on Friday, three game-like um low uh volume uh from a volume standpoint, but um but there's a lot to take from this week, you know, like I said, I thought the joint practice was fantastic. Uh and then obviously this game just to take a lot from it. >> The down by by the tight end, I know you said it was a matter of having not seen it before, was that just a communication issue or or what was that? Cuz it seemed like like a basic >> It It >> Uh for sure. For basic, 100% basic, but like uh le- without getting too too big in the weeds on whose responsibility that was, but it stuff like that happens when you go from a match team to a vision-based team like we are. and uh but there's there's still elements of match in our scheme. And uh it just bringing that awareness to certain certain things that pop up, but uh like I said, I'm glad it happened cuz it it's an easy fix, and for the player to feel that, it's like one of those I get it now. And so for Kevin and Hook and all the safeties and all the corners, um and and the way they communicate those little simple exchanges, it it's a it's a really cool aha moment. Unfortunately, it happened in a game-like atmosphere. Thank god it was preseason. Um but 100% will get fixed. >> Even given everything you said about the vanilla offense, has there been a lot of room these last 2 weeks for crisper execution within what you've done? >> Yeah, like there's always room for improvement. Like in a perfect world we we have three drives and then we have three touchdowns and we move the ball at will. But uh like I said, I think we had a a good first drive that one got points. Um had an opportunity on the fourth and one to extend the drive. I was probably a little more aggressive than I normally would be with the with the ball being on the 35 or wherever it was, but um yeah, I'm you're always going to strive for for better execution.

title: Cam Ward Speaks After the Preseason Win Over Seattle | Titans vs. Seahawks
text: First team offense played there in the first half. >> Uh, I think just missed opportunities on, you know, some plays. Um, particularly our passing game. Uh, I think it was improvement from last week. Um, but just got to be better down the field, you know, as a whole. >> Cam, the pass to Cornell seems like you put it where only he could get it. Just kind of missed his fingertips. Is that something that you guys are working on in practice going forward and just trying to build that connection as you go forward? >> Uh, yeah. Uh, continuously getting more reps in practice when we run zone there um and team periods. Um, and then just, you know, me putting in the a good spot for him to uh end up making a play. Um, but he's made that play a thousand times. So, you know, when the when the time comes, you know, we're going to be able to both make the play. >> Two weeks coach said that you guys are running a basic of basic offense right now. Does that kind of hurt some of those reps uh and some of that connection that you're getting or does it more or less help you as the season as you guys ramp up closer to the regular season? >> Uh, both. Um, you get you take away reps that we do all the time in practice. Um, we're not able to do it in the game. Uh, they also get some real game reps of plays that we're not doing in practice so much. So, it's kind of in between. Um, then it's also, you know, doing what we're good at all the time uh which we're going to, you know, do during the season, not during the preseason. Um, but um it's fun because, you know, you get to, you know, you go through highs and lows of a game. Um, you you see the you see the competitive the competitiveness atmosphere that we all have. Um, and we all just eager to make those plays and we will. >> Two weeks in a row you had a play that could have really bit you if it the ball had bounced differently. What When you look back on the play at the sideline when the guy batted the ball away, uh what might you have done differently and what were you thinking as that was unfolding? >> Um, he dove on the ball and made a good Um, end up losing a couple yards. That's the bad part about it. So, I got to be better in, you know, my ball security standpoint when I'm outside the pocket. Um, but he he made a great play. Um, we just got to be able to, you know, convert on third down. >> Preseason game left, three weeks before the regular season starts. What were the areas where this team needs to make the biggest improvements, you think? >> Uh, I'd say our biggest improvement is, you know, connecting on deep play. we only get a certain amount of, you know, shots that we get to take each and every game because our defense are so good. Uh, so when we get to play downfield, you know, myself and the receivers, we have to make the play. So, I need to throw them, you know, catchable ball. Um, they they're going to do their job by, you know, attacking and making the play. So, uh, I think that's the that's what's left for us. And once we do that, you know, we'll be a a pretty a pretty solid offense. >> Having not gotten the results that you probably wanted in the first two preseason games, where are you in regards to approaching that urgency uh, urgent situation and getting the offense on track for the season? >> What what kind of results? >> Well, I mean, you you had what, one touchdown drive in in uh, six six opportunities. You you could agree that it isn't what what you wanted. You're number one out there, right? >> No, it's not. and it's something that, you know, we got to we got to be able to, you know, go get. Um, as far as the touchdown ratio, uh, that's our goal to score the ball each and every time we step on the field. Um, but it's a it's a lot of things that go into it. And you know, for us, um, we're we're more of, you know, continuously have a next play mentality. Um, and you know, making myself making good decisions. Um, we've had a a lot of good decisions from each and everybody from you know, the receiver when they're sitting down in in certain spots in the zone. Um, the old line passing games, also, you know, everyone playing smart football. Um, but you know, when, you know, it's time to do it for real, I think a lot of stuff will click. Um, but we still have, you know, another week to get better on the little things that we need to get better on. >> Cam, how do you control the highs and lows of going from a joint practice where you seem to have pretty good success running the ball and scoring touchdowns against a good defense to a preseason the where, you you said, you're not getting those touchdown plays or those long drives that you look for. >> Uh you just take the game for as it is. You know, it's a it's going to be a lot of one score NFL games out there. So, I mean it just goes back to you know us making the play. You know, in the running game and the passing game. A lot of things tied down into it. But, you know, we just got to continue to you know, harp on what we say. Continue to you know, have the urge and the urgency to go score the ball each and every drive. And we and we have that. You know, eventually it's going to it's going to show off. >> Do you think playing as much as you are in these preseason games is going to help? >> For sure. >> Um We're getting game reps, but not in a real game, if you know what I'm saying. And whether it's the we're going to get to another team's ones, twos, or threes, you know, there's still good talent out there. It's the NFL for a reason. And so, I think the more games and the more reps that we take, I just think it's going to help us you know, come week one and week two. >> You talked so much about how the scramble drill plays are all about timing. Are you comfortable with where the timing is with you guys right now, or is there something you got to kind of figure out to make some of those scramble drill plays hit like they have in the past? >> Uh no, really just making a play. Me putting in the radius and then us having you know, everything around us, you know, from protection me getting outside to extending the play as long as I can. Then to me putting the ball in the receiver's placement and you know, them making a play. And it ends up just becoming about making a play. We make the play, a lot of stuff take care of itself. But, we're not far off. We're actually you know, right there to to getting where we want to be. And the the the coaching staff, they continue to you know, push us to that to that standpoint where we want to be. But, you know, it's going to end up paying off. >> You talked about making the play when the when you had the chance. The big one was with Gunner today. You kind of just missed it. Did you have a chance to talk with him about how that timed up and what just missed? And how much will you guys look at that? >> We should have never been in that situation. Me and Gunner have to be on the on the same page as as far as the the play on time. And then when we do play off schedule, when I do turn the screw on the drill, that's another ball I'm going to throw to Gunner here again. When it when it comes down to it, you know, I'm going to put a little bit more inside for him and he's going to be able to get both feet down. We're going to connect down the butt, you know, that we go through things. You got to go through things right now that way, you know, you can try to minimize as much, you know, when the season does start. So, you know, it's a it's a good and bad with it. But, you know, me and Gunner, you know, we're going to for sure make that play again. >> So, we all talked about needing the fourth and one. You need to be able to convert that. Keep drives alive. How disappointing was it not to be able to move the chains on that? >> I mean, it's disappointing because we turned the ball over, you know, backed up damn near. But, I mean, it's it's a decision that, you know, Coach Saleh made. And, you know, with that decision, I mean, he's showing a lot of confidence in us. So, you know, we got to be able to run the ball or when we do throw it on, third and fourth, you know, short yardage situation, we got to execute. So, just execution of the play and then, just, you know, continuously, you know, trying to get better. >> You got two joint practices against two tough defenses from last year. What are some of the things you kind of learned going against these defenses that you can take into the next preseason game and then into the regular season? >> I think the biggest thing that I that I've learned is, you know, every every DC, every defense is the same but different in terms of what they want to give the quarterback, what they're what they're willing to let the quarterback beat them on. And then, you know, it also adjust to each and every team's defensive line. But, it's easy for me to adjust to that because of who I go against every day in practice. And so, the the biggest thing that, you know, looking forward is, you know, going against the Bears. You know, they're going to do a lot of things that we've already seen. They're They're going to do some things we haven't seen. So, it's really us playing post snap and us, you know, being able to see stuff after after, you know, guys move into their spaces where they getting a tap or, you know, some type of buzz or whatever. Um and then us being able to play, you know, off schedule, you know, and playing on schedule as well. >> Do you think of things kind of started slowing down in Brian Daboll's offense for you or they do you still trying to take everything in? >> No, everything slowed down. Um we're finally at the point where, you know, we're not going to be installing too much stuff too much stuff. Um one thing about coach Daboll is he can go to walk-through, he can make up a play in his head and we'll run it right there and we'll execute it right there. So, uh it's going it's going to be nice to, you know, really show what we really are what we really are about when the time comes. Um but I mean it's exciting because, you know, you get to get reps on plays that, you know, you don't get at OTAs, so you know, you really get to feel of, you know, what he's getting to feel of what I really like and what I don't like. And then when the time comes, you know, we're going to do a lot of stuff that, you know, the players feel comfortable with. >> That's all. >> How big of a coaching point is the missed throw to Ellic on that third drive? It seems like if you put it over his shoulder a little bit more, he might have scored. So, how how much of a coaching point do you think that'll be for you this week? >> Uh it won't be. really need to throw it more higher up there for him to make it a 50/50 ball. Um but that's something that, you know, me and him just got to, you know, continuously work. Um and you know, we got to make the play at the end of the day.

title: Anthony Hill Jr. on His Interception & Playing Fast | Titans vs. Seahawks
text: Where's that ball headed? >> Right in the trophy case. I'm keeping this one. I got to got to keep this one. >> So, you feel like you gave people a little taste of your kind of play-making ability tonight with some some things you did out there? >> Uh like I'll say really just trusting my keys, trusting my techniques, and I'll just let the plays happen. Like you kind of just do your job and be in the right spots while doing your job and you may make plays. You just got to make them. >> How much faster you think you're playing now than compared to when you first got here? >> Uh I feel like it's by like a a big margin. Like understanding where I need to be at, understanding my keys, you know, it's a it's a long road. I still got a lot of work to do, but it's I feel like it's it's coming along. Just keep working and I feel like everything will be all right. >> Game speed is different than what you play in practice, but how do you how much do you think the joint practices are helping you translate to the field as you're getting these game reps? >> Uh I feel like like practice we practice fast, we practice well. So, kind of like practice is pretty similar to games. You know, it's a little bit more physical, of course, but as far as speed and how everything happens, I feel like it's it's kind of the same. It's just finishing on tackles and some of that little stuff that you can't do that you just got to do in the game. >> How much did you talk to Fred Warner and Eric Jones about playing the middle linebacker position or the linebacker position and kind of growing as an NFL linebacker? >> Uh not much. Like I haven't really had a lot of time to kind of tap in with some of those guys. I mean, I just I just got here like 3 months ago. So, I kind of been focused on what I need to do. I got a lot of vets in my room like James Williams, Sed, Cody. So, I kind of been kind of tapping in with some of them to try to see what I can do to get better. >> How do you evaluate tonight as a whole? Obviously, some struggles early getting stops. You guys made some plays at the end of the end of the win. How do you walk away here feeling? >> Uh like I feel like we played physical and that's one thing like at the end of the day we can clean up everything technique, but as long as we're playing physical and fast, hey, that's going to that's going to get us somewhere. >> How do you feel like you've learned over the just over the the time that since training camp has started? How much better do you feel like you are? >> Uh I'll say like not feeling like I'm just a better just understanding the scheme and understanding where I need to be has has grown, but I have a a lot of work I need to do. So, just continue to get better, continue working, and I feel like I'll be all right. >> James, how do you control not getting too high after getting an interception and then having to come back on the field and make more plays? it's pretty like you know we've been playing football for a long time. So, you know you don't really got to too much you don't get overexcited. Like while I'm in the game, I don't get too high or too low with certain stuff. So, once I got the peak, celebrate, and it's like all right, let's like let's get back to get back to playing ball. >> I I know it hasn't been a long time for you, but is there a point where everything just kind of clicked and then it just fell into line? And if so, what was that point? >> Um I feel like it hasn't happened yet. Like I feel like I'm still learning this I got a lot to learn. It's certain stuff that I want to clean up. So, I feel like football is never a sport where you're like, "Oh, I got it. I clicked on it." Once you feel like you got it, it's over. Like you it's football isn't a sport where you ever feel like you made it or you got it cuz it's somebody always coming behind you that feel like this hungry. So, football is never a sport you can be like, "Well, I got it. It's clicking." So, I'm always going to keep working. I'm always trying to get better. >> What what's the biggest thing you you feel you have to clean up? >> I'll say like right now is play action pass. Like that dig I think it was like second and 20. Just continue to working on that like play action got to get 14. It's just something like small details that you can just get better. I could have had two today. So, just thinking about it as far as that like cleaning up some of the some of the small details I could get better at is some that's important to me. >> How much fun was it seeing I guess the vets celebrate all the young guys at the end making plays and and you guys winning? >> It was it was pretty cool. Like I feel like we're a pretty tight team. So, being able to celebrate when some of the vets make plays and when the young guys make plays it's all one team. So, we all want to celebrate with each other. >> Mhm.

title: Cam Ward Speaks After the Seahawks Joint Practice | Tennessee Titans
text: You know, very good, especially going against a Super Bowl winner. It's a great competition on both sides. I haven't got a chance to, you know, see what the defense was able to do, but I heard they had a pretty good day. A pretty good day. Um, we had some explosive plays on offense. We also had some plays that we wish we had back. But I think overall, you know, it was a it was a good day for us. >> It seemed like red zone, two-minute hurry-up all were really strong. Why why do you think those situational things were so good? >> I think just something that, you know, we continuously walk through in walk-throughs with Coach Dayes and the rest of the staff. Something that they harp on cuz that's when we have to be our best. It's a it's a standpoint, especially for me, Coach Dayes and Coach Dayes, for for me to to to have the plays that I want during that time that I feel very comfortable with, no matter what cover they play. And I think a lot of it has to do with the O-line, you know, how they how they played today, how they handled, you know, everything. In the run game and the pass game, you know, and those guys know, you know, if they're they're able to consistently do, you know, what they've been doing this, you know, whole entire off-season, you know, they'll be the reason why, you know, we win a lot more games. >> It seemed like there was a high degree of the short passing game. Was that kind of taking what the defense gave you, or was that something you guys came in wanting to do? What was behind it? >> Uh, both. We play a defense like Seattle. They really don't give us the big play, so you got to be able to beat them with underneath football. You got to beat them with run after catch for the receivers. You got to make those guys tackle. So, we stuck to, you know, what we felt like we had to do to have a productive day. It'll pay dividends for us, you know, all throughout practice. And, you know, something that, you know, me and the receivers got to continuously to harp on to, you know, not overdo anything unless the time comes to it. Other than that, just play good sound football. >> How tough is it for you, as, you know, you like to get the ball down the field, but like you said, that's something they were trying to prevent. How tough is it for you to, you know, get away from that and check it down or take what the defense gives you, knowing you want to make a big play? >> Uh, it's really not tough at all, Because it's helping everybody else. It's helping me get in a rhythm. It's helping the offensive line by me getting the ball out on time. It's helping the receivers by playing on time. So you know, I think it helps everything. That's what we need to be as a passing game what we did today. And you know, the more that we consistently do that, I think it'll benefit us, you know, throughout the whole year. >> And you like to discuss the one interception that you had and then how did you bounce back from that and have the productive day that you did in this game? >> I just continue to play the next play. You got to have a short-term memory. They end up going a little buzz, little match coverage, little thief as as we call it. Had my back to the defense, turn around. As soon as I threw it, I seen him and he was in a, you know, a great defensive call, great, you know, interception by him. But you know, that's when I got to be better getting through the progression. Whether that turns into a check it down, getting a scramble drill. But it's something that, you know, I get to, you know, learn from. And ideally, it's something that, you know, me and Cornell can talk over film. If he feels him coming down a certain to a certain landmark, he might be able to take his angle higher just so we might be able to get that throw off. But at the end of the day, I just got to continue to, you know, see everything post-snap like I've been doing. But you know, bad plays going to happen. I'm going to have an interception in a game. It's just continuously how you play the next play and how you don't let that affect you know, the plays out there. >> Okay, how much is that short-term memory and how did you bounce back from last week's interception? And how did you have everybody on the whole team to have a successful victory this week and continue the growth pattern in this >> Continue to, you know, what continue to harp on the things that we want to accomplish as an offense and as a team. We consistently want to play, you know, fast and violent. We want to, you know, have a have a short-term memory play to play, but we also want to play, you know, with the the energy that no one else seen. So the old line, D-line, they're they're real standpoint on that on that regard and the rest of it, we just continue to, you know, get better each and every day. Try to you know, not make the same mistakes twice. But I think the more we continue to get better each and every day. I just think throughout the whole year, you know, we'll be able to trim the the bad plays down. You know, we'll be able to outweigh you know, the good plays will be able to outweigh the bad. >> What would you like to improve on from game one to this next game on Sunday? >> Uh just continuing my process in and out of the pocket. Uh continue to work scramble drill with the receivers in the live game setting. That's something that we really want to get working throughout this preseason. Um then continue to you know, play within the system. Trusting the play calls, trusting trusting Dave and what he sees. Him also continue to you know, trust me and what I see on the field. So it's been great. And for for us to to have bad plays in San Fran to have you know, good and bad plays versus Seattle. Those are two playoff teams. So you know, we're we're able to you know, their coaches are able to coach us from that and not let it happen again. But you know, we have a lot of smart guys who don't let it happen twice. >> How much do you feel like you got one maybe many skirmish today out of line is pretty clean. What how would you describe maybe just the competitiveness back and forth between the two teams today? >> Uh very competitive. They got a they got a lot of you know, good good guys on that D line. They're one of the best D lines out there. They have a a pretty good secondary. They got a good nickel as well. So it's really more of us you know, continues to play in our brand of football being physical. And you know, I think we were able to tempo them. You know, we were able to see you know, the the true the them true selves. And you know, I think that's going to be a a great part of our offense being able to get in and out of tempo. Then also you know, settle things down when we need to. But you know, it benefited us for sure. >> How much do you feel like you've gotten better on throws outside the numbers and toward the sidelines this year? >> Uh I think I got better. I think we we've gotten coached better of where we want the ball to hit. And then I think the receiver room has also gotten coached better of keeping keeping space for me. The the landmarks and the yardage that we want the ball to hit. Um, because at the end of the day we got to play on time until we can't play on time. Um, and so you know, I think you know, my room and the receiver room, you know, we're all at the standpoint right now. Uh, we know when the ball is there. We know the They know the timing of my drop. I know the timing of the route. Um, the O line know where I'm setting up. So, I think we're at a we're at a good time and space right now and that's something that we just got to continue to get better on as well. >> What are you seeing that's helping to improve the efficiency of the run game right now? It feels like you guys are having decent success. >> I just think the O line being dogs. Um, they they bring the fight each and every day. Um, all that I control in the run game is, you know, who who I'm telling the receivers to get, the the play calls, sometimes they might Um, and all that, but the run game is specifically the O line and they take pride into it. Um, and you know, that's uh we have to have a run game. Um, we were very average in the run game last year. Um, but I think that's going to take a whole another level this year just because of the mindset that those front five guys have. Um, and they they bring it each and every day. And so, um, we all going to continue to rely on those five guys to get us to where we want to go. Um, and you know, when they need us, we going to be able to, you know, protect them as well. >> Do you think there were some A+ run plays today? It seemed like there were some >> Oh, for sure. >> some holes that were >> Yeah, they they they they made some holes for us, for sure. Um, and they were they were the first ones to the ball. Um, they sprinting when the ball is 30 yd past them. Um, so they they showing that urgency that we preach. Um, and that goes a long way cuz it's hard for those guys to consistently do that in and out each and every day. Um, so a lot of it on their bodies, but they continue to push through it. Um, and so you know, I'm happy to have those guys in front of me. Um, and you know, I'm excited to, you know, get the season rolling. >> How much of that run game is you also finding your lanes and utilizing your ability to run as well? Is that something that you put a more concerted effort towards this off season or is it just something that you're finding as you're progressing in that offensive scheme? >> Uh, just something that I'm finding. Um, then also being with with Daze and Shea, letting them showing me clips and and whether it's practice or other quarterbacks or me last year, just certain certain situations where, you know, I can emphasize to use my legs to have the defense have to guard a third play out there cuz it's hard to to guard two plays for a defense, but when you got a third play with a quarterback scramble or run, you know, it it ends up taxing the defense. And so, you know, just picking picking times when I need to. But when I see a lane, try to get it, try to turn the scramble drill and get what I can and get out of bounds. >> How's Carnell responding to maybe his first cold streak, first adversity in Grove Street? Not catching as many passes as early camp. Coming off the injury, too. How are you seeing him respond to all this? >> Uh he he doesn't have a cold streak. He plays one of the hardest positions in sports. He's either going to get the ball or he's not going to get the ball. And so, you know, he he never he never shows that to the team whether he's frustrated or not. And the thing about Carnell, whether he has a drop or whether I have a bad pass, he never points a finger at nobody. He always comes back with the next play mentality. I think the best thing about him is that, you know, he he wants the ball. And so, when the ball does get thrown his way, he's urgent to it. He he goes up and high points it. There's times where he bails me out when the ball needs to be better. But he he's been great. He may not have had the the splash plays like he always does today, but he's he's going to be a key reason why we're successful on offense. >> What do you say to him on a a day-to-day basis to help him through this first camp? >> I say to him, you know, you're going to have good days and you're going to have bad days, but in the day, you approach each each and every day with the same mindset to get better, the same mindset to make plays from his position. At the end of the day, I mean, control what you can control. He can't control where I'm throwing the ball each and every play. But he can't control how how fast he plays, how much violence he plays with, and you know, just the urgency that he has getting in and out of huddle, getting lined up into his breaks, and then he can control running his routes. So, he's been doing all that. We're going to continue to find ways to give him the ball. But 14, he's going to he's going to be a playmaker for sure. >> Can kind of take us through the last play of two minutes there where it was the clock running down hitting zero is right right after you took the snap and all that kind of just kind of how it unfolded and finding Bell in the corner. >> Uh it was great. Um that was one of our situations that we've been practicing for since the off-season. Um whether in that situation, me and myself, they they say I'm tackled in bounds. We had no more time left, so we got to get on the ball and run our play. Um we had a lot of time on the clock, we were able to get it done. Uh they was trying to sub guys on the field, which I wouldn't know why you would do that in that situation. Um so they were they end up being offsides, probably. Um then they were there was no rush. Um you know, the the old line held up pretty good turn the scrimmage drill, and you know, Bell he worked for us and you know, he made a play. >> You think you would have scored on that play before they marked it down to the one, didn't they? >> Yes. >> Think you would have scored in the game? >> Uh it's practice in the game. Um for sure going to cut it back in there practice. Uh I mean, in the game I'm going to cut it back in there, but in practice we more trying to work the drill, work the situation that we in. So, uh in the game I for sure do think I will. >> And those situations are by design, not not so much as like what you what you're actually trying to work on. >> Right. What you mean? >> Like it's like the the calling it down, you know, it's by time, not >> It is both. Um just depends on the on the I would say where we are um and really what the coach wants to see. So, like sometimes in practice it was just us. So, the coach wanted to see a certain thing or how we handle a certain situation. So, it it's kind of it's kind of yes and no.

title: Jeffery Simmons & Alontae Taylor After the Seahawks Joint Practice
text: There's always things to improve on. But coming off that field, especially that first half of practice, and we were flying around. Uh we talked about it. Take it to the edge. Fast and violent, all gas, no brakes. That's what That's what we saw today, especially on that side. I don't know I didn't see nothing going on on that side. Of course, I was so locked in on our defense side, but I'm I'm very satisfied in the way we attacked the practice today. That's the way um we're talking about being the best defense in the NFL. Going against against us a good offense, I should say, cuz last year was last year. Um our mindset was I mean, we watched the tape. We watched the game against the Cowboys last week. When you turn on the tape, it looked like they wanted to try to be bullies. And when you turn on the tape, you see that, it's like, "Okay, this is all house and that won't happen here." So, we came out with a great mindset today on the defensive side, and I feel like we had a great day. The old BTA. Y'all know what that mean. >> Jordan, the first half, you said first half, do you think they they kind of settled in and maybe adjusted a little bit? >> Man, coming out of the halftime, they got a player or two, especially in the you know, we we especially up front, we got to be able to convert. They came out a out a little bit. I mean, I don't think not in the run game. I would say more in the pass game. We got to be able to convert a little faster, but once after that the first maybe two or three plays, we settled back down and finished the practice the right way. Especially in the two minute, we talked about two minute, you win the game in two minute. Um the first The first play of two minute, we had a pick six. So, just things like that where yeah, sometime that's the nature of the game. We have a halftime, you come out come out a little flat, is how can we come back to the sideline and regroup? And of course, we didn't have the si- We didn't We wasn't able to go to the sideline. We had to figure it out on the go. Um that's how practice goes. So, we figured it out and got right back to where we needed to be. So, we finished practice the right way. >> Because this has been Because this team's been down for the last few years, and you're going against the Super Bowl champs. I know it's just a practice, but does it kind of make a statement that you guys are got a different mindset and a different and a different outlook? >> Listen, man. I I'm a firm believer that you got to prove it again. I don't care about the Super Bowl. We don't care. And that was my That was my message to the team. Who cares? Who cares cuz they won the Super Bowl? We ain't here to It's all standard. Um I don't care how hard knocks. See how it knocks? Like I don't care. They won a Super Bowl, so what? It's about us. The way we The way we attack practice is all standard. We talked about it in the meeting. We talked about fast and violent. I That's what we saw today. I mean, we threw their offensive line went down. I mean, they're the Super Bowl champs. So what? But we came with the right mindset today. Um props to them. I mean, they're a good football team and we got some good work today. Thank God. I mean, it's a little little pushing and shoving here and there, but that's the way joint practice is supposed to be, you know, to be able to get some good work from both sides, but yeah, we didn't care about that. Our mindset was they may be hungry, but we starving. Let's go out here and and continue to continue to starve to get where we really want to get to cuz that's our goal, Super Bowl. >> What you think Hard Knocks >> I'm sure they're going to I'm sure they're going to show only the good plays. I mean, the the two plays that they probably did have a touchdown on, but who cares? Turn on the tape. You guys saw it. I mean, hopefully. Now, I know y'all be on here over with the offense, but you all saw that defense was some good football over there. >> Last week's last week's joint practice to this week. You guys talked about the standard. Do you feel like there was a major incremental or just minimal improvement? >> Oh, we that's I mean, if we if we were the same as last week, we in trouble. Um our mindset is every day we walk into the building and I said, we got one goal, be the best defense in the NFL. And from last week to today, it was a major difference than the way we came out and especially stopping the run and I mean, we playing a lot of man. I mean, that was a big influence of last week coming out of San Francisco. We came man coverage, this and that. Let me ask some guys today, you know, I think you laughing with have one good catch down the field. So, that's that's improvement. So, we we on the same page especially on the defensive side. Um I know we have teammates and then we all on the same page as a whole team, but on that defensive side, we had a great day. >> With that talking about all the talk about last week and man coverage and all that stuff, how did you see those guys respond in meetings and practice? What was the urgency level after all the talk about the recent >> It was interesting. I'll tell you that. I I mean And and then and a lot of that I mean they just like if we in man coverage and they throw a post of 80 yards across the field, that ain't on the DB. That's on us. That's on the front to get to the quarterback. If he could receiver could run from this far red red on this hash to the far hash, that's on the D-line. So, um but to answer your question, I think them guys attacked it with a mindset that, "Okay, people want to challenge us, coach challenge us, Saleh challenge them." I mean, we spent 15 minutes in the team meeting like the O-line and D-line in a board like, "Oh, we bored." But we hearing Saleh talk about man coverage. But not just to the all I mean defense, he's talking to the offense as well. So, when it they made a emphasis from the time we got back to today, them guys took it upon themselves that, "Okay, coach, you want to challenge us, we going to we going to key it into it and get better at it." It walked throughs is all we call man coverage. Practice early this week, man coverage. So, them guys responded well and that's what you expect and want out of the defense. >> Yeah, Saleh just said that he the water bottle he was right to see the starters play in the fourth first half on Sunday night. How do you build on today and what do you all want to see from the starters when you're out there Sunday? >> Fast and violent. We out there so well. I mean, you know, some I and I said it week ago like it's the preseason. I mean, this is my first time playing in the first preseason game in a long time. So, uh last uh last week and it's was one of them you sit there and have thoughts but the game of football. I love this game and when you on the field we expect the same thing. Coach want us play before first half, so be it. We got to go out there and put what we put on tape today. Who knows if they start to play, same thing. Backup, it don't matter. Our standards stay the same. >> Is there an attitude that you guys are kind of developing? I'm sure there's some guys who don't want to be playing on Sunday. Is there an attitude you guys are kind of developing? >> want to play then you shouldn't be in the building. Our mindset is whatever 11 on the field we got to go. It's all gas, no brakes. I think that's the that's the that's the culture we trying to build, that's the foundation we trying to build. And at this point if you ain't bought in when which we know that I mean he told us before the first preseason game before when we first came into training camp that starters, no matter who you are, no matter whoever in this room, be prepared to play in the preseason game. So, if you ain't bought in by now then it's too late. You going to fall off the waist band, so. >> Tell us about the the big play. >> Yeah. Um, coach made a great call. I was playing cloud and um seen Sam go through his progression, knew the ball had to come out and so I just jumped it. >> After a tough week last week, how do you feel you guys went out and redeemed yourself today? >> Good. You know, one thing I can say about this team, man, we we're all about getting better. We understand we got to go through you know, trials and tribulations in order to get better. Can't be on a high all the time, right? I think that's what training camp's about. So, I think we bounced back the right way. >> Jeff talked about Saleh challenging you guys man defense saying that over and over again. I know as a corner, man, that's what you want to do. How do you internalize that, process it and spit it back out? >> You just say thank you. I think you know, you go to coach Saleh and he speaks on that and we're all we're all for the challenge. We want to play man-to-man. And so whenever he tells us, "Hey, this This what we're going to do. We're going to play man. You got to go out there and win. It's a game of inches, a game. You know, we take every advantage of every opportunity we get, win, lose, or draw. We learn from it. I think it'll be it'll be good come season when it is like a crucial moment and he calls man. We know exactly what to do. >> I was kind of joking that that meeting was a little boring for the O-line and D-line. From the DB perspective, of 15 minutes of going back and forth on that, just what do you guys get from that? What does it feel like kind of the coach is focusing on you guys? >> I mean, it just it just lets, you know, he's just putting us out there in front of everybody. Yeah, it was probably boring for those guys, but they understand, you know, what coach Saleh is asking for. And and he's kind of like pointing us out and then he's kind of like making sure that the guys, D-line, O-line, those guys are like holding us accountable. And it's not like there's any surprises to us. So, yeah, it might have been boring for them, but I think that they appreciate it, too, knowing that in front of the whole team coach is calling out the corners. >> You talked about how you guys responded from last week. How important is it to take what you did today and build on that in the next preseason game on Sunday? >> Yeah, very important. You know, we watched the film, we diagnosed the film. I think today was was really good for us against great great team. And now we just, you know, go in, hone in on the good things that we did do. Don't forget about the bad things and, you know, just try to play a complete game come Sunday. >> You guys talked about the standard, you guys want to play at. And of course you last week you guys had a rough go even in the game. Then y'all come out here against a better individual. How how good does that feel getting that kind of bounce back for you guys as cornerbacks? >> It feels good. I think it doesn't matter who who comes in here. I think regardless what team came in here today, we were going to we were going to tighten up and we were going to have a better showing. I think just doing it against those guys just feels a little bit better, right? But the standard is a standard and we want to hold each other accountable to that, no matter what. But we have to be reminded we are humans, right? It's not going to be perfect. Not going to be 100% perfect. And so, glad that we're kind of getting those things out of our system here early on before the season comes where now we're trying to figure out how to figure it out. >> You You an awful lot of ground but that gift on Shaheed. What happened on that play? >> Yeah, I seen a ball go up and in immediately in my mind I said, you know, I think he underthrew it and I was going to go for the ball. As soon as I looked to my left I seen Shaheed in the air and I was like, okay, maybe I'm a little too short. So, I tried to brace, I tried not to It was just kind of like a 50/50 thing and that's why I checked on him at the end. I wanted to make sure he was good. But, just a bang-bang play. >> You ever hit him like that when you guys were teammates? >> Nah, never hit him like that when we were teammates. That's why I apologized to him that play afterwards and then the very next play and he just kept telling me he was good. But, he he knows how I practice and he knows how he practices. >> Does it feel good to bang with those I mean, 2 weeks in a row to get those competitive juices flowing and then also, you know, you got the game on Sunday to try to get it out, you know, even though you're practicing against your own team. How you know, how how how well is it to get it out against a different team? >> Great. You know, I haven't done a lot of joint practices myself. But, it feels really good being able to go against somebody else and try different techniques, try different things and to see how coach calls it calls a practice. But, but it it was really good. Super excited about Sunday. I know everybody else is in the locker room and another opportunity to go get better. We got another week left, right? So, I'll continue to just pound, pound, pound. All gas, no brakes. >> I know you said you haven't done a lot of joint work, but do you like the the 1 day of practice? Do you guys feel like you're getting enough in with cuz typically it's been 2 or 3 days of practice as well. >> Yeah, I think one is more than enough. You know, you don't get a new opportunity come Sunday. You don't get to go play them again on Monday, right? So, go out here joint practice, figure out where you messed up, where you did good at, you know, go watch the tape the next day and then, you know, go play them again on Sunday. That's kind of like your second opportunity versus back-to-back, right? You don't really get a chance to kind of uh uh correct where you were wrong at. So, I think just the 1 day is more than enough. >> How do you personally measure success in a preseason game? >> Man, I think a great question. I think for for myself personally, just was I at the right spot at the right time. Not so much about did he make the play, did he make the play on me, did I make the play, just was I where I needed to be, did I use the right technique, did I play with with good eyes. And I mean as a team, I think just everybody just flying around. I think you got a lot of different people on the field uh just flying around to the ball. And I think if you do that, uh you go to the tape, fix it, correct it, and then come week one, you know, now we can scheme and and have a little good week of practice of first down, second down, red zone, third down, versus now it's just kind of like whatever they throw out there, we got to go out there and play. >> How do you feel like just at this point in camp and you've been players hitting any kind of a camp wall at this stage or >> Um, I think I hit a camp wall my rookie year. Um, I think I think they've done a really good job with with the padded practice the next day is like a walk-through day where guys can hit the cold tubs, hit the hot tubs, get massages, do whatever they need to do to rehab. Um, but but by far I feel like this is probably one of the best as far as guys actually being healthy um throughout training camp and I think guys are a little fatigued here and there, but you know, when we get on the grass, everybody's pushing and going, >> Outside of the challenge, outside of what you say has been the biggest difference from last week to this to this week to see to you know, the better performance and what's it like in the in the DB room? What are you guys saying to each other? >> I think just being tested, man. I think uh you know, our offense tests us right in a different way and then we go we go test against another team and kind of get put in the fire, anxious minds are like different places, different ways. Um, going up against somebody else though, you trying to attack a different way, then you realize, okay, like that didn't work. So, I can't use that going into the next week. So, just trying to figure out what can you use, what you can't use, uh figure out your toolbox, right? I think everybody has a full toolbox of uh of ways to play technique, ways to play certain plays. Um, these are great opportunities to try it against somebody else and if it doesn't work, you throw it away. And if it works, you just add it to the toolbox. So, these are three great opportunities to figure out your toolbox before we get to week one. >> How long has it been at DB? How much How much of your ego goes into, you know, a after a rough game, you sit on it for a week, and then you get a chance to like you said, assess it and then come out, like you said, try to correct those things. How much of your ego goes into that, and then when you get to talk to the coaches, do you dial that back and go to more of a team mindset and unit mindset, or is it still kind of that thing that sticks in the back of your head? >> I think at this stage, um in my personal career, uh year five, I've seen a lot, done a lot, had plays made on me, I've made a lot of plays. I think I'm more now into a space of I'll correct it later, um get to the film room, break it down, figure it out, don't beat myself up too much, give myself grace, um but you know, we kind of joke about it, but like Flo is by far like a great corner to be with, cuz he doesn't allow me to get in my head. I don't allow him to get into his head. Um we correct it, we come out here, we work on it. So, the ego side of it is dismissed off the rip, um but it's just more like how can I get better? Um we understand right now this is all about trying new things. Um I'm going to continue to say that like camp, practice, all that stuff is about trying your toolbox out, figure out what works for you. Um and then later on, you know, we can kind of work on the things that we're really good at and continue to try to get better at the things that we're not so good at. Um but the ego and pride kind of goes out the window, and we just try to figure out how can we get better this week. >> Mhm.

title: Brian Angelichio, Danny Crossman & Patrick Graham Press Conference (August 22) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Brian, what did you see on Will's two interceptions? Were Were they decisions? Were some of the details of the routes not right or anything like that? >> Yeah, I think overall just the execution's got to be better. You know, obviously the quarterbacks are the ones that get, you know, oh, they threw an interception. It goes into their stats, but I think it's it's everybody. You know, it's the it's the offensive line, the runners, the protection, the protection unit, and certainly, you know, the route. So, I think it's it's as an offense, I think we just we have to execute better. I think we all take the blame in that. >> So, Brian, >> Go ahead. >> So, Brian, as you look at Will, like how would you incorporate those interceptions into his overall performance? Like how how do you view how he performed? >> Yeah, I you know, I think what's what's is disappointing is we moved the ball well. I think we had like nine nine-play drive, 11-play drive, and then just didn't execute in the red zone, and certainly we know that's an area that we we need to be better at it certainly if we're you know, for the regular season. That's something we're going to, you know, certainly work on. >> As as you watch Rattler come back here, the issues he's having in pass pro, they more related to technique issues or just the fact that he's coming back from a long layoff and >> Yeah, I think, you know, he's just getting in his try try trying to find his groove, working the right side, the left side. So, you know, we're going to continue to push him and and give him some reps and and see if we can get him to settle in and but I think a lot of that is just getting back and getting out there playing, which is good. It's been good to see him out there and you can see he's getting more and more comfortable. >> After the interception, the first one, Roman didn't try to pursue the the guy that picked him off. Is that something that you guys talk with him when he comes to the sideline? Just that lack of pursuit after the play? >> Yeah, we want you we want all our guys um you know, um running to the ball and you know, Will made a great tackle on that play and you and you saw some guys that were really were really rolling but uh it's you know, it's all our guys. We need to get more of those guys finishing at the end of that. >> And you look at Drew specifically and what he needs to do and work on. Are days like last night where it was a lot of off-platform and a lot of scramble drill kind of things, is that helpful for what you need to see from him or would it be better to see him sort of stand in the pocket and go through progressions? >> Yeah, I think Drew you know, we we certainly um Drew was going through the progressions and they threw a lot of man at us and then the time clocks got off and so then part of that is you know, implementing the scramble drill and you saw he did a great job moving out of the pocket hitting Lake down down on the left side. So you know, that's something you know, we talk about you know, listen to your feet, go through your progressions um and um you know, that's part of playing the quarterback position, you know, then there's a little leakage from your right, you got to slide in the pocket and now uh now it starts to scramble drill. >> We've seen the ways that you've been able to get four quarterbacks reps in practice and training camp settings but as you guys move into the season, you know, as you decide how many quarterbacks and which quarterbacks to keep, how would you determine what reps and the the third and the fourth quarterback on the depth chart would be getting? >> Yeah, that's that's something you know, as far as the season right now we're just trying to get you know, our our our team and roster built and that's something that we'll certainly will talk about as we get into the season when we see where we're at. >> Brian, do you have any expectation for uh Ikaika Aho being available this week and where is he now given the time that he's missed? >> Sure, that that's uh you know, he's been working hard I know with his uh with his rehab and that's something that we'll we'll evaluate you know, each day and and see where he's at but certainly hopeful to get him back. >> How tough is it to evaluate Drew when he's in there with, you know, guys that are down the depth chart and there's a lot of dropped balls, things like that? >> Yeah, I think that's just part of playing the position and learning. So, we're we're I think there's a lot you can gain from it. Just how he handles it, how he moves in the pocket, where his eye discipline is. So, you know, those are all really really good learning ops for him. >> Frank, you've had the same five offensive linemen starting since OTAs. Do you feel that's the group going forward or is there still more competition? >> Yeah, there's still competition. We're we're still, you know, we're 3 weeks away and that that'll continue to uh to be a um, you know, that we'll work through and and where it goes, you know, I think that's that's that'll be decided here in the next couple weeks. >> Did you want to get a longer look at the running game last night and if so, what were your thoughts on the offensive line that night regarding >> Yeah, you know, the one thing we talked about, we just need to get more explosive runs, you know, we didn't get enough explosive runs, but we had, you know, we had a lot four or five yard runs and you know, converted on three third and ones, but yeah, just looking to get some more explosive runs down the field. I think that'll help, but it was consistent, you know, just wasn't those chunks and that's where we're we're hoping to improve on. >> You had the fullback in for two of those third and ones. You see what you want to see from 37? >> Yeah, you know, we're just trying to move Riley around. You see him playing on the line of scrimmage. You saw him playing in the backfield. I thought he I thought he did a good job, you know, he had he had some snaps on the line. I thought he he showed some get off and some snap and then certainly did a good job inserting on a couple of those lead schemes. So, you know, happy with where his progression's gone. >> What did you see out of Caleb getting more chances last night? What do you like and like just overall performance of >> What's that? Say it again. >> What what do you like out of Caleb's performance last night? What did you see out of him with more chances that he got? >> Yeah, I think any you know, anytime you um you know, like with all the guys, just continuing to give guys ops and and looking to see steady improvement and where they grow from play to play and how they how they um you know, how they perform, right? Especially when you get runners, right? They need ops, right? We try we try to give them all a chance to get, you know, the you know, Jaylen and Rico, they I think they got five and four carries or four five and five and then you know, giving KJ chance to to roll a little bit more from the week before. So, that's we're trying to give them all a chance to go out and prove what they can do. >> Yeah, I was going to ask you about Jaylen and Rico. First chance to see those two on the field together and work in that rotation. What did you think of how it played out? >> Yeah, you know, we love the love the way they the the two work together. Uh you know, their mindset for the game and uh you know, they need to you know, get their reps, too, right? To get them game ready and that's what we're continuing to hope, but it was good to see them both out there. >> So, you tried to do some tempo at one point. What's your philosophy on that and how do how do you feel like you guys have been at trying to to implement >> Yeah, just trying to you know, when you when you see you can trap a defensive personnel on the field or help get us in a rhythm, just getting some tempo calls, calls that we know and just being able to go to the line and kind of regulate the defense, but uh and that and that's something, you know, obviously when you get into the two-minute, you know, we were in it probably more than we wanted to be in the fourth quarter, you know, with the way the score went. So, uh you saw a lot more of that in the fourth quarter and then had some of it sprinkled in in the second half and you know, it's always going to be a change up, always be a part of who we are. >> When it comes to when it comes to splitting carries in the backfield, different staffs do it different ways, you know, in terms of which position coach or coordinator head coach determines who's playing on a specific play. How does this staff choose to to do that? >> Yeah, we we you know, obviously going in we wanted to have designated carries for Rico and and um Jaylen with play time, but um you know, that's with all our positions. Like there may be certain plays, whether it's a receiver, tight end, you may tag a number you want that guy in, but uh we'll always have a plan going in of how we're going to use the guys, how we see the reps. Um so, you know, you don't want to overuse somebody as well. So, that's always something we talk about. >> Brown, what are you guys looking at as far as whether the offensive line needs to clean up in pass protection, you know, from first team to second team, whatever, but you know, what are the things you guys been able to identify like, "Hey, we need to do these specific things better right now." >> Yeah, I mean, obviously, you know, pass protection is um you know, essential and then part of that goes into, you know, where's the quarterback's drop, how deep is he in the pocket, you know. So, those are something we're always trying to clean up. What was the protection adjustment? Could we have slid it this way or that way? So, those are all factors that go into and then where's the running backs' helps? They got they're they're you know, they're going to help on their releases and where they can be have the edges protected. So, all that goes into the protection plan and that's something, you know, as we get into the season, you're certainly going to game plan and make sure you're you're taking care of you know, their their their rushers. >> So, what are what are some of the biggest uh coaching points you have for for Will after after his after his performance last night? >> Yeah, you know, Will you know, Will's played a lot of football and um we'll look at the tape and and there's areas that we we all can be better, you know, um and I think you know, you'll see the the growth from that and I think anytime you uh get a chance to um see the tape, see where we could be better, uh whether it's Will or whether it's another player, I think that's all healthy. >> We talked to Will after the game, one thing he did talk about as far as positive take away was the ability to identify and and call the right protections. Did you see that >> Oh, yeah. >> quarterbacks doing a good job? >> Yeah, they they they they uh they've done a good job with that. Um, you know, uh picking up a couple of their overload pressures, adjusting it. Um, and that's that's been something that's been a real positive. >> Brian, there's been a lot of talk about Roman in camp. How do you feel like he's taken what he's done on the practice field onto these into these two games? >> Yeah, I think Rome's, you know, uh, continuing to grow and get better. And I think the more we we continue to have him out there, you see him playing inside, you see him playing outside. I think that's all those are all good, you know, cuz he's just hasn't just been a guy that's playing outside the numbers, you know, he's been inside, he's been in the slot, he's been outside, he's been moving around. And that's where we want to continue to push with all our receivers. So, it allows us to play the game on our terms. >> As you guys prepare for this this last preseason game, what will you be looking for from the guys that are in that running back three competition right now? >> Yeah, we haven't, you know, we'll we'll get together as a staff and and, you know, obviously with coach and and talk about what that game's going to look like and how we want the, you know, the rotations to go. But we haven't, you know, we haven't, talked about that yet. >> Brian, Jeremy played a lot more outside this week than he did last week. What did you see in kind of his first game actually playing outside? >> Yeah, you know, that's, you know, he's been, you know, asked to do that. So, I thought Germ did a good job as far as, you know, doing his job, his assignments. I ultimately the start of the game falls on me in terms of just having those guys ready to go. So, I mean, that's what I'm going to tell them when we get in there and we meet. I'm like, "Listen, I got to do a better job. Obviously, I didn't do my job well enough to have you ready to go. That's That's where it starts. I mean, I'm not going to run from it, hide from it. And then we're going to work today to improve. I mean, we're going to spend time watching that drive as a group. And then probably watch about 30 more plays together as a group, making sure the communication, making sure everybody's on the same page for the vision in terms of when I call a defense, what we're looking to de- fend that particular play. But, ultimately, when it gets to the beginning of the game, I mean, as the coordinator, I got to do a good job of having them ready to go. We spend a lot of time on that, and that was that was That's on me. >> When we talked to Andy Weidl last week, he was saying that Super Bowl teams he's been on, they had two waves of defensive linemen. Where do you feel like you guys are at in terms of establishing depth at that position? There's from that D-line OLB room, there's going to be a lot of NFL players from those rooms. So, whether they're on our team or another team, they mean there there's some good players on the We We have a good situation right now. And I think the biggest thing is getting them all to understand how we want to play up front. You know, I think they they I don't think I know they hear it from me in terms of the physicality standpoint, you know, playing with extension, coming out our hips, knocking the line of scrimmage back. Next time, when it's pass rush, I deem that we're keying the ball and we're trying to gain ground and create space. I want those guys hunting people out of the stack. I want it to be a problem if you catch the ball underneath. I want them to feel us and I'm going to make that very clear today. And just And I got to do a better job coaching it. And just And just cuz they want to and it's been an identity of this defense um in this building and this town for a long time and you know, I think it's our job, and especially mine, um to make sure point out when it's not up to the standard and make sure we let's go. They're the examples. >> And Y.A. has a little bit of a different role this year. How would you evaluate his camp and what does he have to improve on to solidify his role in the organization? >> Again, the thing I love about Y.A. is his energy. You see that. Um I think his role is he's a he's improving as a young defensive player in the league, you know, seeing the blocks, understanding how they're trying to block them. Um playing with extension, you know, coming out of his hips more so that we can get him on the other side of the line of scrimmage. Those are the things I I talked to him about and told him about and I mean, he's he's doing his best to and he's giving his best effort and he's working on it every day. So, I I I really enjoy him. I I really enjoy being around him, too. I know I know I say that about a lot of the guys, but we got some good dudes that happen to love football. So, I mean, I mean, shoot. I mean, I'm a coach. I love that. >> Patrick, you brought in some different pieces in the secondary during camp. Do you feel like you have the type of competition that are going to create difficult decisions? Like, is that group kind of where you want it at this point? >> Uh, it's I mean, you know, the job Omar and those guys do in personnel and coaching, those guys make decisions there. I I like where the competition's going. Um, it's it's always positive when it's really competitive and it's not clear-cut. So, I really like it. Guys are fighting and clawing for playing time. Guys are fighting and clawing to be productive out there, but they're all doing it within the scope of a brotherhood. You know, it's just it's really enjoyable to sit there in the room I'm up in front of the defense and see how they're coaching each other or talking about a certain point and challenging each other. I mean, it's it's one of the best rooms I've been a part of in terms of that. The open discussion, how open they are with one another. Um, they don't include me on the text chain, but that's okay. That's okay. But, I mean, I'm sure it's I mean, it's you know, they give me a hard time. I love what's going on in that room. That's a credit to Simo. That's a credit to Joe. Those guys working. I mean, they they created a really cool environment in that room. >> Patrick, but you have any issue with going into the regular season not having seen Porter and Ramsey? >> They're really good football players. They So, they're going if they go into the regular season, they're going to practice at some point. So, yeah, do I have an issue with it? No. mean, again, really good football players out there on the field as many as possible. And you know, I mean, again, you know, just when they get to practice, they get to practice, but that's our job to get them prepared. It doesn't matter. I mean, it's no different than when you get during the season, somebody you trade for somebody and they come on a Tuesday and if if we're going to play them, we're going to play them. That's the our job. And again, I always talk about nobody really feels sorry for us if we have to get it done in 4 days, 3 days, 2 weeks, whatever it is. So, we just accept the challenge. It's the NFL. I mean, and it's not unique to us. That's what it is never unique to us. There's 32 31 other teams having to deal with the same thing. >> You talked about the box versus the sideline. What's your history there? >> The white versus the seeing in the box versus the sideline. What's your history there? What are some of the pros and cons? [clears throat] >> So, aside from the Snickers joke, I mean, I mean, that's haven't had a Snickers yet, but you know, popcorn. We had popcorn this time. Um, but it's it's one, it makes it easy for me to see the offensive personnel. So, that anybody that's done offensive personnel for me, they're always probably the coach that has to do that, they're probably thankful when I'm up in the box cuz it's less, "What is it? What is it? What is it?" You know, cuz you know, I'm like, and then you tell them after the game, "Hey, I'm just saying that." They're like, "Well, it doesn't sound like you're just saying that." >> [laughter] >> So, that that's number one. So, that makes it is a lot easier to do that. And it's just more calm down there up there. You know, and so, like, you know, you got your sheets spread out there, you know, you're going to your different grids to make your calls, but um, but the it starts with having trust with the coaches down on the field. And so, having a familiarity with Simo is big. I know having a familiarity with Scott is big because, you know, you're trusting them to get the message. And then, as I'm working through with new coaches, whether it's CJ, Pecco, Shawn, you know, them getting a feel for what I need conveyed down there to the players. So, but it I would say me being in the box is about being comfortable for me, but it's also, you know, it's a credit to the assistant coaches that can convey the message for me and then, you know, rally the guys when we need to rally them. That's why, you know, you watch practice, I'm encouraging and coach does a good job of this, be involved, be involved cuz again, they're the ones that are going to be touching them on game day. So, whenever we hit that practice field, we're really training for the game. >> Do you prefer to operate in in chaos or in calmness? What's your >> NFL is chaos. I mean, it's chaos, but I think through our preparation, like you try to prepare yourself to be calm in chaos. I guess, I mean, again, I I would never I don't make an analogy or anything with war or anything like that, but you want to be able to be calm when it is chaotic, but recognize that it is chaotic at times. But, I think through our prep preparation, that gets you ready, a state of readiness that, you know, and then experience as well, you know, 8 years, each year is new, but 8 years of doing this, you know, I don't know if I would want me calling the game, the guy that was calling the game a year 8 years ago. That's what stands out to me and I know he spent a lot of time, you know, whether it's talking with TJ, Alex, those guys, working with CJ. The hand violence and just trying to make sure everything's coordinated. And then the next step is going to be really truly understanding the rushing and how we can manipulate the the protection. That's really a big point of what I That's what I think part of my job is here with him. Um but you you see that I mean the quickness, the upper body flexibility, the the athleticism it it's all positive. And then you know, he does love football. He does love football and I think a big um trait that people miss out on when you start to ascend as a pass rusher is the relentlessness of it. Like not stopping. You know, and he has some good examples on the team to learn from, but he has that trait. Um serious seriousness about his craft, you know, and very coachable. title: QB THOUGHTS, Drew Allar, Will Howard learning experiences, OL struggles, Defense | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to Steelers Rewind here on pennlive.com. Nick Farabaugh here with you all. The Pittsburgh Steelers did not have a practice today, but we did talk to Danny Crossman, Steelers special teams coordinator Brian Angelichio, Steelers offensive coordinator, and Patrick Graham, Steelers defensive coordinator today about the team's preseason game and where it stands. Um I think Angelichio, you know, a guy that's very low-key in his presser, is not going to reveal a ton to you. But one thing I did think he revealed um was, you know, those Will Howard interceptions. How do you go about that process of correcting those? Obviously, you got to throw it out of the memory bank, but also it's not just Will, right? Sure, both those throws I think were substandard and not something they wanted, but, you know, Rowan Wilson, the details on the routes, the pass protection at large over the entire game was poor. I think the O-line play definitely is something that we can talk about as a real bad thing. With Rudolph, you know, I I thought Angelichio kind of made a good point where he said he listened to his feet. I thought he did. I thought sometimes, you know, Drew was able to make plays out of structure where there wasn't really anything. I thought the throw to McFarland was really nice. There were two or three others. There were also two plays where I think he probably should have gotten rid of the ball and took two sacks. Um the third sack he took was just like I think it was the second sack actually. Driscoll just got absolutely abused and he had no shot. But you know, he had a dump-off to Eli on the one and then Weitzman was over the middle. Not like super wide open. The ball probably could have come out though. Um so you know, there's an emphasis I think on pocket movement with both those guys, pluses and minuses. But it's a preseason game. Let's not make a large declaration on either of these guys just yet. It's a preseason game. There's definitely negatives from that. There's positives for both of them. But let's not bury these guys because of one preseason game, right? Just like we can't anoint them for last week's preseason performance. It's a give or a take. Don't ride the roller coaster. I did think Patrick Graham made a few good points about the defense talking just about how these guys that have come on mid-training camp, Atlanta Robinson, Rayshawn Jenkins, had such great games against the New York Jets, and he's really proud of those guys, but that's because they've been studying, and they've been very focused, and the communication feels like it has been very open with those guys, and he took responsibility for that first drive where Geno Smith marched that starting Jets uh offense right down the field. Um but they were without, you know, six or seven starters the Steelers were, but still, you don't want, you know, a blown coverage in the flat that allows them to score from 13 yards out. You don't want third-down conversions on third and longs. Um so, there's some things and details to clean up, and Patrick Graham took mainly the blame for that. Um but I I do think that was interesting. We talked with um with Brian Angelico a little bit just about um Jeremy Bernard, you know, quiet game, had one target. Um but a guy that can play outside because of his play strength in addition to his quickness. Um that's something that they saw from him. You know, they see how quick he is up the line of scrimmage, and they also see how he plays through contact, how he plays, you know, when guys get their hands on him, how he plays through these really traffic-filled areas in the middle of the field. Just a lot of positives, you think there, but felt like overall, you know, from what Mike McCarthy said last night through the coordinators, just a lack of detail and a lack of execution from the team at large. And that's not just, you know, a quarterback thing, that's not an O-line thing. It just feels like it's a whole team thing in many respects. And so, I think the lack of detail and execution overall on this football team last night really showed when you watch the film. Um and so, we'll see where things go. The the quarterbacks get a chance to kind of bounce this back and rewire it, and they have a game on Thursday. So, throw it out the wayside, watch the film, take your breaks from it, and and kind of understand what you got to do and move from it. I think it's good to a degree that you Riler and Will Howard had some rough tape. No matter the surroundings around them, no matter what their decisions were, um having things that you can learn from in the processes where everything is not perfect and curated for you, it's really good film to have. So, folks, make sure like, comment, subscribe, turn on the notification bell for more, and thanks for watching. I'll be back on Monday.

title: Klay Kubiak and 49ers Players Address the Media Following Day 16 of Camp | 49ers
text: All right.
