And I think that's part of his goal is uh and it's part of his game is, you know, he loves to talk. He loves to get under QB's under their skin and try and throw them off their game. And um he obviously lost that battle today. So, it was nice to see. when you're blocking in in the running game and you have a running back like Kalon who seems to hit the hole so quickly and decisively. Do do you feel that like do you >> like how what's that dynamically? >> Uh it just means I mean obviously we want to hold our blocks as long as possible. That's our goal. that's not our man my man type of type of deal where um but when you get a running back who's hitting the hole faster than um you know kind of what you're expected usually you can feel the timing within a play um and when he's beating you there uh and slashing defenders instead of you know shaking in the hole it makes it a lot a lot easier on us and then also it just helps the flow of the offense and the way that we're timing things out. >> You see that play today where I think he like ran into Bindle like knocked Brendle over. I mean, is that I don't know. Is that something that's sort of unexpected or do you have to like get the feel of that with the with the running back like that? >> No, it's part of feel also maybe open your eyes, but um no, it's just collisions happen and if we're in the wrong place, the wrong time, you know, then as long as he's running hard, um tell him to maybe miss him next time, but um you know, I'm not telling him to change anything. Keep running hard. >> What do you think of Willis so far? How hard is it to change positions as you're trying to break into this level? >> It's extremely hard. Um I went through it as a rookie. Didn't work out for me and finally got back out. Um but he strung you know a few good practices together and it was a little bumpy at the start but um he's looking a lot better start. It's just hard when you come into this offense you're told to run and college is not it's not a thing. It doesn't happen. A lot of RPOS's just guys are grabbing onto each other and kind of walking off the line with this offense. We're told to run. So uh it's a steep learning curve for young guys. um he's got all the tangibles to to be able to run and be a guard in this offense. So, um the faster that he picks up on running um you know, getting to the second level, it's that's going to be the big thing for him, but he's looking good. >> How do you feel uh your camp's going? You've been there every day and just >> now that you've been in the system long enough, what what does it feel like for you right now? >> Um feels pretty good. It's nice to have uh consistency obviously on our side with Dom. Um missing there for a week, but uh when you can have someone next to you for three years now. Um build consistency, that relationship. I know what he's doing. He's know he knows what I'm going to do. Um and just my game where it's at, how I'm feeling technique-wise. Um excited for this year again. Um but to have him at a level of where he's at confidence-wise, uh and his understanding the offense helps me. Um, and obviously we get to have a lot of fun out there, too, throwing guys around. So, um, it's going to be exciting year for for me and him. >> How much can a vet help a rookie that's next to him? I know what's happening on the left side is on the other side, >> but you kind of had it with Pun. Is can Trent help Willis if he's in that position? >> Yeah. >> As the games are actually happening. >> Yeah, I mean, you're never going to be able to recreate a game. I mean, the only way you get better at football is playing football. Um, so it's those little moments after a play or in practice that something happens, um, whether it's negative, positive, but you can learn from it. And obviously you pull the guy aside and be like, "Hey, like here's something I would think about on this play if it's, you know, he missed a block, whatever." Just take him and coach him through on like why he missed it or like here's something that can help you get through that next time. And obviously, you don't want to see that correction again. So [snorts] the faster that that correction gets made and then it doesn't happen again, the faster you can evolve as a player. And then it shows that, you know, he's listening to kind of what coach is saying and then the tips that you're giving him. Then it's like, all right, you know, I'm going to pour more into this guy. Uh, that's what I got to see with Dom. And then that's what we want to see out of Carver. >> Thompson. Uh, I know you guys offensive lineman, no defensive lineman. Thompson, you don't go against Thompson, but he's had some incredible one-on- ones. What What's your viewpoint of what he's done? >> Uh, pretty good. At the beginning of camp, it looked like he should be on our side of the ball. Uh we didn't really know, you know, you kind of look at him like, "All right, who's this guy? What's he about?" Uh and then you watch the preseason games and he's bowling guys and getting pressure. He's making plays in the run game, fighting off double teams. Um I think he got to go against us a little bit today, too. So like you see the one-on- ones, like the guy flashes. Um it's not something that you would expect looking at him. Um but I mean, the guy just he's finding a way to make plays and and that's what you want out of guys like that. They surprise you. Um, and you know, if he can help this team, then heck yeah, man. >> Sweet. Thanks, guys.

title: Raheem Morris and 49ers Players Address the Media Following Day 15 of Camp | 49ers
text: Afternoon, guys. >> How you doing? >> You guys are taking off for Australia uh a week from Wednesday. I I be honest, I can't even think about that yet. I've been uh thinking about tomorrow. But uh >> I just ask whether that affects your preparation for this third game. Is it any different just knowing that you have to have that that week one lineup pretty much set? >> I'm really I'm kind of like in the evaluation period for the most part anyway. So like, you know, for all these games is more about evaluation, running what we run, you know, going out and executing the things that we do that we've been doing in practice. I haven't really, you know, schemed up or anything or done anything that way anyway. So, it's kind of normal, you know, whether we're leaving for Australia or whether we playing at home, it wouldn't have mattered. >> I mean, what did you think of the performance of your defense on Thursday night? >> Um, it was a great bounceback performance for those guys to be able to fit and be able to hit and to play with our style and our standard and all those things. You know, we didn't have a great practice, so to watch those guys really respond, you know, to the meeting, to the preparation, to the all the things that we had to do to go out there and play was nice. So watching those guys go out there and play fast and physical, um, I really enjoyed. There's always going to be things to clean up. You know, we had a couple things to clean up that we went through the process and we had a to do those things, but you're really fired up about, you know, some of the statistical achievements and some of the things that the guys were able to do from a physical standpoint. >> What were maybe specifics you think that did improve and had to improve from Tuesday to Thursday? >> No, everything, you know, it was just football, you know what I mean? So like, uh, you know, some of the stuff was realistic, some of it was not. So you get a chance to go out there and play real football and tackle is is awesome. you know, when you're going through and doing some of the things that you see from a naked eye from from practice, it always feels worse. So, it always feels better. Um, but none of that really matters. It's all about getting better every single day. I think the most important thing is that um the growth and the steady improvement sometimes you need days like that. You know, you never heard little adversity always helps you and that was that was a little adverse moments for us to be able to bounce back and do some real good things and I like how the guys responded. I think that was critical. I think that was key. Um I think that's a learning lesson that you can take from the preseason and and apply that into the regular season. Did you do more upfront with your defensive line in terms of movement, stones, what have you in the game to help out your overall defense compared to what you guys did on in the practice? >> No, sir. We just called normal stuff. You know, didn't want to do anything to you're not trying to win that. You just want to you just want guys to get better and that's what guys did when I was able to execute some things and, you know, able to go out there and communicate better. Um, able to go out there and play better, able to go out there and work together better. um the standard of play, you know, um the the the situational awareness on everything I think I think was at a higher level and it was better um for whatever reason, you know, like you can sit here and make all kinds of excuses, but nobody really cares. But I did like the fact that we had to go through some adversity debris to bounce back. >> We're seeing a lot of Jaden Duggar out there. Obviously played a lot. Where do you see his role right now? Is he is he in the rotation maybe right off the bat? you know, it's always in the making, you know, like um you hope the best players and are the best players are going to be out there and and that's what you're going to do. You try to find ways and ways people can help the football team and um he's finding his role. He's finding his niche. He's doing some really good things and there's a lot of guys doing really good things. You know, Tatum Pun, Nick Martin, um you know, obviously the two guys that hadn't played yet. Um that there there are a lot of really good things on the football team and they're making really hard decisions, you know, uh for our management and for our coaches and for everybody involved. So, um, I'm excited to be able to get those guys to the situation that you can game plan and actually do the fun things that you were kind of talking about and alluding to. Um, we just not at that stage yet, but I'm really excited about these guys. >> That that position possibly the SAM or fever, whatever you're calling it, whatever it is, is that something >> I don't even think I gave it a name. I think you guys have like every other week, >> you know, we kind of talk about it and you kind of talk about the the the the changing position and you've seen a bunch of different people be able to do it. So, that's been kind of um fun in itself, you know, really for me. And I didn't mean to cut you off is really like interchangeable parts, you know, guys that can do multiple things, serve multiple roles um for a different a bunch of different reasons, you know, for whether it be um competitive advantage, uh whether it be um to get through and deal with injury, uh whether it be to find out how far you can push a guy and take a guy to a different level. I think all those things come into play. So, I think um it's been really nice to see a lot of those young guys and other guys be able to bounce around, do some of those things. >> I hope that answer your question. I'm not sure. >> Does Doug have a skill set that seems to fit that position? Yeah, he was one of the guys, you know, we drafted, you know, kind of for those kind of super roles, you know, like, uh, those guys that can kind of, you know, he was one of the fortunate people that actually rushed a passer before in college. You seen him off the ball, cover in college. You seen him on the ball before. You seen him do a bunch of different things. You see him in the secondary. Um, you seen him do a bunch of different things in college that he was able to translate those skill sets over to what we're talking about. >> The Ram like the Rams running as much stuff as they did last year with three tight ends. Does that factor into sort of the evaluation of Duggar and how you >> everything? I wouldn't give credit to the Rams for that. But a lot of the stuff that was built, I did a lot of the stuff at the Rams, right? And then we've been able to practice against each other and then some of the things that the Rams kind of evolved into going from their national 11 to the 13 that they did last year. And then they got all different personnel groupings, but interchangeable pieces that we kind of utilized for a long time, whether they've been Atlanta, whether they've been, you know, just all over my different stops. But being able to utilize those pieces definitely comes into play when you're talking about like no different than what has been done here in the Bay, you know, with the athletic skill sets of the linebackers with, you know, all middle linebackers didn't run 44 and cover routes down the field like the way Fred does and he's definitely one of those special players like that and you kind of surround yourself with those type of people. >> Couple more. >> Does Jaylen Strowman in any way stand out to you, Raheem? >> Uh, you know, as a young man that's that's come in here and done a really nice job. you know, obviously, um, you see the flash plays, you see, um, the things that happened in practice with him, you see how he's going out there and playing at a high level and doing a nice job for us. You know, I think, you know, no different than that linebacker group. You see a bunch of different people flashing, whether it's been our starters and right now being, you know, TIG and Seek or whether that next group's going out there and done a really nice job being able to do some different things. What are you talking about Ashton? What are you talking about? At at certain times when you get a chance to put Neil Suran back there. Um there there are a bunch of different guys that's flashing a bunch of different ways and he's one of them. Um and that's a credit to the organization. That's a credit to the group. That's a credit to the standard from the defense and the coaching staff here. >> What's going on back up Mike? Is that in competition? We're seeing Wallo get obviously started. Is he competing with Bthoon? Is he ahead of Bthoon right now? >> That is a great question. Um they've both played extremely well. I it's hard to knock some of the stuff that they both been able to do. Wallow, you know, went went bananas this week, making a bunch of tackles, did a lot of look at things the week before um and has been um throughout the course of the offseason. Um Tatum obviously couldn't practice throughout the course of the offseason coming back off this the injury um that he's been able to bounce back back in the role. You've seen his feet get underneath him. Um you've seen him do some really physical things out there from a standpoint from um when we're talking about the games when he's able to rush the passer last week and beat the back and do a bunch of different things there. They both got the skill set to be able to go out there and play. Mike, you know, obviously is our backup Mike because of who Fred is, but that gives you that overall comfort that we talked about having guys been to play different positions and having those guys being able to move around like that is certainly um something that you welcome. What did you think of your young defensive line, Alfred Collins, uh out there during the >> You know, Alfred just gotten back off the injury. You know, he's got, you know, you could tell the last couple of days he's starting to get better and better. You know, getting his feet back underneath him. That's always the hardest thing when you're talking about a big man. Um being able to utilize his hands and obviously hands for those guys come last. Um but you're starting to see him come back and do some really good things. Um who else is young out there? Uh Romelo, um you know, picked it up a little bit more this game. Um he's been showing flashes in practice and doing a lot of great things in practice. He showed a little bit of flash in the first game, showed a little bit more of this game, and he's still got more left out there. So, um there's more meat in the bone, so to speak, to quote Johnny Holland, but like he's got some stuff out there for us that we really love. Um he's got a lot out there that we that we're liking right now. So, it's been fun to watch these guys grow. Um particularly with a bunch of the guys that, you know, have been out that haven't been able to practice. So, watching these guys get more and more reps for themselves. >> Romelo, during the draft process, it seemed like he was put into this box as like a designated pass rusher. He had that the speed off the edge. um in what you've learned about him over the last several months um how has he kind of grown into how you view him, you know, in this defense? >> I would say 100% right with the box that you mentioned, you know, from from the from the draft evaluation standpoint when it talked about filling that designated pass rusher role um to really replace what they did last year with sort of like huff, right? And that was a box check for us. And then it was that other thing we talked about where he can potentially be, you know, this guy that can walk around, spin, do some different things as well. Um, so that was a a question mark box that he's been able to check and do a lot of things for us there. And then be able to watch him come in and play a physical brand that he's been able to play. You know, he does have some rundown. He does have some some real knock him back when it comes to being able to go out there and stop the run and play at a physical level. Um, which has been fun to watch, you know, particularly in the games. Um, and that's that's been nice. Um, he brings a certain amount of quickness. You probably referring to the play that you saw him make when he made the inside move um throughout the course of the week, but it wasn't new. He we did a little bit last week. He's just able to utilize it and get an opportunity to do it and make that play. So, um I'm I'm really fired up where he's going. Um and it's fun to watch these young guys grow. We kind of talked about it with Price Cycle a couple weeks ago where you take a step in that joint practice and then you watch him go into the games and you watch the confidence build and you've watched his confidence build throughout the course of this training camp as well. So, it's been it's been fun to watch a lot of our young guys. >> Thank you guys. >> Have a good one, guys. Look at the tape. What did you think of your performance? >> Uh, I would say I had a a solid day. Um, still some things to clean up on. Um, you know, playing the first game in the NFL is definitely big. I'm just blessed to be out there and, you know, playing a game that I love. a few weeks into training camp now. Can you speak to the the difference in intensity and college practices versus NFL practices? >> Yeah, definitely. Um, both very intense. Uh, but I'll say in the NFL is more, you know, even more about the details. Um, I came from a program that was really key on the details, but in NFL it's even more. It's a whole different level. Um, especially coming in as a rookie. Um, just learning the offenses, um, learning blocking schemes. Um, especially in our offense as well where it's a lot of complicated schemes. So, you know, just coming in knowing that everything is way more intense. >> Is the last piece of the puzzle getting in the the pass game. It look like they were making a concerted effort in this practice to to nail that down for you. >> Yeah, definitely, man. Uh really just allound game, you know, in the run game, pass game, um and just making sure that everyone is really keyed into what they're supposed to be doing um to help the offense, you know, flow as good as it can. >> Seems like you've really picked up on pass concepts here in the preseason. Um did it help at Indiana? um with that transition just the you mentioned emphasis on details. >> Yeah, I would definitely say it helped uh coming from a system that we did and you know having to scan and just being keyed in to certain people um even in the league you know having to be keyed into the details um seeing safety shells and paying attention to linebackers seeing different tails and things of that nature. Um, I also have a very detailed coaching, Bobby Turner. Um, he's very, you know, hard on me and making sure that I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing on the field and, um, he's very he has very high expectations for me and, you know, I'm I'm up for the challenge. >> Get on you about the most specifically, >> man. My my tracks, you know, just being very detailed into every single thing, you know, being in the right spot before the play and even after the play, very big on landmarks and, you know, just being, you know, the best all-around football player that you can be. um just being focused at all times and you're never having those brain farts. >> When you say landmarks, are you talking about like the wide zone and and just getting out far enough before you you cut it back in? >> Really just the all-around game, especially in our offense um in terms of, you know, certain areas on the field um where the ball is supposed to, you know, cut back to where it's actually supposed to be as opposed to where it'll end up after the play is going on. So, little things like that. you had a great college career and and yet they didn't invite you to the combine. How how much did that serve as maybe a little extra motivation for you? >> Uh in my mind I would say a lot. But you know I'm I'm a man of not much words. So I just use it as that motivation to you know just keep me going each and every day. Um staying prayed up talking to the Lord each and every day you know give me the strength the motivation to just keep going and you know just being me at the end of the day never letting you know outside noise get to me and you know just always playing hard playing ferocious. about your teammates have talked about you kind of have an advanced understanding of outside zone where you're not afraid to kind of hit the hole, put your foot in the ground and go. Where where does that come from? Is that just over years of of working it or is it is there kind of an innate ability for you to see it and and just go? Uh >> I would definitely say just time put in, you know, just being focused to the details. Um I ran a lot of outside zone at Indiana. Um and even at James Madison with the same coach. So, you know, just being used to it, but also just knowing that you you're on a different level now. This is the pro leagues, so you have to stick your foot in the ground. you have to get vertical and um you want to impose your will on everybody regardless of who it is. >> Coach Miller, you had him at JMU, you also had him at Indiana. How much do you credit him for the fact you're standing here right now? >> Man, a lot man. That's my guy. Um when I when after I got drafted, I talked to him. He was the first person I called because I told him, man, I was I want to be the first one that you have drafted. And you know, I was. And I just got to give all credit to God, you know, for putting me in this position. Um, and you know, credit to God for having given me a coach like him to allow me to, you know, grow um over time and just be me. >> Thank you all. Jaden, what's it been like trying to process everything that's been thrown at you since you got here? You're learning all of these different positions. Um, what's that been like for you? >> I mean, uh, when a coach ask you to do something like that, you know, it get very challenging, but I mean, this is something I was asked to do in college, too. So, like, I'm kind of used to it. So, I mean, I just learned how to study multiple positions at one time. So, I've been I've been able to keep up with it pretty well. >> After watching the film, what did you think of your performance on Thursday >> Uh, I mean, I feel like I did pretty well. I mean, some stuff to always clean up, just little technique stuff. I mean, just trying to get better, just critiquing myself hard. But, I mean, I feel like I'm getting better and better each week by week. So, I mean, it's a that's a positive in itself right there. So, >> feel different than it looks afterwards. >> Uh, yeah. Yeah, I feel like early in the game I came out like I was a little too jittery. I feel like I had to calm myself down. So looking back at film, just seeing film, I feel like I like over time as the game went on, I feel like I created some of my mistakes. So >> got more comfortable as the time went on. >> For sure. Yeah. >> What's been the most difficult part of this transition for you to this level? >> Uh most difficult part uh I mean it's always tough to learn a whole different scheme. I mean that in itself. So that's the hardest part I would say. Not really physically, nothing like physically too hard, but just learning the scheme, trying to stay in my books, just learning multiple positions at one time. That's probably what I would say. >> You kind of came in like pretty NFL ready in terms of like the plays you're making, how impressive you're playing right now. What What has kind of played into that? Like where do you feel you are right now? I mean just working just putting in work and being confident in myself and then my coaches and teammates just putting out confidence in me as well just let me know I can do it and then just making plays in practice like like you build your confidence up so you know like all right I can go do this in a game too. So just doing all that stuff combined right there just make me very comfortable out there on the field. >> How do you learn from Dre Greenlight and Fred Warner or what is something you want to learn from them? >> I mean I learned a lot from them just especially technique stuff. I mean I was here with them the whole summer. I didn't go home. So, I stayed out here all summer with Fred and Dre. So, I just learned so much from them. Just what to expect out of certain stuff, just certain techniques, just a lot of stuff. So, just picking up stuff from those bets and those the two best linebackers. So, it's been good for me. >> One of the only rookies that stayed from OTAAS and rookie mini camp through >> uh there was a there was a couple rookies out here. Uh I can't really remember. It was a couple months ago now, but I wasn't the only one. Do you have a like a list of questions for Fred and Dre like when you first got here or what was it like? I mean those two guys had just a ton of experience between the two of them. >> Uh no honestly I kind of wanted to feel them out first you know I didn't really know. I never got to meet them so when I got to meet them and they were very welcoming. So like I didn't really have a list of questions but just naturally learning the defensive question about the game just seeing film I asked questions but I didn't come in with a list of questions. DJ Wright like as a linebacker's coach? >> I mean, he's a great coach. Uh, I mean, that's a coach who like who believes in you. You know, he believes in you. He builds you up. So, that's like one of the most important things that you can ask for, a coach who believes in you. But, he also like when you mess up and when you don't do what you're supposed to do, he's going to let you know. So, it's a it's like he's a good coach. It's a good balance of telling you need to hear and then telling you to clean up. >> how much interaction do you get with Johnny Holland? >> I mean, a lot. He's in there all the time, too. So he's a great coach, too. Just to hear from him, I mean, he's been around this game so long, coached a lot of great linebackers. So just uh just to hear from him, from both coaches, I mean, it's been great just to learn and pick their brains. Is there any player past or present that you try to like model your game a little bit after or like learn from a little bit? Uh Fred, especially now, like watching Fred and Jerry, just like how they play the game, like just like their approach to the game. So relentless for sure. And then like when growing up a lot, Luke Keequley was a great one. Just not a linebacker, but I like Jaylen Ramsey, how he approached the game, how he's so physical. So those are like players I like to watch. Did KJ tell you that he was trying to draft himself when when they draft? Like your I think your physical measurables are similar. Um did you guys have a conversation about that or? >> Um he he told me about that when I first got here. That's what the coaches said. But actually I didn't even know like how big he was until I got here. I thought he was like 510. I didn't know he was that big. When I seen him for the first time, I was like, "Damn, you're bigger than I thought." So it was cool to see that. But I mean, yeah. So, he talked about it before, but I think it's just a little joke going on. But you actually said he didn't know I got drafted until he seen it on the TV. So, I'm not sure >> because it is unusual to see a linebacker of your height playing the way you do. >> Yeah, it is. But, I mean, I feel like it has it advantages as well, too. So, >> what's the most important thing you've learned from Fred and Dre so far? >> Uh, really the approach to the game. That's what's the most important. Like being relentless, running to the ball all the time. I mean, if you watch film, you going to see them guys running to the ball all the time. That's like the 49er way. I mean, you you're taught that in college, but like they don't harp on it as much. But like now when you come here, like that's what that's the standard in practice. Even if you're 40 yards away, you go chase the ball. So just watching those guys and watching the team in general, just the culture around here just that that's what it taught me. >> A lot of guys that come up and notice that. I mean, Kyle Shanahan starting to do the team meetings a little bit more. The way he explains plays, does it change the way you see the game? >> Oh, yeah, for sure. I mean, it can get it get very complicated when he start breaking it down from offensive point of view. But yeah, I mean, him getting up there and just hearing it from offensive point of view and seeing how they want to block things, how they what they're thinking, when they're in motion and just stuff like that, it's good to hear just so you can know like what not to do when they're doing certain things. So, for sure. What was that day of practice with when you're working with the defensive line uh or the edge uh like for you and and working with Caceric and and seeing just seeing that side of things? Um I think it was just the one day but >> it was good. Uh I mean I did it a little bit in college for a year and then sometimes like I go down the line of scrimmage now you probably see. So, I mean it's good like just cross trainining myself just to have those tools and sharpen them because you never know what like well I do it sometimes too on the line of scrimmage. So, yeah. >> Thanks. >> Thanks. No problem. Thank you.

title: Why the 49ers are Fortunate to Still Have Mac Jones
text: All right. How good would you guys say M. Jones is? I thought it was a pleasure to watch him play. Like he was actually healthy. He was never really healthy last year. He had that PCL injury. He was kind of limping around. Uh he hadn't had a much of a training camp to write about, but like who are his receivers? He comes out in this game. It's his first live action since he posted a 115 quarterback rating against the Rams. and then got benched. And he looked really good. I mean, he wasn't just throwing to Dejon Stribbling the way Curtis Ror was. He was throwing to Braden Willis and all kind of people. Cadel Hajj and Jordan Watkins. He throw He's so different than Brock Perie. Brock Purie kind of toys with you. He holds the ball. He moves around. And when he does that, he, you know, but holes get tight. Brock Perie doesn't play like that. I mean, M. Jones doesn't play like that. Uh, the longer he holds the ball, the worse things get. But for a guy who can see it, make the decision, and rip it, he's really good at that. And I'm looking at him last night thinking, man, I think he would make a lot of teams better. I think I said this earlier, but isn't he better than Daniel Jones? I mean, of all the Joneses that are quarterbacks in the league, isn't he the best? Which Jones is better than M. Jones? title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 16 of 49ers Camp: Evans Leaves Early Again
text: The 49ers just finished day 16 of training camp. Here's who stood out. The good, tight end George Kittle. He practiced for the first time since he tore his Achilles in January. He participated in individual drills with the other tight ends but did not participate in one-on-one or 11-on-11 team drills, which are dangerous. The Niners are smart to go slow with Kittle considering he's way ahead of schedule. I expect he will fly to Australia and play against the Rams in week one. I don't think he'll dominate as he has in the past, but I think he'll help and I think the Niners will win. Call me a homer. Tight end Jake Tanjis. He must be worried about Kittle taking all of his playing time because in the past two practices, Tanjis has gone absolutely crazy. Today he caught a team high six passes. He was Brock Purdy's go-to guy, particularly after Mike Evans went down for the third time in camp. More on him in a minute. After Evans left the field, the Niners started using 13 personnel, which is one wide receiver, one running back, and three tight ends. I've never seen them do this before. Hopefully they'll do it during the season with Kittle, Tanjis, and Luke Farrell. Running back Christian McCaffrey. He practiced for the first time in two weeks and looked fresh and ready for week one. Unlike Kittle, McCaffrey participated in team drills with no restrictions. He seems poised to have a good year, particularly because the Niners seem intent on resting him at times. They really like Kaylin Black. Running back Kaylin Black. He caught two passes from Purdy in the first three plays of 11-on-11s. Black isn't a hybrid slot receiver like McCaffrey, but he can catch passes and the Niners will throw to him. He's a three-down player, but the best thing he does is run the ball, particularly between the tackles. He has the speed to get to the perimeter, but he wants to run downhill. He hits holes between the tackles with zero hesitation and can squirt through the tiniest of creases. In that sense, he reminds me of Frank Gore. At one point, he took a helmet-to-helmet hit from Fred Warner on a pass over the middle, stayed down for a second, shook his head, ran back to the huddle, lined up in the backfield, took the handoff, and exploded around the left side for a 20-yard gain. He's so tough. Wide receiver De'Jon Stripling. He returned to practice after missing yesterday with a shoulder injury. He wore a black non-contact jersey but still participated fully and even caught a 15-yard pass near the sideline from Purdy while being covered by Jack Jones. Cornerback Deommodore Lenoir, he also returned to practice after missing yesterday with a shoulder injury. At one point even lined up in the slot as a nickelback, something I haven't seen him do in 2 years. Wherever he lines up, Purdy usually stays away from him. Nickelback Utton Stout, he intercepted Purdy while covering Shribling in the slot. Shribling ran a dig route over the middle. Purdy released the pass before Shribling turned his head and Stout broke on the pass before Shribling knew it was coming his way. Stout and Lenoir are by far the best players in the Niner secondary. The rest of the starters are shaky. Safety Ashton Davis, he intercepted Mac Jones on a pass over the middle that was intended for Jacob Cowing. Davis is nearly 30 years old and he hasn't had much success playing safety in his career, but he just might be good enough to start for the 49ers considering their starting safety Marquis Seagull almost never makes plays on the ball. And today he blew his assignment in the middle of the field and gave up an uncontested 70-yard touchdown catch to Jordan Watkins. Give Davis a chance. Cornerback Ifeanyi Orizu Okeke, he broke up two passes. A deep one intended for Will Pauling and a short one intended for Malik Turner. It's just a matter of time before Price-Lock joins Lenoir and Stout as the starters in the secondary. He has incredible athletic gifts, he doesn't give up much separation, and he makes plays on the ball. What more could you want? Linebacker Dre Greenlaw, he broke up and nearly intercepted a pass from Purdy over the middle that was intended for Evans. Greenlaw hasn't made a ton of plays in camp and he frequently comes off the field in clear passing situations third down. But on this play he nearly made a one-handed pick. Still, I wonder about his ability to break down and change directions after tearing his Achilles. Don't expect him to be a full-time player this year. Defensive tackle James Thompson Jr., he's probably the second best defensive tackle on the team after Osa Odighizuwa. Thompson Jr. is a terrific run defender who actually can rush the passer, too. Today he lined up with the starters and beat Carver Willis to sack Purdy. Whoever scouted this guy deserves a promotion. The not-so-good. Wide receiver Mike Evans. He left practice early yet again. A few days ago he left the joint practice against the Chargers early due to a quad strain. This injury doesn't appear serious and yet Evans can't make it through consecutive practices without re-aggravating it. Today he ran a deep corner route which required him to sprint. He pulled up at the end of the play, took off his shoulder pads and watched the rest of practice from the sideline. He just doesn't seem like he's going to make it through the entire season. I wouldn't be surprised if he starts some games he doesn't finish. No wonder the Niners are breaking out their three tight end formations. Practically all of their wide receivers are banged up. Defensive end Nick Bosa. He hasn't practiced in more than three weeks. He didn't even show up to watch practice from the sideline. Either he's extremely unhappy with his contract and is holding in for an extension or his knee tendonitis is worse than the Niners have let on. If he plays week one, it's fair to wonder how effective he'll be. He probably won't be in football shape and new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris might not know how to use him. And without Bosa, the Niners defense is in serious trouble. I don't think Morris has the chops to build a viable defense without his only effective edge rusher. Defensive end Romeo Okwara. He missed practice with an undisclosed injury which means both of the Niners primary edge rushers are injured. Not to mention MyCole Pruitt, their first round pick from last year who seems months away from returning from a torn ACL. I don't see how the defense can be good without legitimate edge rushers. Linebacker Fred Warner. He nearly knocked out Kaylin Black with a vicious helmet-to-helmet hit. Remember, Warner knocked out Ronaldo Green from the joint practice against the Chargers a few days ago and knocked out Jordan James for three weeks after punching him when he wasn't wearing pads and breaking his ribs. Warner has been out of control all of camp. And he's been loud about it, too. You frequently can hear him taunting the offense. So today, Purdy completed a pass right over Warner's head, then immediately screamed an obscenity at Warner. I didn't know Purdy uses words like that. Afterward, Warner walked over to Purdy and they appeared to hash things out. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, he's trying to install so many new things and he doesn't currently have the personnel to pull off any of them. To be fair, his players do a good job aggressively breaking on intermediate passes over the middle, but they can't seem to stop anything else. Today, Morris kept using a defense with five defensive linemen, one linebacker, and five defensive backs, and it couldn't stop anything, not the run or the pass. On third down, he wants to be aggressive and blitz. This just leaves his sub-par safeties one-on-one against superior players. title: QB Jayden Daniels Speaks To The Media After The Game | Washington Commanders
text: Uh, honestly, it was just good to get back out there and play football again. It's been uh a little over eight months since I played live football, so it was good. It was good to go back out there. >> And as you were standing once you left the game and looked at the game the rest of the game, what did you see from the other quarterbacks? >> Uh, I mean, you know, they were doing what the coaches told them, flip-flopping series. Um, and they just stayed in it. You know, they kept battling. Uh, made some throws. Sam made some throws. Aan made some throws. So super proud of them and how they battled out um you know to try to make plays and give us a chance to win. >> Considering you guys you know the first didn't go according was there any thoughts you know possibly going back out did you have any say in that at all? >> I listen what coaches tell you. Um no I mean you know it's good to go out there and just operationally go out there and live bullets. I mean joint practice is great practice. Um you know it's a different type of urgency when you're going up against somebody else that is live. So, it was good to get back out there and like I said, play football once again. >> How tough is it for you as a competitor to like ramp up to game level and then have to ramp it down quickly? >> Uh, I mean, it's tough, but it's kind of it comes with the business now. Like, kind of understand I'm going to year three now, so understand you can't play all however many play 60 plus plays in the preseason game. Uh, the main goal is week one and then uh games after that. So, uh, you try to just build up, ramp up, and, you know, try to knock out the rust here and there. But, uh, from there, you kind of just go out there and trust your coach and trust everything they got to say. >> Jay, from your perspective, I know sometimes it's a conversation around the value of preseason, whether or not you should play in a preseason game or not. So, what is that value of just getting some live action even if it's just not a whole quarter? I mean, at the end of the day, we I get paid I get paid to play football. So, I'm a football player. Uh my job is to go out there and play football. So, if I'm asked to go play football, I'm gonna go out there and play football. So, uh I think you know it's it's valuable reps, you know, whether it's preeason practice, you're always just learning from uh each and everything. So, it's very valuable to me. >> And there's been a lot of movement on the line. How have you been able to just kind of gel with the offensive line? >> Yeah, I mean I think it's just it's still a work in progress and like I said, it's only preseason. We still got practices and everything and by the time we get to game one, you know, we'll have it set in stone. Um, but for me, it's really just trusting those guys up front. Uh, trusting the play calling, trusting my reads and everything, getting the ball out, uh, what I have to do and playing on time. >> J, I know you had an Instagram post last week, I think. How is everything going with kind of the fallout with LSU? Uh man, I mean, like you said, I posted that um you know, the statement is out, but for me now, it's really just focused on Commander football. Uh I said everything I had to say within the statement, and now it's really just getting ready for week one. >> And where do you think you guys are in the offense? Like learning everything, >> Uh I think we still there. I mean, it's you don't really game plan. Uh now, you still trying to work your fundamentals and everything, your your foundation. Um, but I think week by week, I mean, as you week one is getting closer and closer, you start to get into that game planning mode and everything. So, I think overall we have the foundation of our offense and now you just kind of put different wrinkles on stuff and things like that. >> Do you feel like there's value in the joint practice as far as maybe the competition value of it? >> I do. >> I do. I mean, you're going against somebody else other than um our for us our defense. So, uh, you're going against other people, you get to make other plays, uh, see different defenses, um, that you might not see in an actual preseason game. Um, and, you know, kind of just go out there and compete and you want to compete against other people other than yourselves. >> And J, you talked about time is ticking and everything. When you look at the YC overall, some of the younger guys like Bradley and some of those guys that out there making plays, what are you seeing from that group overall? And particularly some of the that you don't people don't talk about a lot. >> Yeah, I think um it starts from the top down. Um the vets that they have in that room uh with Terry, Steph, Van, uh Dei, those guys, Trey, uh guys that made plays and you know, they breathe life into the young guys in the room to go out there and make plays. Uh you know, when JB made that one-handed catch, we were all pumped up on the on the sideline. I think some of us made it onto the field, but uh you know, you just see people work so hard and uh to go out there and have those type of moments uh not only for theirel but their family. Uh they're living out dreams of, you know, playing the NFL, catching passes. Um to go out there and just having fun, that's what we kind of try to preach to them. >> What have you thought of in two games now? >> Uh kid, he's funny. He got a lot of personality. Uh you know, he's go out there and he make throws, man. And you know that throw to Nick Nash, the one to JB, uh he made plays. So, I'm super happy for him. >> Appreciate y'all. [laughter] 329. Yeah.
